elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt. Apply each supported command (START, STOP, WRITE with din=0, and READ) while providing released-high bus conditions and any required filtered SCL progression. Wait for each command's cmd_ack before applying the next command.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen exhibits the command-specific timed bit-level SCL pattern for every accepted command, including the required low and released-high phases for START, STOP, READ, and WRITE, and each sequence completes with one cmd_ack. This demonstrates bit-level controller behavior rather than an unrelated or byte-level operation.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model synchronized to posedge clk to predict clk_en, FSM phase progression, clock-stretch handling, and registered scl_oen latency. Compare the observed scl_oen waveform and cmd_ack pulse against the model for each command, checking phase ordering and completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset while idle and ena=1, apply NOP (0000) and each unsupported cmd encoding other than 0001, 0010, 0100, and 1000 for multiple enabled clock-divider ticks, while keeping SCL and SDA externally released high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: scl_oen does not produce any corresponding timed bit-level SCL pattern, remains in the idle released state, and no cmd_ack is generated. The observation is distinguishable from the required bit-level controller behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen and cmd_ack on every posedge clk and compare against an idle/no-op reference model. Assert that no command-phase low/high sequence occurs and that cmd_ack remains low throughout each unsupported-command interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=START (4'b0001), and keep scl_i and sda_i high so the bus is released and idle. Hold inputs until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the observed_via shows: from command acceptance through completion, sda_oen participates in the START-specific timed sequence by releasing SDA, then driving SDA low while SCL is high; scl_oen participates by releasing SCL and then driving SCL low. A one-clock cmd_ack pulse terminates the sequence.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_oen and sda_oen against a reference START-sequence model and confirm the ordered release/drive phases and exactly one cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=STOP (4'b0010), and keep scl_i and sda_i high except as driven by the DUT. Hold inputs until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the observed_via shows: scl_oen and sda_oen participate in the STOP-specific timed sequence by first driving SDA low, then releasing SCL high, and finally releasing SDA while SCL is high. A one-clock cmd_ack pulse terminates the sequence.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate STOP reference model to check the ordered scl_oen/sda_oen phases, requiring no phase transition before the modeled timing tick and exactly one completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=1, cmd=WRITE (4'b0100), and din=0. Keep scl_i high and externally release SDA. Hold inputs until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the observed_via shows: sda_oen drives SDA low for din=0, scl_oen releases SCL for the timed high phase, then drives SCL low; the command completes with one cmd_ack pulse. The output-enable changes occur only on the modeled enabled timing ticks.
elements.check_method: Compare sampled scl_oen and sda_oen on every settled posedge with a prescaler-aware WRITE reference model, checking phase order, clk_cnt timing, completion, and absence of arbitration loss.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=READ (4'b1000), keep scl_i high, and drive sda_i first low and then high in separate runs during the released SCL read window. Hold inputs until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the observed_via shows: sda_oen remains released so the external device can drive SDA; scl_oen releases SCL for the read window and then drives SCL low before completion. The sequence ends with one cmd_ack pulse, and the externally driven bit is captured in dout.
elements.check_method: Check the read protocol trace against a reference model: SDA remains released, SCL release precedes the filtered SCL rising-edge sample, SCL is subsequently driven low, dout matches each driven bit, and cmd_ack is one clock.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=NOP (4'b0000) while idle; repeat with unsupported cmd values 4'b0011, 4'b0101, and 4'b1111. Keep the bus released and wait at least the maximum expected command-acceptance interval for each value.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding contrast of the observed_via shows: because no supported bit command is accepted, scl_oen and sda_oen remain in the non-command idle/released state and do not exhibit a command-correlated timed sequence. No cmd_ack pulse occurs.
elements.check_method: Assert that the output-enable trace remains at the reset/idle released values for the entire observation window, with no command-sequence transition and no cmd_ack, using a negative reference model for NOP and unsupported commands.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1, drive cmd=0000 (NOP) and each unsupported cmd value from 4'b0011, 4'b0101, 4'b0110, 4'b0111, 4'b1001 through 4'b1111 while scl_i and sda_i remain high.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting otherwise case: cmd_ack remains low, busy and al remain unchanged, dout does not update, and scl_oen and sda_oen remain in the released idle state. No command-specific START, STOP, WRITE, or READ sequence occurs.
elements.check_method: Compare all output traces against an idle reference model on every posedge; assert no cmd_ack pulse and no command-phase output-enable transition for each unsupported encoding.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, clk_cnt=1, a released-high bus, and no arbitration or stretching, issue cmd=0001 (START) for command acceptance, then provide the normal filtered bus progression through the START sequence.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case for START support: sda_oen sequences from released to low while SCL is high, scl_oen then drives SCL low, and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock at completion. A filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high sets busy.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate command reference model and monitor scl_oen, sda_oen, cmd_ack, and busy after settled posedges; check phase ordering, one-cycle acknowledgment, and busy assertion at the filtered START event.

elements.stimulus: First establish busy with a filtered START, then with ena=1 and a released-high bus issue cmd=0010 (STOP), allowing each timed STOP phase to complete.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case for STOP support: sda_oen drives SDA low, scl_oen releases SCL, sda_oen releases SDA while filtered SCL is high, and cmd_ack pulses for exactly one clock. The filtered SDA low-to-high STOP transition clears busy.
elements.check_method: Score the output-enable sequence and command acknowledgment against a STOP reference model, and compare busy with the filtered STOP event rather than raw SDA transitions.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, clk_cnt=1, and a normal released-high bus, issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=0 and then repeat with din=1; externally allow SDA to match the driven or released value.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case for single-bit WRITE support: din=0 drives SDA low and din=1 releases SDA, scl_oen releases SCL for the high phase and then drives it low, sda_oen follows the data polarity, no false al asserts, and cmd_ack pulses exactly once after completion.
elements.check_method: Run both data values through a reference model and compare sda_oen polarity, scl_oen phase ordering, al, and one-cycle cmd_ack after each settled posedge.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=1, wait until SCL is released high for the WRITE arbitration phase, and externally hold SDA low; separately repeat with din=0 while SDA is held low.
elements.expected_response: For din=1 this is the contrasting arbitration-loss case: al asserts, the active command aborts, cmd_ack does not pulse, and both scl_oen and sda_oen release. For din=0, low SDA is expected and no arbitration loss occurs; the WRITE completes and cmd_ack pulses once.
elements.check_method: Detect the released-high WRITE window from the reference model, compare al and output enables immediately after the filtered SDA observation, and verify the mutually exclusive ack/no-ack outcomes for din=1 versus din=0.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a normal bus, issue cmd=1000 (READ); first drive a stable filtered SDA=0 during the released-SCL sample window, then repeat the complete READ with stable filtered SDA=1.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case for single-bit READ support: sda_oen remains released, scl_oen releases SCL for the sample window and then drives it low, dout captures 0 or 1 respectively on the filtered SCL rising edge, and cmd_ack pulses exactly once after the low phase.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered SCL rising edge as the sampling reference, compare dout with the filtered SDA value only within read_window, and verify output-enable sequencing and one-cycle cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Issue a supported START, WRITE, or READ with scl_i externally held low whenever the DUT releases SCL high; keep the line low for several enabled timing ticks, then release it high.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case for slave clock stretching: scl_oen remains released, the command phase and cmd_ack are delayed while filtered SCL remains low, no premature terminal phase occurs, and the command resumes and completes with one cmd_ack after filtered SCL becomes high.
elements.check_method: Compare the trace with a stretching-aware reference model; assert no FSM phase advance or ack during the low filtered-SCL interval and verify eventual phase ordering after release.

elements.stimulus: During a command phase in which the DUT has released SCL high, drive an external filtered SCL falling edge and hold the bus low for several timing intervals before allowing SCL high again.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case for multi-master clock synchronization: the controller recognizes the externally caused SCL fall, reloads timing, keeps SCL released while the other master holds it low, and does not advance the high-phase command sequence until filtered SCL returns high.
elements.check_method: Correlate the filtered SCL falling edge with the synchronized timing model and output-enable trace; check that the remaining command latency is extended and no premature cmd_ack is generated.

elements.stimulus: Start a WRITE or READ, then generate an unexpected stable filtered STOP before the active non-STOP command reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting aborted-command case: al asserts and remains asserted, the active command returns to idle, both scl_oen and sda_oen release, and cmd_ack does not pulse. No successful command completion is reported.
elements.check_method: Inject the STOP only after the reference model marks the FSM active, then compare al, output enables, FSM completion, and cmd_ack against the arbitration-abort model; verify al remains high until reset.

elements.stimulus: After reset, apply SDA and SCL raw pulses shorter than the configured filter sampling interval so that the three-sample majority never changes; then apply stable SDA high-to-low and low-to-high transitions while SCL is stably high.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting glitch-filtering case followed by the holding case: short glitches do not change busy, do not generate START or STOP processing, and do not assert al; stable filtered transitions generate START/STOP behavior, including busy set on START and clear on STOP.
elements.check_method: Model synchronizers, sampling intervals, three-sample majority, and filtered edge detection; assert no status or command-visible transition for glitch-only input and verify expected transitions for stable input.

elements.stimulus: Apply alternating and stable scl_i and sda_i values with clk_cnt equal to 0, 1, and a larger value while ena=1; issue a READ during stable bus conditions and observe synchronized and filtered behavior.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case for SDA/SCL input synchronization and glitch filtering: output decisions use synchronized, majority-filtered values rather than raw inputs; clk_cnt=0 still permits enabled progress and filtering, and READ dout updates only on a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.check_method: Compare raw-input, two-stage-synchronizer, filter-history, filtered-edge, and command-output traces against a parameterized reference model for all three clk_cnt values.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena=1 on a released-high bus, allow the START sequence to complete, then issue a STOP command and allow its sequence to complete. Observe scl_o, sda_o, scl_oen, and sda_oen after every settled posedge throughout idle, START, and STOP phases.
elements.expected_response: The holding case is satisfied: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0 at every observation. During phases that drive a line low, the corresponding enable is 0; during phases that release it, the corresponding enable is 1. Thus the external lines are controlled only through active-low enables, with no nonzero drive value on either data output.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-by-cycle scoreboard asserting scl_o==0 and sda_o==0, and map each START/STOP FSM phase to the expected scl_oen and sda_oen values. Independently model each external line as low when its enable is 0 and otherwise released to the pull-up, and compare the observed bus level.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a released-high bus, issue WRITE with din=0 and complete the bit cycle, then issue WRITE with din=1 and complete the bit cycle. During each WRITE, observe the SDA output and enable in the data phase and the SCL output and enable in low and released-high phases.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting drive/release case is satisfied: scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0. For din=0, sda_oen becomes 0 and the external SDA line is driven low; for din=1, sda_oen becomes 1 and SDA is released so an external pull-up can make it high. SCL similarly drives low with scl_oen=0 and releases with scl_oen=1. Any nonzero scl_o/sda_o or reversed enable polarity is a failure of the specified open-drain control.
elements.check_method: Compare registered outputs after each posedge against a reference phase model. Assert constant-low drive outputs, verify the din-dependent SDA enable polarity, verify SCL drive/release phases, and sample the externally modeled open-drain lines with pull-ups to distinguish driven-low from released-high behavior.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset, deassert it, leave the bus idle with ena high, and sample scl_o, sda_o, scl_oen, and sda_oen on every subsequent rising edge.
elements.expected_response: The constant-drive outputs scl_o and sda_o are 0 on every sample. Because both lines are released in the idle state, scl_oen and sda_oen are 1; this is the released side of the active-low polarity shown by the requirement.
elements.check_method: A scoreboard compares every sampled scl_o and sda_o value against 0 and compares both output enables against 1 during the idle/released phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command with ena high and a released-high bus, then observe the phase in which SDA is driven low while SCL remains released.
elements.expected_response: scl_o and sda_o remain constantly 0. During the START SDA-drive phase, sda_oen is 0, demonstrating the driven side of active-low SDA enable, while scl_oen is 1 because SCL is released.
elements.check_method: Use a phase-aware scoreboard keyed to the START command sequence; assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 every cycle, and check sda_oen==0 with scl_oen==1 in the SDA-drive/SCL-release phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a START command and allow it to reach the phase that pulls SCL low after SDA has been asserted low.
elements.expected_response: scl_o and sda_o remain 0. When SCL is driven low, scl_oen is 0, and SDA remains driven low with sda_oen equal to 0; this is the driven side of the active-low enable behavior.
elements.check_method: A reference phase model identifies the SCL-low phase and compares both constant outputs to 0 and both output enables to 0 for that phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, issue a STOP command and observe the phase after SCL is released and SDA is released while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: scl_o and sda_o remain constantly 0. In the final released-high phase, scl_oen and sda_oen are both 1, demonstrating that value 1 releases each open-drain line; the contrasting released side of the polarity is observed after the driven phase.
elements.check_method: A phase-aware scoreboard checks scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 throughout the STOP sequence, then checks scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==1 in the final released phase.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue a START command on a bus with no external device pulling SCL or SDA low. Observe the START sequence until the registered sda_oen becomes 0 while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: sda_oen=0 drives SDA low, so the resolved SDA bus line is low despite the external pull-up. scl_oen remains released as required for the START SDA-low phase.
elements.check_method: After each posedge update settles, sample sda_oen and the resolved SDA bus value from an open-drain bus model. Assert that whenever sda_oen=0 in this phase, resolved SDA=0; record coverage for the driven-low SDA case.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue a START command on a bus with no external device pulling SCL or SDA low. Continue the START sequence until the registered scl_oen becomes 0 after SDA has been pulled low.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: scl_oen=0 drives SCL low, so the resolved SCL bus line is low despite the external pull-up.
elements.check_method: After each posedge update settles, sample scl_oen and the resolved SCL bus value from an open-drain bus model. Assert that whenever scl_oen=0 in this phase, resolved SCL=0; record coverage for the driven-low SCL case.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it while no external device drives either bus line low. Before issuing any command, observe the registered reset output state with the external pull-ups enabled.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of shows: reset drives sda_oen=1, releasing SDA, so the external pull-up makes the resolved SDA line high.
elements.check_method: Sample sda_oen and resolved SDA after asynchronous reset initialization. Assert sda_oen=1 and resolved SDA=1 with no external low drive; record coverage for the released-high SDA case.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it while no external device drives either bus line low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue a START command and sample the initial START phase in which both lines are released.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of shows: scl_oen=1 releases SCL, so the external pull-up makes the resolved SCL line high.
elements.check_method: After each registered scl_oen update settles during reset and the initial START release phase, compare scl_oen with the resolved SCL bus value. Assert scl_oen=1 and resolved SCL=1 when externally undriven; record coverage for the released-high SCL case.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide clk_cnt=1 and a released-high bus, then issue a supported START command and keep the bus released so the command can complete.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0006: scl_oen follows the Bit Command Controller's command-specific START pattern, including release of SCL, the required low phase, return to the released state, and completion coincident with a one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Sample registered scl_oen and cmd_ack after each posedge, compare the observed sequence against a reference START-command model, and require exactly one completion pulse after the expected phases.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and repeatedly apply NOP=0000 and an unsupported cmd=0011 while keeping the bus released; do not issue a supported START, STOP, READ, or WRITE command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for REQ-0006: scl_oen remains in the idle released state and does not produce a command-specific Bit Command Controller SCL sequence or cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Sample scl_oen and cmd_ack after every posedge while each no-op command is applied; compare against the idle reference model and require no SCL enable transitions and no completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, release both external I2C lines high, and issue cmd=START for one enabled clock; keep inputs stable until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: during START execution, scl_oen remains released while the START precondition is established, sda_oen changes to low-driving while SCL is high, and then scl_oen changes to low-driving for the remainder of the bit operation; the sequence completes with a one-clock cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after NBA settling, compare scl_oen and sda_oen against a reference START phase model and verify the phase ordering and cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, establish a busy bus, and issue cmd=STOP for one enabled clock; keep the external bus released high until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting supported-operation case of shows: scl_oen releases SCL after the STOP sequence drives SDA low, and sda_oen subsequently releases SDA while SCL is high; the output-enable pattern differs from START and completes with a one-clock cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use a STOP reference model to compare the sampled scl_oen/sda_oen phase sequence, verify SDA-low precedes both releases, and verify cmd_ack occurs once.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue cmd=WRITE with din=0 on a released-high bus; allow the complete operation without stretching or arbitration interference.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: sda_oen drives SDA low for din=0, scl_oen releases SCL for the high phase, then drives SCL low again; the command returns to idle and generates exactly one cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Compare output-enable samples with the WRITE din=0 reference sequence and assert that SDA is driven low before and throughout the SCL high phase, followed by SCL low and cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue cmd=WRITE with din=1 on a released-high bus; allow the complete operation with external SDA remaining high during the released high phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting data-controlled case of shows: sda_oen releases SDA for din=1, scl_oen releases SCL during the high phase, and scl_oen then drives SCL low before completion; no arbitration loss occurs and one cmd_ack is generated.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_oen and sda_oen to the WRITE din=1 reference model and check that the output-enable pattern is distinct from din=0 while the command completes without al.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ, and have the external slave hold SDA high during the released SCL read window; allow the operation to complete.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: sda_oen remains released so the slave can control SDA, scl_oen releases SCL for the read window, then drives SCL low; the operation completes with dout=1 and one cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Compare output-enable traces with the READ reference sequence, verify SDA is never driven by the DUT during the read window, and check dout and cmd_ack at completion.

elements.stimulus: Start a WRITE with din=1, ena=1, and clk_cnt=0; during the released SCL high phase force the external SDA line low to cause arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting abort case of shows: on arbitration loss the command stops rather than continuing its commanded phase, cmd_ack is not asserted, al becomes sticky, and both scl_oen and sda_oen are released.
elements.check_method: Detect the arbitration-loss event and compare subsequent output enables and status against an abort reference model; assert no cmd_ack pulse after the abort and both enables equal released.

elements.stimulus: Begin a supported START command with ena=1, then assert nReset low asynchronously during an active line-control phase and hold it through a clock edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting reset case of shows: command-dependent line control is aborted; scl_oen and sda_oen asynchronously return to released values, cmd_ack, busy, and al clear, and no stale command phase resumes.
elements.check_method: Sample outputs immediately after nReset assertion and after the following posedge, comparing against reset values and checking that no completion pulse is produced.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1, cmd=0001 (START), and a released-high external bus; hold the command until cmd_ack is asserted.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0008: scl_oen and sda_oen generate the START bit-level pattern by releasing SCL and SDA, then driving SDA low while SCL is high, then driving SCL low, followed by a one-clock cmd_ack; both enables are released after completion.
elements.check_method: Compare sampled registered scl_oen and sda_oen phases and cmd_ack timing against a command-sequence reference model, checking phase ordering and completion.

elements.stimulus: Complete a START command to establish busy, then with ena=1 drive cmd=0010 (STOP) and hold the command until cmd_ack is asserted.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0008: scl_oen and sda_oen generate the STOP bit-level pattern by driving SDA low, releasing SCL for the high phase, then releasing SDA while SCL is high, followed by a one-clock cmd_ack; both enables are released after completion.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed enable waveforms, phase order, and cmd_ack pulse with the STOP reference-model trace, allowing timing variation from the divider and filtering.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1, cmd=1000 (READ), provide a stable external SDA value, and hold the command until cmd_ack is asserted.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0008: sda_oen remains released so the external device can drive SDA; scl_oen releases SCL for the read high/sample phase and then drives SCL low, followed by a one-clock cmd_ack and released idle outputs.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_oen and sda_oen against the READ reference-model phase sequence and verify that the command completes with exactly one cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1, din=0, cmd=0100 (WRITE), keep the external bus released/high, and hold the command until cmd_ack is asserted.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0008: sda_oen drives SDA low for din=0, scl_oen releases SCL for the write high phase and then drives SCL low, and the controller returns to released idle with one cmd_ack and no arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Compare the registered output-enable polarity and ordered WRITE phases against a reference model parameterized with din=0; check cmd_ack and al outputs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1, din=1, cmd=0100 (WRITE), keep the external SDA high so arbitration succeeds, and hold the command until cmd_ack is asserted.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0008: sda_oen releases SDA for din=1, scl_oen releases SCL for the write high phase and then drives SCL low, and the controller returns to released idle with one cmd_ack and no arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Compare the registered scl_oen and sda_oen phases against a reference model parameterized with din=1, and verify completion without al.

elements.stimulus: After reset while idle, drive ena=1 and cmd=0011, an unsupported command encoding, for multiple enabled clock and divider ticks; then return cmd to NOP=0000.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case of REQ-0008: scl_oen and sda_oen do not show any START, STOP, READ, or WRITE phase-specific pattern; they remain or return at released idle values, and cmd_ack remains low.
elements.check_method: Use an assertion that no command-phase enable transition occurs during the unsupported-command interval and that cmd_ack stays low; compare idle outputs with the reference model.

elements.stimulus: Instantiate i2c_master_bit_ctrl from the DUT source through an interface-checking wrapper. Connect one-bit signals to clk, rst, nReset, and ena, and a 16-bit signal to clk_cnt. Drive clk, rst, nReset, and ena with both 0 and 1 values, and drive clk_cnt with 16'h0000 and 16'hFFFF while compiling and elaborating the design.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: elaboration succeeds, clk, rst, nReset, and ena are single-bit input ports, and clk_cnt is a 16-bit input port. The wrapper can drive every connected input, including both clk_cnt boundary values, without width or direction diagnostics.
elements.check_method: Use compile-time interface reflection or the simulator's elaborated port table to compare each port's direction and width against the required signature; require zero connection-width and illegal-driver diagnostics.

elements.stimulus: Run the same interface-checking wrapper against deliberately nonconforming DUT variants: change one of clk, rst, nReset, or ena to a multi-bit or output port, and separately change clk_cnt to a width other than 16 bits. Attempt the same input connections and boundary-value drives.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the declaration does not hold, so the interface checker or elaboration must reject each mutated variant with a diagnostic identifying the incorrect port direction or width; no mutated variant may be accepted as the required interface.
elements.check_method: Use negative compilation/elaboration tests and assert that each mutation produces the expected port mismatch or illegal-driver error, while the conforming signature remains the only accepted interface.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate the DUT against a wrapper that connects cmd as a 4-bit input and connects cmd_ack, busy, and al as single-bit output signals; do not drive any runtime transaction.
elements.expected_response: The interface declaration succeeds and exposes cmd[3:0] as the command input, with cmd_ack declared as the command-complete acknowledge output, busy as the I2C bus-busy status output, and al as the I2C bus-arbitration-lost status output. This is the 'shows' side of each observed port.
elements.check_method: Use compilation/elaboration and interface reflection or a bound wrapper to verify port names, directions, and widths exactly: cmd input width 4 and cmd_ack, busy, al output width 1.

elements.stimulus: Compile and elaborate a negative DUT variant in which one required status port is omitted or is declared with the wrong direction; attempt to connect the wrapper's corresponding cmd_ack, busy, or al signal as specified.
elements.expected_response: Compilation or elaboration fails with a missing-port, direction, or connection-mismatch diagnostic, so the DUT does not provide cmd_ack as the command-complete acknowledge output, busy as the bus-busy status output, or al as the arbitration-lost status output. This is the 'otherwise' side of the observed-port shows clauses.
elements.check_method: Run the HDL compiler/elaborator and require a deterministic interface mismatch diagnostic; additionally inspect the elaborated port list to confirm the invalid variant cannot satisfy the required output declarations.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate and compile the DUT against an interface checker that connects din as a 1-bit input and dout as a 1-bit output; use reflection or compile-time port metadata to inspect both declarations.
elements.expected_response: HOLDING CASE: interface elaboration succeeds, din is present with input direction and width 1, and dout is present with output direction and width 1. This is the required side of the observed dout behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the simulator/compiler elaboration result and port metadata API, or a static interface assertion, to compare each port's name, direction, and width against the required declaration.

elements.stimulus: Run interface elaboration separately with mutated DUT declarations in which dout is absent, declared as an input, or declared with a width other than 1; also apply the analogous invalid mutation to din where applicable.
elements.expected_response: CONTRASTING CASE: elaboration or interface checking fails for every invalid variant; a design with dout absent, non-output, or not 1 bit wide is not accepted as satisfying the interface requirement.
elements.check_method: Expect a compile-time or elaboration-time error from the interface checker and verify that the diagnostic identifies the missing or mismatched dout declaration, including direction or width mismatch.

elements.stimulus: Elaborate the DUT through a typed I2C wrapper that declares scl_i and sda_i as inputs, scl_o and sda_o as outputs, and scl_oen and sda_oen as active-low output-enable controls; connect all six ports by name and run interface/port-direction inspection.
elements.expected_response: The holding case of REQ-0012 is observed: elaboration succeeds and inspection reports scl_i and sda_i as line inputs, scl_o and sda_o as line outputs, and scl_oen and sda_oen as active-low output-enable controls.
elements.check_method: Use compile/elaboration success plus an AST or simulator-introspection check of every named port's existence, direction, and documented role; require exact width 1 and exact port names.

elements.stimulus: Run the same interface checker against negative interface variants, each with one of scl_o, scl_oen, sda_o, or sda_oen removed, reversed in direction, or assigned the wrong role; also test variants that reverse scl_i or sda_i to outputs.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting non-holding case is detected: the interface check fails and identifies the absent, wrongly directed, or wrongly typed/role-assigned port rather than accepting the variant as a conforming I2C interface.
elements.check_method: Use compile-time interface-contract assertions or AST lint results and compare diagnostics against the expected port name, direction, and role mismatch; pass only when every injected defect is rejected.

elements.stimulus: Set nReset=1, apply rst=1 for one rising edge and then deassert rst. Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. With scl_i and sda_i released high, issue START; after its cmd_ack, issue WRITE with din=1, then READ while driving a stable filtered SDA value, and finally STOP. Change cmd, din, ena, scl_i, and sda_i only between rising edges while recording cmd_ack, busy, al, dout, scl_oen, and sda_oen continuously.
elements.expected_response: The synchronous-update side of REQ-0013 is observed: each of cmd_ack, busy, al, dout, scl_oen, and sda_oen changes only on a rising edge of clk corresponding to a synchronous state update, and each remains unchanged throughout the interval between rising edges. Command phases and status changes may occur on different rising edges because of filtering and FSM timing, but no listed output changes asynchronously during normal operation.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model sampled after nonblocking assignments on every posedge clk. Assert that any change in each listed output has a timestamp equal to a posedge clk, and use an asynchronous monitor between posedges to assert that all six outputs remain stable; correlate each edge change with the model's expected synchronous update.

elements.stimulus: Start a timed command sequence with nReset=1, rst=0, ena=1, and clk_cnt=1. After the FSM is active and at least one registered output is non-default, assert nReset=0 midway between two rising edges, hold it low across the next edge, then release it high between clock edges.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting, non-synchronous-reset side of REQ-0013 is observed: asserting the separately specified active-low asynchronous reset may change cmd_ack, busy, al, dout, scl_oen, and/or sda_oen between rising edges as they are immediately initialized. After reset is released, subsequent state and output changes again occur only on rising edges; any non-edge change must be attributable to the asynchronous reset assertion rather than ordinary synchronous operation.
elements.check_method: Timestamp every change on the six observable outputs and classify it against nReset transitions and clk posedges. Require reset-induced initialization changes to occur without waiting for a posedge, verify reset values, and then assert no output changes between posedges once nReset is high.

elements.stimulus: Release nReset, keep rst low, set ena high and clk_cnt to 0, leave cmd_ack-producing commands inactive, and run clk for multiple cycles while sampling cmd_ack continuously between successive rising edges.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: cmd_ack remains stable throughout every interval between rising edges of clk; no cmd_ack transition occurs between edges.
elements.check_method: Use a waveform assertion sampled continuously or at a resolution finer than one clk period: any cmd_ack value change must be associated with a recorded posedge clk; specifically verify no transition in each inter-edge interval.

elements.stimulus: Release nReset, keep rst low, set ena high and clk_cnt to 0, hold scl_i and sda_i high, issue a START command on a rising edge, and continuously monitor cmd_ack through command completion and the following cycle.
elements.expected_response: Changing side of shows: when cmd_ack changes value, each assertion or deassertion occurs only after a rising edge of clk; cmd_ack does not change during any interval between rising edges.
elements.check_method: Correlate every observed cmd_ack transition timestamp with the clk waveform using a temporal assertion such as $changed(cmd_ack) |-> $rose(clk), while also checking that cmd_ack is stable between consecutive clk rising edges.

elements.stimulus: After asynchronous reset release, set rst=0 and ena=1, issue a WRITE command with din=1 and clk_cnt=0, wait until the WRITE FSM is active, then set rst=1 and hold it through a rising edge of clk.
elements.expected_response: At the rising edge while rst is high, the synchronous reset side of the observation applies: cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, dout=0, scl_oen=1 releasing SCL, and sda_oen=1 releasing SDA. The command FSM, divider counters, and filtered-input state return to their reset initialization.
elements.check_method: Sample registered outputs immediately after the reset posedge and compare against reset-value assertions; use the reference model and licensed internal probes to confirm the FSM, counters, and filter state reset on that edge rather than before it.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset deasserted, rst=0, and ena=1; issue a WRITE command with din=1 and clk_cnt=0 while providing a released-high SCL and SDA bus, and allow the command to reach its terminal phase without asserting rst.
elements.expected_response: The non-reset side of the observation applies: the command FSM continues normal WRITE behavior instead of resetting, including the released-SCL high phase and subsequent completion with a one-clock cmd_ack pulse. cmd_ack is therefore allowed to be high at completion rather than being forced low by reset; scl_oen, sda_oen, busy, al, and dout retain their ordinary command-dependent behavior rather than reset values.
elements.check_method: Compare the post-posedge waveform with a non-reset reference model, checking that WRITE phases advance and cmd_ack pulses once at completion; assert that no reset-value transition is attributed to rst while rst remains low.

elements.stimulus: With nReset initially high, ena high, and clk_cnt=0, issue a START command and wait for a clocked active phase in which scl_oen=0. Then drive nReset low between two rising edges of clk, without applying another clock edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding-case is not applicable; this is the asserted-reset side of the requirement. scl_oen changes asynchronously from 0 to 1, the reset-state released value, before the next rising edge of clk.
elements.check_method: Timestamp the falling edge of nReset and sample scl_oen continuously or with an event-based assertion until the next clk rising edge; require scl_oen==1 before that edge and require no wait for a posedge.

elements.stimulus: With nReset high, ena high, and clk_cnt=0, issue a START command and wait for a clocked active phase in which scl_oen=0. Keep nReset high and hold all other inputs constant while allowing multiple clk periods to elapse between rising edges or while observing the interval immediately after a rising edge before the next one.
elements.expected_response: This is the deasserted-reset contrast. scl_oen remains 0 throughout the inter-edge interval; it does not change asynchronously to the reset value 1 merely because time passes. Any change must occur only on a rising edge of clk or another specified synchronous control event.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen and clk; assert that scl_oen has no transition to 1 between consecutive clk rising edges while nReset remains high and no other control event occurs, and compare transitions only at posedge clk.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, configure clk_cnt=1, present a supported START command while the filtered bus is released high, and maintain ena high until the command reaches its terminal completion phase.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-high side of the observed behavior: cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock cycle after the START sequence completes.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked assertion/reference model to identify START terminal completion and compare the registered cmd_ack waveform, requiring one and only one high cycle with no additional pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=0, present and hold a supported START command while maintaining a released-high filtered bus; keep ena low for multiple enabled-clock intervals and through the time the command would normally progress, then withdraw the command before re-enabling ena.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-low side of the observed behavior: command acceptance and timing progression are disabled, so cmd_ack does not pulse for the presented START command.
elements.check_method: Monitor cmd_ack on every settled posedge while ena is low and for the withdrawn command, and compare against a reference model with divider, filter, and FSM advancement disabled; require cmd_ack to remain low throughout.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set clk_cnt=0, keep the bus released and free of stretching or arbitration loss, assert ena=1, issue a supported WRITE command, and after the command is accepted but before its terminal phase set ena=0 and hold it low for several clocks.
elements.expected_response: Holding-case of shows for cmd_ack: while ena is low, normal timing and FSM progression stop, cmd_ack does not pulse, and the command remains incomplete. When ena returns high, the command resumes and eventually produces exactly one cmd_ack pulse; no extra pulse is generated.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model and scoreboard to compare command-phase progress and cmd_ack. Assert no cmd_ack and no phase advancement on every clock with ena=0, then require one completed-command pulse after re-enabling.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset, clk_cnt=0, free-bus WRITE command sequence, but keep ena=1 continuously from command acceptance through completion.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise-case of shows for cmd_ack: with ena high throughout, the active command progresses normally to completion and cmd_ack pulses for exactly one clock without an enable-induced postponement.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed FSM phase timing and cmd_ack pulse against the reference model for continuously enabled operation, and verify completion occurs without the pause seen in TP-0000.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT with the bus idle, establish filtered SCL high and filtered SDA high, set clk_cnt=0, drive SDA low while keeping SCL high to form a START-shaped transition, and hold ena=0 throughout the transition and for multiple filter sampling intervals.
elements.expected_response: Holding-case of shows for busy: filter timing and input-filter progression are gated by ena, the START is not processed, and busy remains at its pre-transition value of 0 while ena is low.
elements.check_method: Monitor filter sample/update activity and busy on each clock; require no filter progression or filtered START detection during ena=0 and require busy to remain 0.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset and idle-bus setup with filtered SCL high and filtered SDA high, drive and hold SDA low while SCL remains high, but keep ena=1 long enough for synchronization and filtering to process the transition.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise-case of shows for busy: with ena high, the stable START-shaped transition advances through the input filter, is detected as a filtered START, and busy becomes 1 after that detection.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to predict the filtered transition and compare the cycle of START detection and registered busy assertion; require busy to change from 0 to 1 only after the filtered START.

elements.stimulus: With nReset inactive, clk_cnt set to a nonzero value, a released non-stretching bus, and ena high, issue and accept a WRITE command. After acceptance but before completion, drive ena low and hold it low for multiple clk cycles, with no reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: This is the ena-low side of the observed difference: the clock divider is reloaded and the input filter counter is reset, timing progression is prevented, the active WRITE command does not advance to its completion phase, and cmd_ack does not pulse while ena remains low.
elements.check_method: At every posedge while ena is low, compare cmd_ack against 0 and verify no WRITE phase transition or completion occurs; observe cnt_zero/filter_cnt_expired and filter counter behavior with the licensed probes, and check that resuming ena does not produce an acknowledgment until the command subsequently completes.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same accepted WRITE setup, clk_cnt, bus conditions, and command data as TP-0000, but keep ena high throughout the command and do not apply reset, arbitration loss, or SCL stretching.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting ena-high side of the observed difference: the WRITE advances through its timed phases and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock at command completion.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the divider and WRITE timing, then compare the observed registered cmd_ack pulse and write phase progression; require exactly one completion pulse and no missing or premature acknowledgment.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, keep rst=0 and ena=1, hold clk_cnt=1, keep scl_i and sda_i released high with no stretching or external SCL synchronization, then issue a supported WRITE command with din=0 and hold cmd stable until acceptance.
elements.expected_response: The WRITE phases advance only at clk_en ticks paced by the loaded clk_cnt value, and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock after the terminal phase. This is the holding side of the requirement: cmd_ack pulses after clk_cnt-dependent phase timing rather than immediately or at an unpaced fixed latency.
elements.check_method: Use a divider/FSM reference model to predict each enabled tick and terminal phase, measure command-acceptance-to-cmd_ack latency in clk cycles, require agreement with the model, and assert that cmd_ack is high for one cycle only.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the identical reset, bus, ena, cmd, and din sequence as TP-0000, but hold clk_cnt=8 instead of 1; do not introduce stretching, external SCL synchronization, or reset during the command.
elements.expected_response: The terminal cmd_ack pulse occurs later than in TP-0000 by the additional divider-paced phase time and remains exactly one clock wide. This is the contrasting observation at cmd_ack: if clk_cnt were not loaded or did not generate clk_en pacing, the pulse would occur at the same latency as TP-0000 or without the expected paced progression; either result is a failure.
elements.check_method: Compare measured acceptance-to-cmd_ack latency against the reference model for clk_cnt=8 and against TP-0000, requiring the larger prescale to produce the corresponding larger modeled latency; check one-cycle pulse width and absence of premature ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16. Hold scl_i and sda_i stable at 1 and run enabled clk cycles while observing filter_cnt, filter_cnt_expired, and filter_sample_update.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the SDA/SCL filter sampling interval is derived from clk_cnt through filter_cnt; the effective filter interval is four enabled clocks (floor(16/4)), with filter_cnt reloading and expiring at that interval before synchronized samples are shifted into the filter histories.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed filter_cnt reload/decrement/expiry sequence and filter_sample_update events against a reference model implementing effective_interval=max(1,floor(clk_cnt/4)); require four enabled clocks between successive sample updates.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Hold scl_i and sda_i stable at 1 and run consecutive enabled clk cycles while observing filter_cnt, filter_cnt_expired, and filter_sample_update.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting boundary case: with clk_cnt=0, the derived filter interval must not become stuck or exceed the enabled-clock cadence; the zero interval is treated as sampling on every enabled clock, so filter_cnt expires and the filter sampling update occurs once per enabled clock.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed filter_cnt and filter_sample_update sequence against a reference model using effective_interval=max(1,floor(0/4))=1; require no multi-cycle stall and one sample update per enabled clock after reset initialization.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. While the FSM is idle, drive cmd=4'b0001 (I2C_CMD_START) and hold it through the enabled clock that accepts the command.
elements.expected_response: Positive side of the observed behavior: the idle FSM decodes cmd=I2C_CMD_START, enters the START sequence, and sda_oen transitions from 1 to 0 during the SDA assertion phase while scl_oen remains released high.
elements.check_method: At each posedge clk after registered outputs settle, compare sda_oen and scl_oen against a reference FSM model; require acceptance only while idle and ena=1, followed by sda_oen=0 with scl_oen=1 in the START SDA assertion phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, drive ena=1, clk_cnt=16'h0000, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. While the FSM is idle, drive cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) for multiple enabled clocks and do not issue a START command.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of the observed behavior: for cmd=NOP, sda_oen remains high during the idle command-decode window; no START sequence is entered and SDA is not asserted low by the controller.
elements.check_method: Sample sda_oen and scl_oen after each posedge clk and compare with the idle reference model; require sda_oen=1 throughout the NOP interval and no transition into a START-phase output pattern.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT to idle, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt, keep the released bus high, then drive cmd=4'b0010 (I2C_CMD_STOP) through an enabled clk_en acceptance tick. Continue clocks until command completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after STOP command acceptance, sda_oen is driven low first, then scl_oen is released high, and sda_oen rises to 1 while SCL is high before the STOP command completes with a one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Trace sda_oen, scl_oen, and cmd_ack on settled posedge samples; assert the ordered pattern sda_oen=0 followed by scl_oen=1 and then sda_oen=1 before cmd_ack, with no missing or reordered STOP phases.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT to idle, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt, keep the released bus high, then drive cmd=4'b1000 (I2C_CMD_READ) through an enabled clk_en acceptance tick. Continue clocks through the read bit cycle and completion.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: for this different supported command, sda_oen must not exhibit the STOP-specific low-then-release sequence before command completion; it remains released for the READ data window, while the READ operation completes with its own cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Trace sda_oen from READ acceptance through cmd_ack and compare against the STOP signature; fail if sda_oen transitions low and later rises to 1 in the STOP-specific ordering during this window, while confirming the READ operation reaches completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, drive din=0, and present cmd=0100 (I2C_CMD_WRITE) until it is accepted on an enabled clock tick. Continue supplying the high bus response through the WRITE high phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: after WRITE acceptance, the data phase drives SDA low with sda_oen=0, then releases SCL for the WRITE high phase; the WRITE sequence completes without arbitration loss and produces cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge, compare the observed sda_oen waveform against a transaction reference model; require sda_oen=0 during the din=0 data phase, the expected subsequent SCL phases, no al assertion, and exactly one cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, drive din=1, and present cmd=0100 (I2C_CMD_WRITE) until it is accepted on an enabled clock tick. Keep external SDA high during the released WRITE high phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: after WRITE acceptance, the data phase releases SDA with sda_oen=1 for din=1, then performs the released-SCL high phase and completes with cmd_ack without asserting al.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge, compare sda_oen and the phase progression with a reference model; require sda_oen=1 during the din=1 data phase, no arbitration loss while external SDA is high, and exactly one completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, drive cmd=0000 (NOP), and run once with din=0 and once with din=1 during the same enabled idle observation window.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of shows: NOP does not enter a WRITE data phase, sda_oen does not exhibit din-dependent WRITE behavior, the FSM remains idle, and cmd_ack remains low for both din values.
elements.check_method: Compare the sda_oen traces from the din=0 and din=1 runs cycle by cycle and check that no WRITE-phase transition or cmd_ack occurs; require identical idle output behavior independent of din.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the bus released, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, drive cmd=4'b1000 (I2C_CMD_READ) through an enabled command-decode event, then continue clocking.
elements.expected_response: The idle command FSM enters the READ sequence; fsm_active becomes high and read_sequence is asserted. This is the READ/requirement-holds side of the decode distinction.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after the command-decode event, compare fsm_active and read_sequence against a command-decode reference model and require both to assert during READ execution.

elements.stimulus: For independent trials from reset-idle, keep ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, and at an enabled command-decode event drive cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) and each unsupported encoding in {4'b0011,4'b0101,4'b0110,4'b0111,4'b1001,4'b1010,4'b1011,4'b1100,4'b1101,4'b1110,4'b1111}; continue clocking without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: For every NOP or unsupported command, the FSM remains idle: fsm_active and read_sequence stay low and no READ sequence is entered. This is the idle/unsupported-command, requirement-does-not-hold side of the decode distinction.
elements.check_method: For each command trial, compare fsm_active and read_sequence on every subsequent posedge with a reference model that decodes only I2C_CMD_READ as a transition to active READ execution; require no active assertion for NOP or unsupported encodings.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=WRITE (0100), clk_cnt=0, and din=0; issue the command on a rising edge and keep din=0 through command completion while the external SCL and SDA lines remain released high.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data phase after write_sequence begins and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 0, meaning the DUT drives SDA low. This is the din=0 side of the specified behavior: sda_oen is 0 when din is 0.
elements.check_method: Use the write_sequence probe to delimit the WRITE operation, identify the data phase before cmd_ack, and compare the registered sda_oen value against din=0 on every applicable clock.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=WRITE (0100), clk_cnt=0, and din=1; issue the command on a rising edge and keep din=1 through command completion while the external SCL and SDA lines remain released high.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data phase after write_sequence begins and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 1, meaning the DUT releases SDA. This is the din=1 side of the specified behavior: sda_oen is 1 when din is 1.
elements.check_method: Use the write_sequence probe to delimit the WRITE operation, identify the data phase before cmd_ack, and compare the registered sda_oen value against din=1 on every applicable clock.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=WRITE (0100), and din=0. Keep the external SCL and SDA lines released high so the WRITE proceeds without arbitration loss. Clock until write_sequence is active and continue through the active WRITE data-bit phase before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: during the active WRITE data-bit phase, sda_oen is 0, driving SDA low for din=0. The write may then complete with cmd_ack=1.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge while write_sequence is active and before cmd_ack or abort, compare sampled sda_oen against 0; record a pass only if it remains 0 throughout the data-bit drive phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=WRITE (0100), and din=1. Keep the external SCL and SDA lines released high so the released SDA does not cause arbitration loss. Clock until write_sequence and its active WRITE data-bit phase are reached, before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case of shows: during the active WRITE data-bit phase, sda_oen is 1, releasing SDA high for din=1. The write may then complete with cmd_ack=1.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge while write_sequence is active and before cmd_ack or abort, compare sampled sda_oen against 1; record a pass only if it remains 1 throughout the data-bit release phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, enable the controller, issue a READ command, and keep the external scl_i line stably low after the controller releases SCL for the READ sample window; provide a valid stable sda_i value.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in shows: while the externally supplied scl_i remains low during the READ sample window, scl_oen remains 1, so the controller continues releasing SCL and does not complete the high phase or pull SCL low.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge after READ enters its sample window, compare scl_oen against a reference model of the open-drain bus and verify scl_oen stays 1 for the entire interval that filtered scl_i remains low; verify no transition to the post-window low phase occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, enable the controller, issue a READ command, and hold the external scl_i line stably high after the controller releases SCL for the READ sample window; provide a valid stable sda_i value.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting case in shows: with scl_i high, the READ window completes and scl_oen becomes 0 to pull SCL low again.
elements.check_method: At settled posedges, compare scl_oen and the filtered SCL phase with the READ reference model: verify scl_oen is 1 during release, then transitions to 0 after the high sample window completes while scl_i is high, followed by normal READ completion.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, issue a READ command with ena high, release SCL, then externally hold scl_i low long enough for the synchronized and filtered SCL to remain low during the read window. Subsequently release scl_i high and allow the filtered SCL to become high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen remains 1 while the filtered SCL is low due to clock stretching, and transitions to 0 only after filtered SCL is high and the normal read high-phase timing completes.
elements.check_method: Use the divider/filter reference model and sample scl_oen after each posedge; assert that no read-window completion occurs while filtered SCL is low and that the low-drive transition occurs only after filtered SCL becomes high and the required timed phase expires.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, issue a READ command with ena high and a normally released-high SCL. Inject a raw scl_i low glitch shorter than the synchronizer/filter acceptance interval while scl_oen is released during the read window, then keep scl_i high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the rejected raw SCL glitch does not make the controller treat SCL as stretched; scl_oen follows the normal timed read-window completion and transitions to 0 without the glitch causing an additional postponement.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed scl_oen timeline with a no-glitch reference run and verify that the filtered SCL history never reaches the low majority value and that read-phase timing is unchanged.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, issue a WRITE command with din=1 and ena high, wait until the WRITE stable-high phase with scl_oen=1, then externally force scl_i low long enough to create a synchronized and filtered SCL falling edge before releasing it.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the external filtered SCL fall causes clock synchronization; the WRITE high phase and subsequent scl_oen low transition are postponed or retimed, and the controller does not complete the high phase using the original unretimed schedule.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen and, where available, scl_sync, fscl, and the divider reference model; verify that the filtered falling edge is recognized while SCL is released and that the phase timing is reloaded or extended accordingly.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, issue a WRITE command with din=1, wait until the stable-high phase with scl_oen=1, inject a raw scl_i falling pulse shorter than the synchronization/filter acceptance interval, then keep scl_i high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the unfiltered raw fall does not assert clock synchronization or retime the WRITE phase; scl_oen follows the normal timed high-phase release and subsequent low transition.
elements.check_method: Compare scl_oen timing against a no-glitch WRITE reference and verify through the filter model that no filtered SCL falling edge is generated from the injected pulse.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, establish filtered SCL high, drive filtered SDA high-to-low while filtered SCL is high to create a valid START, then drive filtered SDA low-to-high while filtered SCL remains high to create a valid STOP.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: busy rises after the synchronized and filtered START condition and falls after the synchronized and filtered STOP condition.
elements.check_method: Use the synchronizer, three-sample majority filter, and delayed-value reference model to identify sta_condition and sto_condition, then compare busy transitions to those modeled filtered events with the specified registered latency.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset with filtered SCL and SDA high, inject a raw scl_i or sda_i glitch shorter than the synchronizer/filter acceptance interval that nominally resembles a START or STOP, then return both lines to their original levels without applying a stable filtered transition.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the rejected raw glitch produces no filtered START or STOP condition, and busy remains unchanged.
elements.check_method: Run the filter reference model to verify that the three-sample majority values and delayed values do not form sta_condition or sto_condition; check that busy has no transition after the modeled observation latency.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, issue a READ command with ena high, provide a stable SDA value, release SCL, and drive scl_i high long enough to produce a synchronized and filtered SCL rising edge during the READ sample window.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: dout captures the synchronized, filtered SDA value at the filtered SCL rising edge, with the registered output update on the corresponding processing clock.
elements.check_method: Model the two-stage synchronization, filter majority history, filtered rising edge, and registered dout update; compare dout with the modeled filtered SDA value only at the in-window filtered SCL rise.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, issue a READ command, and inject a raw scl_i rising pulse shorter than the synchronization/filter acceptance interval during the read sample phase, or apply a stable SCL rising edge only while the FSM is outside the READ sample phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the rejected raw SCL glitch, or a filtered SCL rise outside the READ sample phase, does not cause the read sample attributed to this requirement; dout remains at its prior value until a valid in-window filtered SCL rising edge occurs.
elements.check_method: Use the filter and FSM reference model to classify each SCL rise as accepted/rejected and in-window/out-of-window; assert no dout update for rejected or out-of-window events and require capture only for a valid in-window filtered rise.

elements.stimulus: Enable the controller, hold scl_i high, and drive the external sda_i line high-to-low long enough to pass the SDA synchronizer/filter as a START condition. Then drive sda_i low-to-high while scl_i remains high long enough to pass the filter as a STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the requirement: busy asserts after the filtered START transition and deasserts after the filtered STOP transition, demonstrating that the external SDA line presented through sda_i is used for bus-condition detection.
elements.check_method: Monitor the filtered SDA history/transition and compare registered busy against a reference model: busy must rise following the filtered high-to-low transition with filtered SCL high, then fall following the filtered low-to-high transition with filtered SCL high.

elements.stimulus: Enable the controller with scl_i held low, and toggle the externally driven sda_i line through high-to-low and low-to-high transitions. Also inject an SDA pulse while scl_i is high that is shorter than the filter interval, so no qualifying filtered SDA transition is produced.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding case of the requirement: busy must not change because of these sda_i transitions; in particular, no START or STOP status effect is allowed without a qualifying filtered SDA transition while SCL is high.
elements.check_method: Compare busy and the filtered SDA transition indicators against the reference filter model on every clock. Confirm that the injected transitions do not produce a qualifying filtered START or STOP and that busy remains at its pre-stimulus value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep filtered SCL high with both lines externally released, then drive sda_i from high to low and hold it long enough for the two-stage synchronizer and three-sample majority filter to qualify the transition.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for busy: after the synchronized and filtered SDA high-to-low transition, busy asserts, corresponding to filtered START detection; busy does not assert before the filtered transition.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the SDA synchronizer, sampling history, majority filter, and delayed filtered SDA. Compare the predicted filtered START event and registered busy value cycle by cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep filtered SCL high and busy low, apply an sda_i low pulse shorter than the synchronization/filter qualification interval, then return sda_i high before a filtered SDA transition is produced.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for busy: busy remains low and no START/STOP status change occurs because the SDA event has not passed synchronization and filtering.
elements.check_method: Drive the pulse with respect to the reference model's qualification boundary, verify that the filtered SDA history never produces a START or STOP transition, and assert that busy remains at its pre-event value.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, first create a qualified filtered START so busy is high, keep filtered SCL high, then drive sda_i from low to high and hold it long enough for synchronization and three-sample filtering to qualify the transition.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for busy: busy clears only after the synchronized and filtered SDA low-to-high transition, corresponding to filtered STOP detection.
elements.check_method: Compare sda_i, the modeled synchronized samples, majority-filtered SDA, STOP detection, and registered busy against the reference model on every enabled clock.

elements.stimulus: With busy high from a previously qualified START and filtered SCL high, apply an sda_i high pulse shorter than the synchronization/filter qualification interval, then return it low without allowing a filtered SDA low-to-high transition.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for busy: busy remains high; the raw SDA pulse does not create a STOP indication or clear busy.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to confirm no qualified low-to-high filtered SDA edge occurs, then compare the observed busy output with the expected unchanged value.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a READ command while the bus is idle, allow the controller to release SDA and enter the READ sample window, drive sda_i to a stable high value sufficiently before the filtered SCL rising edge for synchronization and majority filtering to qualify it, and allow the filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for dout: dout updates to 1 on the registered cycle that processes the filtered SCL rising edge, reflecting the synchronized and filtered SDA value rather than an unqualified raw value.
elements.check_method: Model the SDA synchronizer/filter and filtered SCL edge, then compare dout at the read sampling cycle with the modeled filtered SDA value and verify the registered one-cycle output latency.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a READ command with dout initialized to 0, enter the READ sample window, and change sda_i from low to high too late for the two-stage synchronizer and three-sample filter to qualify it before the filtered SCL rising edge; keep the raw transition visible at that edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for dout: dout remains 0 at the read sampling point and does not capture the late raw SDA high value, because that value has not passed synchronization and filtering.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to show that filtered SDA is still 0 when filtered SCL rises, then compare the registered dout result with the modeled filtered value rather than the raw sda_i level.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a WRITE command with din=1, wait until the FSM reaches the released-SDA stable high arbitration-check phase, and apply an sda_i low pulse shorter than the synchronization/filter qualification interval before releasing it high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for al: al remains deasserted and the WRITE is not aborted, because the transient low SDA evidence has not passed synchronization and filtering.
elements.check_method: Correlate the write-high-phase and arbitration-check timing with the modeled filtered SDA value; verify no filtered arbitration-loss condition occurs and compare al and command completion with the expected normal path.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a WRITE command with din=1, wait for the released-SDA stable high arbitration-check phase, then hold sda_i low long enough for synchronization and majority filtering to qualify the low value.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for al: al asserts when the synchronized and filtered SDA indicates arbitration loss, the active WRITE aborts without cmd_ack, and both output enables release.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to predict the filtered SDA low and arbitration-loss event, then compare al, cmd_ack, FSM completion/abort behavior, and scl_oen/sda_oen after the registered updates.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, issue cmd=START=4'b0001, and provide the bus conditions needed for the START sequence to reach its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the START sequence finishes, cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle; it is low on the following cycle and no additional acknowledge pulse occurs.
elements.check_method: Use a reference FSM to identify the START terminal completion edge, sample cmd_ack after each posedge clk, assert a one-cycle high pulse at that edge, and assert low on the next and all subsequent idle cycles.

elements.stimulus: Reset the controller, establish a busy bus by completing a START command, then set ena=1 and issue cmd=STOP=4'b0010 with scl_i and sda_i driven to permit the STOP sequence to finish.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the STOP sequence reaches completion, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle, then returns low and remains low while idle.
elements.check_method: Track the STOP sequence terminal phase in the reference model and compare the registered cmd_ack waveform cycle by cycle, requiring exactly one high sample associated with STOP completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the bus released high, issue cmd=WRITE=4'b0100 with din=0, and allow the write bit sequence to complete without arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at completion of the WRITE bit cycle, cmd_ack is high for one clk cycle only; it is low before completion and on every cycle after that pulse.
elements.check_method: Predict the WRITE terminal completion edge from the driven bus and reference timing model, then compare cmd_ack after every posedge for one-and-only-one asserted cycle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep SDA released and drive the external SDA value to 1 during the READ sample window, issue cmd=READ=4'b1000, and allow the read bit cycle to complete.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the READ sequence finishes after its sample and low phase, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle and then is deasserted.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to locate the READ terminal phase, verify cmd_ack is low before that phase, high for exactly one sampled clock cycle at completion, and low on the next cycle.

elements.stimulus: While idle with ena=1, drive cmd=NOP=4'b0000 and each unsupported encoding 4'b0011, 4'b0101, 4'b0110, 4'b0111, 4'b1001, 4'b1010, 4'b1011, 4'b1100, 4'b1101, 4'b1110, and 4'b1111 for at least one enabled clock each, without issuing a supported command.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise case: because no supported command is completing, cmd_ack remains low for every cycle and no acknowledge pulse is generated.
elements.check_method: Scoreboard cmd_ack against the reference command decoder for each command encoding and assert that it never becomes high during or after these no-op command drives.

elements.stimulus: Issue cmd=WRITE=4'b0100 with ena=1 and hold filtered SCL low after the controller releases SCL, preventing the write sequence from reaching its terminal phase; observe cmd_ack while the command is stalled.
elements.expected_response: Otherwise case: while the current WRITE command has not finished, cmd_ack remains low; if the bus is subsequently released and the command completes, exactly one pulse occurs only at that later completion.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model's slave-wait state to identify nonterminal cycles, assert cmd_ack is low throughout the stall, then verify one and only one pulse at the eventual terminal completion edge.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i and sda_i high, and issue cmd=START for one enabled idle clock. Allow the START sequence to progress through its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the START sequence finishes, cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle and is low on the immediately preceding and following cycles.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model to identify the START terminal phase; sample cmd_ack after each posedge and assert a single-cycle pulse exactly at that terminal event, with no adjacent-cycle assertion.

elements.stimulus: Establish a busy bus state, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=0, hold the externally released bus high as needed, and issue cmd=STOP for one enabled idle clock. Allow the STOP sequence to complete.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the STOP sequence finishes, cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle and is low before and after that completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Reference-model the STOP terminal phase and compare the registered cmd_ack waveform cycle by cycle, requiring one and only one high cycle aligned with completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i high and provide sda_i high, set din=0, and issue cmd=WRITE for one enabled idle clock. Let the write bit sequence reach its terminal low phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the WRITE command finishes, cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clk cycle, with cmd_ack low on all other cycles surrounding the completion.
elements.check_method: Determine completion from the reference FSM terminal transition and check that cmd_ack has exactly one registered high sample aligned to that transition and no extra or stretched pulse.
