elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, set clk_cnt=0, release SDA externally high during the read window, and issue cmd=READ for one enabled idle clock. Allow the read sequence to capture the bit and complete its following low phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when the READ command finishes, cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle and returns low on the next cycle; it is not asserted during the earlier read sampling window.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model's read terminal phase and filtered-SCL event to distinguish sampling from completion, then compare cmd_ack cycle by cycle for one pulse only at completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, accept a WRITE command with ena high and clk_cnt=0, hold the bus response valid, and observe the command while it is in an intermediate SDA/SCL phase before its terminal low phase; continue running afterward until the command completes.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case (the 'otherwise' side): while the active WRITE sequence has not reached its terminal completion phase, cmd_ack remains low and does not produce a completion pulse; only the later terminal phase may produce the one-cycle pulse.
elements.check_method: Reference-model every non-terminal WRITE cycle and assert cmd_ack=0 for those cycles; separately verify that any eventual pulse occurs only at the modeled terminal phase and lasts one cycle.

elements.stimulus: While idle with ena high and clk_cnt=0, drive cmd=NOP=0000, then each unsupported 4-bit command encoding other than START=0001, STOP=0010, WRITE=0100, and READ=1000, holding the bus released.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case (the 'otherwise' side): no supported command sequence finishes, so cmd_ack remains low for every observed clk cycle and no one-cycle completion pulse is generated.
elements.check_method: Enumerate all unsupported command values and compare the observed cmd_ack trace against a reference model that keeps the FSM idle, requiring cmd_ack=0 throughout.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 long enough for the synchronizer and three-sample filter to settle. Drive sda_i=0 while keeping scl_i=1 until sta_condition asserts, then hold the bus and later drive sda_i=1 while scl_i=1 until sto_condition asserts.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: busy rises after the filtered START condition and remains high during the START-to-STOP interval; busy falls after the subsequent filtered STOP condition.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered START and STOP probe assertions as reference-model events, then compare registered busy after each event: busy must be high after sta_condition and low after sto_condition, with no unexpected intermediate transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=0 and sda_i=1 until the filtered lines settle. Toggle sda_i from 1 to 0 and back to 1 while scl_i remains 0, then keep both lines stable without generating a filtered START or STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: because no START is detected while filtered SCL is low, busy does not rise; without a prior active START-to-STOP interval, busy remains low and does not fall from a falsely asserted state.
elements.check_method: Assert that sta_condition and sto_condition remain deasserted during the stimulus and compare busy against a reference model initialized low; sample busy after filter settling and after each transition, requiring it to remain low.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al=0, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a value that permits progress, issue a WRITE command with din=1, and keep the external SDA line low throughout the phase where the master has released SDA (sda_oen=1) and performs its arbitration check. Keep filtered SCL high for the write high phase.
elements.expected_response: At the arbitration-loss event, al rises to 1, indicating that arbitration has been lost. The indicator remains asserted after the command aborts and is not cleared by subsequent idle clocks.
elements.check_method: Monitor the registered al output after each posedge and compare it with a reference model keyed to the released-high WRITE arbitration-checking phase and filtered SDA low; verify assertion on the loss event and persistence until reset.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al=0, set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a value that permits progress, issue a WRITE command with din=1, and keep the external SDA line high during the entire phase where the master has released SDA (sda_oen=1) and performs its arbitration check. Provide normal SCL timing without stretching.
elements.expected_response: At the corresponding arbitration-checking point, al remains deasserted at 0 because arbitration has not been lost; the WRITE proceeds normally rather than indicating arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Monitor al after each posedge and compare against a reference model for the non-loss case; verify it remains 0 through the arbitration-checking phase and until normal command completion.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a released-high bus, issue WRITE (cmd=0100) with din=1. Wait until the write bit reaches its released SCL-high arbitration-checking phase (sda_oen=1 and sda_chk=1), then externally hold SDA low long enough for the filtered SDA value fsda to become 0 while the command remains active.
elements.expected_response: al asserts high when filtered SDA is low during the released-SDA arbitration-checking phase, as the holding side of the requirement. The write command aborts without generating cmd_ack and the controller releases both output-enable lines.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after the filtered SDA update, assert that al becomes 1 on the first qualifying fsda=0 and sda_chk=1 event while sda_oen=1; also assert that no cmd_ack pulse occurs for the aborted command and that al remains high until reset.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a released-high bus, issue WRITE (cmd=0100) with din=0 or din=1 and wait until the command is active with filtered SCL high. Drive filtered SDA from low to high by changing the external SDA drive and holding the resulting line levels long enough for the STOP condition to be detected, without issuing a STOP command.
elements.expected_response: al asserts high when an unrequested filtered STOP condition occurs during the active WRITE command, as the holding side of the requirement. The active command aborts and no cmd_ack pulse is generated.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered transition reference model to identify sto_condition=1 while fsm_active=1 and the command is not STOP; assert that al is high on the corresponding registered output update, that cmd_ack remains low for the aborted command, and that al stays high until reset.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and a released-high bus, issue WRITE (cmd=0100) with din=1. Keep external SDA high throughout the released SCL-high arbitration-checking phase and do not generate a STOP condition; allow the write command to complete normally.
elements.expected_response: al does not assert at the arbitration-checking event or during normal completion, as the contrasting non-holding side of the requirement. The command proceeds to completion and produces its normal one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Monitor fsda, sda_chk, sda_oen, fsm_active, and sto_condition with a cycle-accurate reference model; assert that no qualifying arbitration-loss condition occurs and that al remains 0 through command completion, while exactly one cmd_ack pulse is observed.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000), allow the READ sequence to enter its sample window with scl_oen=1, hold the external SDA line at 1, and provide a stable SCL high transition that produces a filtered_scl_rise.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to 1. This is the holding case of shows: dout updates to the received data bit.
elements.check_method: Monitor filtered_scl_rise and sample dout after the subsequent registered update; compare dout against the externally driven filtered SDA value of 1 and verify the value changes from a known opposite pre-sample value.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, issue cmd=READ, enter the READ sample window with dout initialized to 0, present SDA=1, and apply an SCL high glitch shorter than the filter interval so that no filtered_scl_rise occurs.
elements.expected_response: dout remains 0 and does not update to the presented received bit because the required filtered SCL sampling event did not occur. This is the non-holding side of shows: dout does not update to the received data bit.
elements.check_method: Assert that filter_cnt_expired and filter_sample_update do not produce a filtered SCL rising edge for the glitch, then compare dout before and after the glitch and require no change to 1.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous reset, release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a READ command on an enabled clock, and model the external bus so filtered SCL is low during the initial phase, then drive SDA stably low and release SCL high long enough for the three-sample filter to produce a filtered SCL rising edge while filtered SDA is 0.
elements.expected_response: At the registered update corresponding to the filtered SCL rising edge, dout becomes 0, equal to the filtered SDA value captured at that edge. This is the shows side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronization, three-sample majority filtering, filtered SCL edge detection, and registered dout timing; compare dout immediately after each posedge where filtered_scl_rise is asserted and require dout == fsda.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and establish a known dout value, issue a READ command with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the external SCL low so filtered SCL remains low, and toggle or stably change external SDA from the value corresponding to the current dout to the opposite value without allowing a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: While no filtered SCL rising edge occurs, dout retains its previous value and does not change to the new filtered SDA value. This is the otherwise side of the requirement.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter model to identify cycles with filtered_scl_rise=0; compare dout against its prior registered value on those cycles, including after filtered SDA changes, and require no premature capture.

elements.stimulus: After reset, observe the DUT in idle, then with ena=1 issue START, WRITE with din=0, READ, and STOP commands while allowing each command to progress through all FSM phases.
elements.expected_response: The required shows side is observed: scl_o remains exactly 1'b0 during idle and throughout every START, WRITE, READ, and STOP phase, independently of scl_oen and command activity.
elements.check_method: At every clock observation after settled registered updates, assert scl_o == 1'b0 and record coverage for idle and each command sequence; independently compare scl_o against a constant-zero reference model.

elements.stimulus: While the DUT is idle and again while it executes an enabled command, force or inject a nonzero value on the scl_o observation net for at least one interface observation, without changing scl_oen or the external SCL bus.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting otherwise side is observed: scl_o is nonzero. The checker shall flag this observation as a failure of REQ-0039, because scl_o must be constant-low; scl_oen remains the only intended SCL line-control signal.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_o on every sampled interface observation and deliberately inject a nonzero value; verify the assertion/reference comparison reports a violation at the first injected nonzero sample and distinguishes it from scl_oen activity.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and both external bus lines high. Issue the START command and advance clocks until the START sequence reaches its phase that pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: During the SCL-low phase, scl_oen is 0, which is the shows side indicating that SCL is driven low; with the external bus model, the observed SCL line is low.
elements.check_method: At each settled rising clock edge, compare registered scl_oen against the reference START phase and verify that scl_oen=0 coincides with a low modeled SCL line.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and both external bus lines high. Issue the START command and observe the preceding START phase in which the controller releases SCL, before it pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: While SCL is released, scl_oen is 1, which is the contrasting shows side indicating that the controller does not drive SCL low; the modeled SCL line remains high because no external participant drives it low.
elements.check_method: At each settled rising clock edge, compare registered scl_oen against the reference START phase and verify that scl_oen=1 coincides with a released, high modeled SCL line.

elements.stimulus: Deassert reset, set ena=1, present cmd=START while the bus inputs are released high, and hold the command and bus inputs so the accepted START sequence reaches its initial release phase before SDA is pulled low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: during the START initial release phase, scl_oen is 1, indicating that SCL is released for the external pull-up, and sda_o is 0.
elements.check_method: At settled samples after each posedge, identify the START release phase by scl_oen=1 followed by the subsequent sda_oen transition from 1 to 0 while scl_oen remains 1; compare scl_oen and sda_o against the expected values and record bins for scl_oen=1 and sda_o=0.

elements.stimulus: Using the same accepted START command, continue clocking with ena=1 until the START sequence pulls SCL low, then hold the sequence in that phase long enough to observe the registered outputs.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: scl_oen is 0 when the controller drives SCL low, while sda_o remains 0 rather than becoming high; this is the otherwise side of the scl_oen observation and confirms the constant-low SDA drive value.
elements.check_method: After the START release phase, detect the transition of scl_oen from 1 to 0 and sample outputs after the corresponding posedge; assert scl_oen=0 and sda_o=0 for the SCL-driven-low phase, with no observed sda_o=1 value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and the externally driven SDA line high, set din=0, and issue a WRITE command. Run until the WRITE data phase is reached.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data phase, sda_oen reads 0; this is the holding case of REQ-0042, and the active-low enable drives the SDA line low.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare the observed sda_oen value with the reference command-phase model and verify that sda_oen=0 coincides with a low resolved SDA bus level when no external device drives SDA.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and the externally driven SDA line high, and issue a READ command. Run until the READ SCL-high sampling window is reached.
elements.expected_response: During the READ window, sda_oen reads 1; this is the contrasting case of REQ-0042, and SDA is released rather than driven low.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare the observed sda_oen value with the reference READ-phase model and verify that sda_oen=1 leaves the resolved SDA bus high when no external device drives it low.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, then deassert reset with ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and external SDA and SCL released high. Issue the START command cmd=4'b0001 and observe the command sequence after each posedge clk.
elements.expected_response: During the START sequence's phase before SDA is pulled low, sda_oen is 1; this is the holding case for REQ-0043, and the open-drain bus model shows SDA released so the external pull-up drives SDA high.
elements.check_method: At settled post-posedge samples, correlate the START command sequence with sda_oen. Assert sda_oen==1 during the SDA-release phase and, with no external SDA-low drive, assert the modeled SDA line is high.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, then deassert reset with ena=1, clk_cnt=0 and external SCL released high. Issue the WRITE command cmd=4'b0100 with din=0, and observe the write data phase after each posedge clk.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data phase, sda_oen is 0; this is the contrasting non-holding case from REQ-0043, and SDA is driven low rather than released for the external pull-up.
elements.check_method: At settled post-posedge samples during the WRITE data phase, assert sda_oen==0 and use the open-drain bus model to assert that SDA is low even when the external participant does not drive it low.

elements.stimulus: Operate the module after reset in idle with ena=1, then issue NOP and unsupported cmd values while keeping scl_i and sda_i high.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: scl_o=0 and sda_o=0 at every sampled clock edge; the module never drives either line high directly. Any scl_o=1 or sda_o=1 is the otherwise side of shows and fails the requirement.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk after reset settles, compare scl_o and sda_o against constant 0 and record a failure on any high value.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, execute START, WRITE with din=0, WRITE with din=1, READ, and STOP sequences, allowing normal SCL high/release and low/drive phases and completing each command.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows across every command phase: scl_o=0 and sda_o=0, including when scl_oen or sda_oen releases a line and when either line is driven low. Any scl_o=1 or sda_o=1 during an active or terminal phase is the contrasting otherwise side of shows and fails the requirement.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_o and sda_o continuously at settled posedge observations throughout each commanded sequence; assert both outputs are always 0 independently of output-enable state, command, and bus phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, observe the DUT in idle, then issue NOP, START, STOP, WRITE with din=0, WRITE with din=1, and READ commands with ena high while allowing each command to progress through its normal FSM phases.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_o and sda_o remain constantly 1'b0 at every clock observation during idle and every command/FSM phase, independent of output-enable activity.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge observation, assert scl_o === 1'b0 and sda_o === 1'b0; record coverage for idle and each exercised command phase.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the idle and command-phase observation while applying a verification-only fault injection that forces either scl_o or sda_o to 1 for at least one clock observation.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding contrast: an observed scl_o=1 or sda_o=1 is classified as a violation of the requirement; the required DUT behavior is the contrasting constant-low value 1'b0.
elements.check_method: Use the assertion/checker to compare each sampled output against 1'b0 and require a failure at the forced-high observation, confirming that the checker distinguishes the non-holding side of the port behavior.

elements.stimulus: Release the external SCL and SDA drivers, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=0, and issue the WRITE command (cmd=0100). On each clock, monitor the registered output enables and stop during the WRITE low phase when scl_oen=0 and sda_oen=0.
elements.expected_response: For the asserted-low side of REQ-0046, scl_oen=0 causes the resolved SCL line to be low and sda_oen=0 causes the resolved SDA line to be low, regardless of the external drivers being released. scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0.
elements.check_method: Use an open-drain bus model: resolved_scl = 0 when scl_oen=0 or the external SCL driver is low, otherwise 1; resolved_sda = 0 when sda_oen=0 or the external SDA driver is low, otherwise 1. At the monitored WRITE low phase, compare both resolved lines with 0 and verify both enables are 0.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, then release it while keeping ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and external SCL/SDA drivers released. Wait for the reset state and then allow the controller to remain idle without issuing a command.
elements.expected_response: For the released-high side of REQ-0046, scl_oen=1 causes the resolved SCL line to be released and sda_oen=1 causes the resolved SDA line to be released; with external pull-ups, both resolved lines are high. scl_o and sda_o remain constant 0.
elements.check_method: After asynchronous reset settles, verify scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1. Use the open-drain bus model with released external drivers and pull-ups, and compare resolved_scl and resolved_sda with 1. Confirm the enables remain high while idle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=START, and leave scl_i and sda_i high with no external participant pulling either line low. Accept the START command and observe the initial START-sequence interval in which both lines are intended to be released.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1. With the external pull-ups and no competing low drive, the observed SCL and SDA lines are high; the high level is supplied externally rather than driven by the DUT.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge during the released interval, compare scl_oen and sda_oen against 1 and model each bus line as high when its DUT output enable is released and the external line input is high. Fail if either enable is 0 or either released line is observed low without an external low driver.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=0, cmd=WRITE, and leave the external SDA and SCL participants released high. Accept the WRITE command and observe the data-drive phase before SCL is released.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: sda_oen=0 and the resolved SDA line is low because the DUT actively pulls it low; the high level is not provided by the external pull-up in this interval. The output enable must not be 1 for this din=0 data phase.
elements.check_method: During the WRITE data-drive phase, compare sda_oen against 0 and resolve SDA as low when the DUT drives low, regardless of the external pull-up. Confirm the phase is distinct from the released-high case by checking that sda_oen is not 1.

elements.stimulus: Apply no command or bus stimulus; review item 2 and its associated requirement text.
elements.expected_response: No DUT behavior, output value, timing, or status transition is required by this item.
elements.check_method: Requirements review confirms that item 2 contains no behavioral obligation or observable expectation; no DUT assertion is generated.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0, then release it and keep rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=3, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Issue a supported START command on an enabled clock and, after command acceptance, continue clocking with the bus released until the reference divider model predicts cnt expiration.
elements.expected_response: This is the timing-enable side of the observation: when cnt expires, cnt reloads from clk_cnt and clk_en is asserted; on the following registered FSM update, scl_oen changes to the next START command timing phase, rather than holding its prior value. Subsequent phase changes occur only at further predicted timing-enable events.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of cnt reload/decrement and clk_en generation with clk_cnt=3. Sample scl_oen after each posedge and compare every change against the model's predicted command-phase transition; assert that the transition occurs at the first expiration and that no phase transition occurs on intervening non-expiration clocks.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0, then release it and keep rst=0, clk_cnt=3, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Issue a supported START command with ena=1 and wait until the command is active and scl_oen has entered a non-idle START phase. Before the next predicted timing expiration, drive ena=0 and hold it low for several clocks, then restore ena=1.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding side of the observation: while timing is disabled by ena=0, scl_oen holds its current command-phase value and the FSM does not advance, even though the disabled-counter behavior reloads cnt from clk_cnt and asserts the timing-enable condition. After ena returns high, the FSM resumes only on a subsequently modeled enabled timing event.
elements.check_method: Record scl_oen immediately before ena is deasserted and compare it after every posedge while ena=0; require no change and no command-phase advancement. Use the divider reference model to verify reload behavior at disable and require the first post-enable scl_oen transition to align with the next valid enabled clk_en event.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 asynchronously, then nReset=1 and rst=0. Set ena=1, clk_cnt=4, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1 with no external clock stretching or SCL synchronization. Issue the supported START command for one enabled clock and then drive cmd=NOp. Measure clk cycles from command acceptance until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case for REQ-0050: while ena=1, reset is inactive, the divider is nonzero, and no synchronization or slave-wait condition occurs, the divider countdown progresses on every rising edge. cmd_ack remains low during the expected nonzero-divider countdown and pulses for exactly one clock only at the START terminal phase, with latency matching the reference divider model for clk_cnt=4.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of cnt reload/decrement and FSM advancement. Assert that each enabled rising edge before counter expiry advances the modeled countdown, that cmd_ack is absent before the modeled terminal phase, and that the observed one-cycle cmd_ack agrees with the modeled divider-dependent latency.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 asynchronously, then nReset=1 and rst=0. Set ena=1, clk_cnt=4, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Issue a supported START command and, after the command has been accepted and is active, set ena=0 for three rising edges of clk; then set ena=1 and continue until completion. Keep rst=0, nReset=1, and prevent external SCL stretching or SCL synchronization throughout.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case: while ena=0, the divider is reloaded and command timing is paused, so the counter does not decrement and cmd_ack does not pulse or occur earlier than it would with the three disabled clocks included as a pause. After ena returns high, countdown and FSM progress resume, and cmd_ack is a one-clock pulse at the correspondingly delayed terminal phase. An uninterrupted countdown producing an earlier ack is the REQ-0050 violation side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Compare cmd_ack timing against two reference traces: an enabled countdown model and a model that holds/reloads timing during the three ena-low clocks. Assert no cmd_ack during the disabled interval and require the post-resume pulse to match the paused model, not the uninterrupted-countdown model.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a nonzero value, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0 while the bus is initially high, then, after the WRITE sequence releases SCL, externally hold scl_i low long enough for the filtered SCL to remain low and slave_wait to assert. Keep rst=0 and nReset=1 and maintain the external SCL-low condition for several enabled clock intervals.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case of the requirement: while slave_wait is asserted, scl_oen remains 1 and does not transition to 0; the WRITE high phase and timing progression remain paused, inserting wait states until filtered SCL becomes high.
elements.check_method: After each posedge clk, sample scl_oen after registered updates settle and compare against a reference divider/FSM model. Confirm slave_wait is asserted and that scl_oen stays 1 across multiple expected counter-expiration opportunities, with no transition to 0 until the external SCL release is filtered high.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt to a nonzero value, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0 while the bus is initially high, and keep scl_i high after the WRITE sequence releases SCL so filtered SCL is high and slave_wait does not assert.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case of the requirement: when filtered SCL is high and no stretching is active, scl_oen transitions from 1 to 0 at the normal timing phase boundary, pulling SCL low and allowing the WRITE sequence to continue.
elements.check_method: After each posedge clk, sample scl_oen after registered updates settle and compare with the reference divider/FSM model. Confirm no slave_wait assertion and verify that scl_oen transitions to 0 after the expected clk_en/timing interval rather than remaining at 1 indefinitely.

elements.stimulus: No DUT stimulus; inspect the requirement text and its linked verification plan entry.
elements.expected_response: No functional DUT response is required or asserted because REQ-0052 states no obligation and defines no observable output.
elements.check_method: Requirements-review check confirming the element records REQ-0052 as non-functional scaffolding and introduces no additional DUT expectation.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, select a valid WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=0, configure clk_cnt=0, keep the bus initially high, and accept the command. When the WRITE sequence releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1), externally hold scl_i low long enough for the synchronized three-sample filter to make fscl low.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in which the requirement's shows clause applies: slave_wait asserts while scl_oen remains 1 and filtered SCL remains low; the WRITE FSM does not advance to its post-high-phase state or complete the command until fscl becomes high.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after outputs settle, compare scl_oen, fscl, slave_wait, fsm_active, and cmd_ack against a divider/filter/FSM reference model. Require slave_wait to assert after the released-SCL phase is reached, remain asserted throughout filtered SCL low, and require no cmd_ack or high-phase advancement during the wait.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, select a valid WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=0, configure clk_cnt=0, keep the bus and scl_i stably high, and accept the command. When the WRITE sequence releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1), continue driving scl_i high so the filtered SCL becomes and remains high.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding case in the shows clause: slave_wait remains deasserted because filtered SCL is high; scl_oen is released only for the normal high phase, the FSM advances to pull SCL low, and the WRITE command eventually produces its normal one-clock cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after outputs settle, compare scl_oen, fscl, slave_wait, fsm_active, and cmd_ack against a divider/filter/FSM reference model. Require no slave_wait assertion while scl_oen=1 and fscl=1, require normal transition out of the released-high phase, and require exactly one cmd_ack with no indefinite hold.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1, set clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=0 and sda_i=1, issue the supported START command cmd=4'b0001 on a clock edge, and continue holding scl_i=0 after the controller releases SCL through scl_oen=1.
elements.expected_response: When the command reaches its released-SCL phase, slave_wait asserts because the filtered external SCL remains low. The low external SCL indicates that a slave or another bus participant is holding SCL low; cmd_ack remains low and the START command does not complete for as long as scl_i remains low.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate divider, synchronizer, and filter reference model to identify the released-SCL/slave-wait interval. Assert scl_oen=1 and scl_i=0 during that interval, then assert cmd_ack=0 on every settled posedge until scl_i is released high and the modeled command completion phase occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1, set clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, issue the supported START command cmd=4'b0001 on a clock edge, and leave scl_i high after the controller releases SCL through scl_oen=1.
elements.expected_response: The released SCL is high, so the slave-wait condition does not persist; the command progresses through completion and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock. This is the contrasting non-holding case to the requirement's low-external-SCL indication.
elements.check_method: Use the same cycle-accurate reference model to determine when the filtered SCL becomes high and the START sequence completes. Check that cmd_ack is low before completion, asserts for one settled posedge only, and returns low on the following clock, with no indefinite postponement attributable to SCL stretching.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt. Issue a WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=0 while the bus is initially high. When the WRITE phase releases SCL (scl_oen=1), externally hold scl_i low long enough for filtered SCL to remain low and slave_wait to assert; then keep scl_i low for multiple expected timing ticks before releasing it high.
elements.expected_response: While the stretch remains active and slave_wait=1, scl_oen remains 1, the WRITE FSM does not advance to the phase that pulls SCL low, and the timing counter does not expire or generate timing progress. After filtered SCL becomes high, timing resumes and scl_oen eventually transitions to 0 at the next permitted WRITE phase. This is the holding case of the specified scl_oen behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the clocked reference model for the divider, filtered SCL, slave_wait, and FSM phase. During every cycle with slave_wait=1, assert that the modeled counter value and WRITE phase are unchanged and that observed scl_oen remains 1. After filtered SCL rises, compare the observed scl_oen transition to 0 against the first resumed enabled timing tick.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and the same nonzero clk_cnt used in the stretch scenario. Issue a WRITE command cmd=0100 with din=0 while externally holding scl_i high throughout the transaction, including immediately after the controller releases SCL during the WRITE high phase.
elements.expected_response: Because filtered SCL is already high after scl_oen is released, slave_wait does not remain active; the timing counter continues to run and scl_oen transitions from 1 to 0 at the next permitted WRITE timing phase without the stretch-induced delay. This is the non-holding side of the specified scl_oen behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the same divider and FSM reference model with filtered SCL high. Confirm slave_wait is not asserted for the interval, verify the counter progresses and the WRITE phase advances, and compare the observed scl_oen transition to 0 with the model's next enabled timing tick; contrast its latency with the held-low scenario.

elements.stimulus: Encounter Item 4, the list-item marker, during requirements interpretation; apply no DUT input stimulus.
elements.expected_response: No hardware behavior is required or inferred, and no output obligation, state transition, timing requirement, or protocol response is generated for the DUT.
elements.check_method: Review the derived verification model and testplan traceability for Item 4; confirm it produces no DUT-facing checks or output expectations beyond this applicability audit.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and provide a released-high bus. Issue a START command, then wait until the START sequence releases SCL (scl_oen=1) and the filtered SCL is high. While SCL remains released, have another master pull scl_i low and hold it long enough for the synchronizer and three-sample filter to produce a filtered SCL falling edge.
elements.expected_response: For the holding case in REQ-0057, the controller asserts scl_sync when the filtered SCL falling edge is detected while scl_oen=1. The indication occurs only after the modeled synchronization/filter latency and does not occur before the filtered falling edge.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for two-stage SCL synchronization, filter sampling, majority filtering, and filtered-edge detection. At each enabled clock compare the scl_sync probe with the model prediction, requiring an assertion at the modeled filtered falling edge while scl_oen is high.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and provide a released-high bus. Issue a START command, then wait until the START sequence releases SCL (scl_oen=1) and the filtered SCL is high. Keep scl_i high and stable for multiple filter sampling intervals, with no external SCL falling edge.
elements.expected_response: For the non-holding contrast in REQ-0057, scl_sync remains deasserted because no falling edge occurs on filtered SCL while SCL is released.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm that filtered SCL remains high and contains no falling edge throughout the observation window; assert that scl_sync is low on every enabled clock in that window.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and the bus initially released high, issue a WRITE command with din=1. During the WRITE stable-high phase, while scl_oen=1, externally force the shared SCL line low and hold it long enough for the synchronized, majority-filtered SCL value to fall; then release the external SCL driver and allow the WRITE to complete.
elements.expected_response: The falling filtered SCL edge while scl_oen=1 is treated as another master forcing SCL low. cmd_ack is postponed beyond the normal WRITE terminal timing while synchronization timing is reloaded and the controller waits; after SCL is available again, the WRITE completes and produces its normal one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the synchronizer, filter, divider reload, and WRITE FSM timing. Record the expected normal completion point and assert that the observed cmd_ack does not occur at that point, occurs only after the filtered SCL synchronization and recovery sequence, and is exactly one clock wide.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and the bus initially released high, issue the same WRITE command with din=1 and keep the external SCL line high throughout the WRITE stable-high phase; do not create any externally forced filtered SCL falling edge while scl_oen=1.
elements.expected_response: The no-forced-falling-edge side of the contrast applies: cmd_ack occurs at the normal WRITE completion after the controller pulls SCL low by returning scl_oen low, with no synchronization-induced postponement.
elements.check_method: Use the same reference model and clock_cnt as the forced-SCL test. Assert that cmd_ack occurs at the modeled normal terminal timing, is not delayed by a synchronization event, and is exactly one clock wide; compare this result against TP-0000.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and a nonzero clk_cnt, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0, and model the bus as released high. When the WRITE sequence releases SCL (scl_oen=1), have another master drive the shared SCL low long enough for the synchronized and filtered SCL to produce an externally caused falling edge, then release SCL and allow the command to continue.
elements.expected_response: The command completion cmd_ack pulse is postponed relative to the normal WRITE timing: after the filtered SCL falling edge while scl_oen=1, the controller reloads its timing counter, restarts the low-period timing, and does not acknowledge until that restarted timing has elapsed and the terminal WRITE phase completes.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the divider, synchronizer, filter, scl_sync event, and command FSM. Compare the observed one-clock cmd_ack pulse against the model and verify it occurs only after the synchronized low-period reload interval; correlate the event with scl_sync and cnt_zero probes.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and the same nonzero clk_cnt used in TP-0000, issue the same supported WRITE command with din=0, and model the released SCL line as remaining high throughout the WRITE high phase; do not inject an externally caused filtered SCL falling edge while scl_oen=1.
elements.expected_response: cmd_ack occurs at the normal command-completion timing for the WRITE command, without the additional synchronized low-period delay that is required when another master forces SCL low.
elements.check_method: Run the same cycle-accurate reference model and compare the observed one-clock cmd_ack pulse with the no-synchronization baseline. Verify no scl_sync event occurs and that the acknowledgment precedes the delayed acknowledgment from TP-0000 by the modeled reload-and-low-period interval.

elements.stimulus: No DUT stimulus; treat the numbered list-item marker "5." as scaffolding only.
elements.expected_response: No functional behavior, output, state transition, or timing obligation is expected from the DUT for this item.
elements.check_method: Specification-to-testplan review confirms that the item contains no requirement text or observable expectation; record the scenario as not applicable.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, hold scl_i high and sda_i high with busy low, then drive sda_i low on a clock boundary and hold it low for enough rising clk edges to pass through both synchronization stages and the input filtering interval.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of observed_via.shows: busy remains low during the required two-stage synchronization and filtering latency, then rises only after the synchronized and filtered SDA high-to-low transition is detected while filtered SCL is high.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of cSCL/cSDA capture, filter sampling, majority filtering, and START detection. Compare the sampled busy waveform and verify that no busy rise occurs before the modeled synchronization/filter latency and that busy rises at the modeled filtered START detection.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high, hold scl_i high and sda_i high with busy low, drive sda_i low between two rising clk edges, and return sda_i high before the next rising clk edge so the pulse is absent at both synchronization capture opportunities.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case of observed_via.shows: busy remains low; the short raw SDA pulse must not propagate through cSDA, must not produce a filtered START condition, and must not change the bus-busy status.
elements.check_method: Check the busy waveform against the reference synchronizer/filter model and assert that busy remains low for the entire test. Also verify that no filtered START event is produced after the pulse.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, set rst=0, ena=1, and clk_cnt=8. Drive scl_i=0 and sda_i=0 continuously. Run posedge clk cycles through the first filter_cnt_expired event while preserving ena=1.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the requirement: when filter_cnt_expired is asserted with ena=1, filter_sample_update asserts and the newly synchronized samples are shifted into both fSCL and fSDA histories. The corresponding fscl and fsda history values update according to the three-sample shift reference model.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, compare filter_sample_update, fscl, and fsda against a reference model of the filter counter, synchronized samples, and three-sample history shift. Require a history update on the modeled expiry event.

elements.stimulus: After reset release, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, drive scl_i=0 and sda_i=0 continuously, and observe a window of enabled posedge clk cycles beginning immediately after a filter-sample update and ending strictly before the next modeled filter_cnt_expired event.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of the requirement: while ena=1 but filter_cnt_expired is not asserted, filter_sample_update remains deasserted and neither fSCL nor fSDA shifts; both histories retain their prior values until the filter counter expires.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter-counter model to identify cycles between expiry events, then assert that filter_sample_update is 0 and that fscl and fsda equal their previous-cycle values throughout that interval. Flag any history change without a corresponding expiry as a failure.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset, then deassert it with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Keep the externally resolved SCL line high and SDA high until the filter histories are high. Then keep SCL high and drive SDA low continuously for at least two filter_sample_update events, allowing the synchronizer and filter model to account for their latency.
elements.expected_response: At the update where the three-sample SDA history contains at least two low samples, the majority-filtered SDA becomes low while the majority-filtered SCL remains high; busy rises after the corresponding registered detection. This is the majority-holds case of REQ-0063.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the synchronized samples, three-sample histories, and majority function. At every filter_sample_update compare fscl/fsda with the modeled majorities, and compare busy with the modeled START detection, requiring busy to transition from 0 to 1 only after the majority-filtered SDA high-to-low transition with majority-filtered SCL high.

elements.stimulus: Assert reset, then deassert it with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Keep the externally resolved SCL line high and SDA high until the filter histories are high. Drive SDA low only long enough to produce exactly one synchronized filter sample update, then return SDA high before a second low sample can be shifted into the history.
elements.expected_response: The three-sample SDA history never has a low majority, so the majority-filtered SDA remains high, no filtered START transition is detected, and busy remains unchanged at 0. This is the non-majority side of REQ-0063.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to confirm the history contains at most one low sample and that fsda remains equal to the majority value high while fscl remains high. Check that busy has no rising transition and remains 0 after the transient.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, allow the bus to settle with scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 until the controller is idle and the filtered SCL is high. Drive sda_i low for one clk, shorter than the filter sampling interval, then return it high without issuing a command.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: busy remains low; the short SDA glitch does not produce a filtered SDA high-to-low transition or a filtered START condition.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of the synchronizers, sampling interval, three-sample histories, and majority filter. At every settled posedge after the pulse, compare busy against the model and assert that no busy-high event occurs.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, allow scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 to settle while idle. Drive sda_i low and hold it for enough enabled clocks and filter samples to pass the three-sample majority filter while scl_i remains high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: busy rises after the filtered SDA high-to-low transition produces a filtered START condition.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to determine the cycle of the filtered START condition, then compare the registered busy output on subsequent settled posedges and require exactly the expected busy assertion.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, hold sda_i at 1, and drive scl_i low long enough for the filtered SCL value to become low. Then drive scl_i high for one clk, shorter than the filter sampling interval, and return it low.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: dout does not update; the short SCL high glitch does not produce a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.check_method: Record dout before the pulse and compare it after the pulse using the synchronizer/filter reference model to confirm no filtered SCL rising edge occurred and dout stayed unchanged.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8, hold sda_i at 1, and drive scl_i low until the filtered SCL is low. Then drive scl_i high and hold it long enough for the three-sample majority filter to produce a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: dout updates on the resulting filtered SCL rising edge to the filtered SDA value, which is 1.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to predict the filtered SCL rising-edge cycle and filtered SDA value, then compare dout after the registered update and require dout=1 only at that modeled event.

elements.stimulus: No hardware stimulus; inspect the specification mapping for list item 6 and execute the DUT test suite without adding behavior-specific stimulus for this item.
elements.expected_response: No hardware behavior, output value, timing property, protocol action, or state transition is required or attributed to list item 6.
elements.check_method: Static testplan/specification review: confirm the requirement is represented as having no observable hardware obligation and that no DUT assertion or coverage target is generated for behavior from this item.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 long enough for the synchronized three-sample filter histories and delayed filtered values to settle high. Continue holding scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 for multiple enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: The non-holding side of START detection is observed: because filtered SDA does not fall while filtered SCL is high, sta_condition remains 0 on every filtered-sample update; no START indication is produced.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after filter state updates settle, compare sta_condition with a reference model of the synchronizer, three-sample majority filter, delayed filtered SDA, and expression ~sSDA & dSDA & sSCL. Require sta_condition=0 throughout the stable-high interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. First drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 long enough for filtered SCL and SDA to settle high. While continuing to hold scl_i=1, drive sda_i=0 and hold it low long enough for synchronization and the three-sample majority filter to recognize the falling filtered SDA transition.
elements.expected_response: The holding side of START detection is observed: when filtered SDA falls from 1 to 0 while filtered SCL remains 1, sta_condition asserts for the detection interval, indicating an I2C START condition.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage input synchronization, filter sampling, three-sample majority histories, and delayed filtered SDA. Check that sta_condition equals 1 on the filtered transition cycle satisfying ~sSDA & dSDA & sSCL, and returns to 0 after the delayed transition is no longer present.

elements.stimulus: With ena high, drive the bus to a stable filtered state of sSCL=1, dSDA=0, and filtered SDA=0. Hold scl_i high and drive sda_i high long enough for synchronization and the three-sample filter to update filtered SDA to 1 while filtered SCL remains high.
elements.expected_response: The STOP condition is detected: sSDA=1, dSDA=0, sSCL=1, and sto_condition asserts for the corresponding detection cycle. This is the positive side of the required STOP-condition behavior.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare the reference-model filtered values and delayed SDA value against the DUT probes, and assert sto_condition == (fsda && !dsda && fscl); require sto_condition to assert only when all three terms are true.

elements.stimulus: Establish dSDA=0 and filtered SDA=0, then drive sda_i high long enough for filtered SDA to rise while driving scl_i low long enough that filtered SCL is 0 during the transition. Keep the filtered SCL low throughout the filtered SDA rising transition.
elements.expected_response: The STOP condition is not detected: although sSDA=1 and dSDA=0, sSCL=0, so sto_condition remains deasserted. This is the negative side of the required STOP-condition behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the filtered SDA rising transition and verify the DUT probe satisfies sto_condition == (fsda && !dsda && fscl); specifically require sto_condition == 0 for the transition while fscl == 0.

elements.stimulus: Review the Item 7 requirement record and run the complete applicable DUT scenario set without introducing any behavior-specific stimulus attributed to Item 7.
elements.expected_response: No additional DUT output, timing, state transition, or interface behavior is required or expected solely because of Item 7.
elements.check_method: Traceability and coverage audit: confirm REQ-0068 has no specified activation, observable, or expected behavior, and confirm the testplan contains no Item 7-specific DUT assertion beyond documenting that it is non-constraining.

elements.stimulus: With the bus initially idle and filtered SCL high, drive filtered SDA from high to low to create a valid START condition, then keep filtered SCL high and do not issue a STOP or reset.
elements.expected_response: When the START condition is detected, busy becomes high and remains high on every subsequent clock while no STOP condition occurs. This is the holding-high side of the requirement's observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor sta_condition and busy after registered updates; assert that busy is high in the cycle following START detection and remains high through a defined run of enabled clocks with no sto_condition, nReset assertion, or rst assertion.

elements.stimulus: With the bus initially idle and filtered SCL high, drive a valid START by transitioning filtered SDA from high to low, then while busy is high drive filtered SDA from low to high with filtered SCL remaining high to create a valid STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: busy becomes high after START detection, remains high until STOP detection, and becomes low after the STOP is detected. This is the contrasting low-after-STOP side of the requirement's observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor sta_condition, sto_condition, and registered busy; assert busy high between the detected START and STOP, then assert busy low in the cycle following STOP detection and before any subsequent START.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al cleared, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=0100 (WRITE), and din=1 for an enabled clock tick. Model the bus released high and keep filtered SDA high throughout the WRITE stable-high arbitration-checking window, identified by sda_chk=1, sda_oen=1, and scl_oen=1. Allow the WRITE sequence to complete.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting ordinary case from REQ-0070: because released SDA is observed filtered high during SDA arbitration checking, al remains low and no arbitration loss is reported.
elements.check_method: At every clock while sda_chk=1 and sda_oen=1, compare al against a reference model requiring 0; also verify al was 0 before the command and remains 0 after normal completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al cleared, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=0100 (WRITE), and din=1 for an enabled clock tick. Drive the bus so SDA is released by the DUT and SCL is released during the WRITE stable-high arbitration-checking window; then hold external sda_i low long enough for the synchronized three-sample filter to make filtered SDA low while sda_chk=1 and sda_oen=1.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case from REQ-0070: when the controller releases SDA high but observes filtered SDA low during SDA arbitration checking, al asserts. The active WRITE is aborted without a command-complete pulse, and the output enables are released.
elements.check_method: Use the reference synchronizer/filter model to determine when filtered SDA becomes low, then sample al after the corresponding posedge and require al=1 while sda_chk=1; verify no cmd_ack is generated for the aborted WRITE and that al remains asserted until reset.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT and set ena=1 with a nonzero clk_cnt. Accept a READ command while the bus is released high. During the active READ high phase, drive the external SDA line low long enough for the filtered SDA value to become low, then drive it high while filtered SCL remains high, producing a filtered STOP condition before the READ command completes.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered STOP-detection event while the FSM is executing the non-STOP READ command, al asserts; this is the asserting side of the observed_via shows behavior. The active command aborts and both output enables are released, with no cmd_ack for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: Use the filter and FSM reference model to identify the filtered STOP event and confirm fsm_active with a non-STOP command at that event. Sample al after the corresponding posedge and require it to be high, require no cmd_ack pulse after the abort, and require scl_oen and sda_oen to be released.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT with al cleared, set ena=1, and issue a requested STOP command while the bus is busy with filtered SDA low and filtered SCL high or becomes high during the STOP sequence. Allow the STOP sequence to release SDA while filtered SCL is high so that the expected filtered STOP condition is detected.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered STOP-detection event while the FSM is executing the requested STOP command, al remains deasserted; this is the non-asserting side of the observed_via shows behavior. The STOP command completes with exactly one cmd_ack pulse and busy clears.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the filtered STOP event and verify the active command encoding is STOP. Sample al after that posedge and require it remains low; separately count cmd_ack pulses and compare busy against the filtered STOP status transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue WRITE (cmd=0100) with din=1 while the bus is released high. Allow the command to enter its released SCL-high WRITE phase, then externally hold SDA low long enough for the filtered SDA value to become low while SDA is released; keep reset inactive and do not accept a new command.
elements.expected_response: Arbitration loss causes the main FSM to return to idle: on the cycle immediately following the arbitration-loss indication, fsm_active is low and both scl_oen and sda_oen are high, releasing SCL and SDA. This is the holding side of the observed_via shows statements for REQ-0072.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after the filtered arbitration-loss condition, sample settled registered outputs and the fsm_active probe; assert fsm_active==0, scl_oen==1, and sda_oen==1 before any new command is accepted.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue WRITE (cmd=0100) with din=0. Keep the external SDA line low as driven by the master and do not inject arbitration loss; observe the command during its active setup phase before SCL is released high.
elements.expected_response: Without arbitration loss, the FSM remains active: fsm_active is high, and the output enables follow the active WRITE sequence rather than the released-idle pair (during setup, scl_oen is low and sda_oen is low for din=0). This is the contrasting ordinary-behavior side of the observed_via shows statements for REQ-0072.
elements.check_method: At a settled posedge in the active WRITE setup phase, assert fsm_active==1 and compare scl_oen and sda_oen with the reference FSM phase, expecting both enables low; also verify no arbitration-loss transition has occurred.

elements.stimulus: Apply a representative reset and idle sequence, then exercise no specific behavior attributable to Item 9.
elements.expected_response: No DUT output, state transition, timing constraint, or protocol behavior is required by Item 9; any observed behavior is outside the scope of this requirement.
elements.check_method: Review the requirement-to-test trace and confirm that Item 9 is represented as non-behavioral and that no implementation assertion or pass/fail expectation is derived from it.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, rst low, ena high, and clk_cnt configured for enabled timing, issue cmd=READ (1000). Allow the READ sequence to release SDA and SCL, drive the external SDA line to a stable 0, and wait until the filtered SCL signal has a rising edge while the filtered SDA value is 0.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to 0, the current filtered SDA value. This is the holding case described by observed_via.shows.
elements.check_method: Use the filter/reference model to identify each filtered SCL rising edge and its corresponding filtered SDA value; sample dout after the clocked update settles and compare it with fsda at that edge, accounting for the specified registered one-clock observation timing.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted, rst low, ena high, and a READ command active, complete one filtered SCL rising-edge sample, then hold filtered SCL low so no new filtered SCL rising edge occurs while change the external SDA line and allow filtering to make fsda change.
elements.expected_response: dout retains its previously sampled value and does not capture the changed filtered SDA value, because no filtered SCL rising edge occurred. This is the otherwise/non-holding case described by observed_via.otherwise.
elements.check_method: Track filtered SCL transitions and fsda with the reference model; during the interval containing no filtered SCL rising edge, compare dout on every settled clock against its value before the fsda change and flag any update attributable to the SDA change.

elements.stimulus: With nReset deasserted and ena high, issue cmd=1000 (READ). During read_window, hold the external SDA line stable at 0 and allow filtered SCL to rise, producing filtered_scl_rise.
elements.expected_response: At the posedge that processes filtered_scl_rise, dout becomes 0 and remains available for the byte controller. This is the holding side of the observed_via shows condition: dout provides the received filtered SDA bit.
elements.check_method: At each filtered_scl_rise during read_sequence, compare the post-posedge registered dout value with the reference model's filtered SDA value; require dout=0 for this sample and no dependence on the raw, unfiltered SDA level.

elements.stimulus: Complete one READ sample with filtered SDA=0, then issue another READ with ena high. During its read_window, change the external SDA line and hold it stable at 1 long enough for filtering, then allow filtered SCL to rise and produce filtered_scl_rise.
elements.expected_response: At the second filtered_scl_rise, dout updates to 1 rather than retaining the previous 0. This is the contrast to the otherwise side of observed_via: dout must provide the newly received filtered SDA bit at the READ sampling edge, not fail to provide it or remain stale.
elements.check_method: Record dout after the first sample, then compare dout after the second filtered_scl_rise against the filtered SDA reference model; require the observed transition 0-to-1 at the corresponding registered sampling update.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 so the timing-enable tick occurs on every enabled clock. Issue a START command and keep the bus released high; observe scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack after each posedge until the command completes.
elements.expected_response: The command FSM advances through the START output phases only on clocks where the reference divider model asserts clk_en: output-enable phase changes occur on those clocks, and the terminal phase produces the one-clock cmd_ack. This is the 'clk_en asserted, FSM advances' side of the observation.
elements.check_method: A cycle-accurate reference model computes clk_en from ena and clk_cnt and predicts each START phase. Compare sampled scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack after settled posedges; flag any FSM-related output transition or completion pulse on a cycle for which the model says clk_en is not asserted.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=3. Issue a START command and keep the bus released high. After the command is accepted and the first START phase is visible, hold all inputs constant and monitor every posedge until the next divider expiration, then continue through completion.
elements.expected_response: During each interval in which the divider has not expired and the reference model therefore has clk_en deasserted, scl_oen and sda_oen remain in the current FSM phase and cmd_ack remains low; no command phase transition occurs. The next phase transition may occur only on the following clk_en assertion. This is the 'clk_en not asserted, FSM holds' side of the observation.
elements.check_method: Use a reference divider model to identify non-enable cycles and compare output enables and cmd_ack after each posedge. Require stable FSM-observable outputs on every non-clk_en cycle, while permitting and checking the expected phase transition only on the next clk_en cycle.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release nReset and rst, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold the bus released high, then present cmd=4'b0001 (START) while the FSM is idle for an enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: The FSM enters the START sequence: start_sequence becomes asserted and the START output phase begins. This is the supported-command side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset deassertion, compare the observed start_sequence probe and output-enable phase against a command-decode reference model; verify that start_sequence asserts and stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence do not assert for this command.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release nReset and rst, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish an idle bus state, then present cmd=4'b0010 (STOP) while the FSM is idle for an enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: The FSM enters the STOP sequence: stop_sequence becomes asserted and the STOP output phase begins. This is the supported-command side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset deassertion, compare the observed stop_sequence probe and output-enable phase against a command-decode reference model; verify that stop_sequence asserts and the other three sequence probes do not assert for this command.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release nReset and rst, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold the bus released high, then present cmd=4'b1000 (READ) while the FSM is idle for an enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: The FSM enters the READ sequence: read_sequence becomes asserted and the read operation begins with SDA released. This is the supported-command side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset deassertion, compare read_sequence and read_window against a command-decode reference model; verify read_sequence asserts and start_sequence, stop_sequence, and write_sequence do not assert for this command.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release nReset and rst, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold the bus released high, set din=0, then present cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) while the FSM is idle for an enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: The FSM enters the WRITE sequence: write_sequence becomes asserted and the write operation begins, with SDA driven according to din. This is the supported-command side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset deassertion, compare write_sequence, write_high_phase, and sda_oen against a command-decode reference model; verify write_sequence asserts and the START, STOP, and READ sequence probes do not assert for this command.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, release nReset and rst, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep the FSM idle, and present cmd=4'b0000 (NOP), then repeat with unsupported values 4'b0011, 4'b0101, 4'b0111, 4'b1001, 4'b1010, 4'b1011, 4'b1100, 4'b1101, 4'b1110, and 4'b1111, each for an enabled clock tick.
elements.expected_response: The FSM remains idle for every unsupported or NOP command: none of start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, or write_sequence asserts, and no command sequence is initiated. This is the contrasting non-supported-command side.
elements.check_method: For each command value, sample fsm_active and all four sequence probes after the enabled posedge and compare with a reference decoder; require fsm_active=0, all sequence probes=0, and no command-sequence output transition attributable to the command.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=START, and keep scl_i and sda_i released high. Apply the command while idle and run until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after command acceptance, the START sequence exhibits the prescribed phases: scl_oen and sda_oen initially release both lines, then sda_oen drives SDA low while scl_oen remains released, then scl_oen drives SCL low; sda_chk remains deasserted except where the timing reference model prescribes otherwise, and cmd_ack is a one-clock pulse at completion.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model triggered by the accepted START command and compare scl_oen, sda_oen, and sda_chk at every enabled FSM phase through cmd_ack, allowing registered-output latency.

elements.stimulus: Issue START as in TP-0000 and observe the transition from the initial START phase to the phase in which SDA is pulled low while SCL remains released.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the output pair changes from the START release phase (scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1) to the SDA-drive phase (scl_oen=1, sda_oen=0), with sda_chk matching the prescribed START-phase value; this is the required phase-dependent difference, not an inconsistent port level.
elements.check_method: Monitor consecutive settled posedge samples and assert the reference-model transition and exact active-low output-enable levels at the START phase boundary.

elements.stimulus: Establish busy with a completed START, then set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=STOP, keep scl_i and sda_i released high, and run until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the STOP sequence first drives SDA low with sda_oen=0, releases SCL with scl_oen=1 while SDA remains driven low, then releases SDA with sda_oen=1 while SCL is high; sda_chk follows the prescribed STOP phases and cmd_ack is a one-clock completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed scl_oen, sda_oen, and sda_chk waveform against the STOP reference-model phase sequence, including the registered output update and completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: Issue STOP after START and observe the transition from the STOP phase that drives SDA low to the phase that releases SDA while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: scl_oen remains released while sda_oen changes from 0 to 1, distinguishing the SDA-low STOP phase from the SDA-release STOP phase; sda_chk remains at the prescribed STOP value rather than using a WRITE arbitration-check value.
elements.check_method: Use phase-qualified assertions on consecutive posedge samples to check the required STOP output-enable transition and sda_chk value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=READ, keep scl_i released high, drive sda_i first low and then high on separate runs, and run each command until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the READ sequence releases SDA (sda_oen=1), releases SCL for the read window (scl_oen=1), captures the filtered SDA value on the filtered SCL rising edge, then pulls SCL low while keeping SDA released; sda_chk remains deasserted as prescribed and cmd_ack occurs after the low phase.
elements.check_method: Run the READ reference model for both returned data values and compare scl_oen, sda_oen, sda_chk, filtered-sample timing, and command completion at settled clock edges.

elements.stimulus: Issue READ with sda_i released high and observe the transition at the end of the read window when SCL is pulled low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the read-window phase has scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, while the following phase changes scl_oen to 0 and retains sda_oen=1; sda_chk remains at the prescribed READ value. The differing scl_oen levels demonstrate phase-dependent behavior.
elements.check_method: Detect the reference-model filtered SCL rising edge and compare the next enabled phase's registered output-enable levels and sda_chk against the READ waveform.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=WRITE, run once with din=0 and once with din=1, keep scl_i released high, and run until cmd_ack without externally forcing arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: WRITE drives or releases SDA according to din, releases SCL for the stable high phase, asserts sda_chk only in the din=1 released-high arbitration phase, then pulls SCL low and acknowledges. For din=0, SDA is driven low and no false arbitration check or loss occurs.
elements.check_method: Compare both din cases with the WRITE reference model at every phase, checking active-low sda_oen polarity, scl_oen, sda_chk qualification, and one-clock cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Issue WRITE with din=1 and observe the transition from the data-setup phase to the stable high phase, leaving SDA externally high.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the data-setup phase has sda_oen=1 for din=1 with SCL low, then the stable high phase has scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, and sda_chk=1; the later SCL-low phase has scl_oen=0. These changing levels are the prescribed WRITE timing contrast, not an inconsistent output.
elements.check_method: Use phase-qualified assertions and the reference model to check the consecutive WRITE output-enable levels and that sda_chk is asserted only during the released stable-high phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, present cmd=START, and keep scl_i and sda_i released high so the START sequence can complete normally.
elements.expected_response: At the terminal START phase, the FSM returns to idle, fsm_active deasserts, and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle before returning low. This is the holding case of the observed port's shows statement.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to identify the terminal START phase; sample cmd_ack and fsm_active after every posedge clk, requiring one and only one consecutive cycle with cmd_ack=1 and no additional pulse afterward.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, drive cmd=STOP while the bus is busy and scl_i/sda_i are initially high; allow the STOP sequence to reach its terminal phase without reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: When the STOP sequence completes, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack is high for exactly one clock cycle, then remains low until another command completes. This is the holding case of the observed port's shows statement.
elements.check_method: Compare the observed trace with a command-sequence reference model and assert that cmd_ack rises only at the modeled terminal completion boundary, stays high for one sampled clock, and is low on both adjacent completion-window clocks.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=WRITE with din=0, keep the external SDA and SCL lines high when released, and allow the write bit sequence to complete.
elements.expected_response: At completion of the WRITE sequence, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clk cycle; it is low before and after that cycle. This is the holding case of the observed port's shows statement.
elements.check_method: Monitor write_sequence, fsm_active, and cmd_ack after each posedge; correlate the terminal write phase with the reference model and require fsm_active=0 and a single-cycle cmd_ack pulse at that boundary.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ, keep SDA released and externally return a stable high data bit, allow filtered SCL to rise and the read low phase to finish, and do not reset or stretch SCL.
elements.expected_response: After the READ terminal phase, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock cycle and then deasserts. This is the holding case of the observed port's shows statement.
elements.check_method: Use filtered_scl_rise and read_sequence in the reference model to locate the terminal phase; check fsm_active deassertion and require cmd_ack=1 for exactly one consecutive sampled clock.

elements.stimulus: Start a supported WRITE command with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then assert nReset=0 asynchronously while write_sequence is active and before its terminal completion phase; release nReset and provide clocks afterward.
elements.expected_response: Because the sequence was reset before terminal completion, cmd_ack is absent for that aborted sequence and does not remain high; the FSM is reset to idle and both output enables are released. This is the contrasting 'otherwise' side of the observed port's shows statement.
elements.check_method: Trigger the reset during fsm_active, then monitor cmd_ack for the remainder of the aborted command window and compare against the reset-aware reference model; require no completion pulse and require idle/reset outputs after reset.

elements.stimulus: Apply any valid clocked input sequence, including reset, enable changes, and command values, while recording the DUT behavior.
elements.expected_response: No requirement-specific response is asserted because REQ-0080 states no obligation or observable behavior.
elements.check_method: Mark the scenario as covered by review of the requirement text; do not compare DUT outputs against a requirement-specific expected value.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the bus externally high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue cmd=4'b0001 (START) while idle, then continue enabled with the command inputs inactive. Record sda_oen and scl_oen on every posedge until the START command completes.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0081: during the START sequence, sda_oen is initially high and scl_oen is high; subsequently sda_oen changes to low while scl_oen remains high, producing the required SDA-low transition while SCL is released high. The sequence then proceeds to the command's normal completion.
elements.check_method: A cycle-accurate scoreboard samples registered sda_oen and scl_oen after each posedge and asserts the ordered pattern: (sda_oen=1, scl_oen=1) followed later by (sda_oen=0, scl_oen=1), with no intervening scl_oen=0 before the SDA-low observation.

elements.stimulus: After reset with the bus externally high, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Keep the controller idle and apply cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) for multiple enabled clocks, then apply an unsupported command value such as cmd=4'b0011 for multiple enabled clocks. Record sda_oen and scl_oen throughout.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case for REQ-0081: because no START command is issued, the START-specific released-then-driven-low behavior is absent. sda_oen and scl_oen remain high; in particular, there is no transition to sda_oen=0 while scl_oen remains high.
