elements.check_method: A monitor compares the observed output-enable trace against the non-START reference behavior and asserts that sda_oen=scl_oen=1 for the entire interval, with no START sequence and no command-completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: Set nReset=0 and release it, keep rst=0 and ena=1, drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, set clk_cnt=0, then issue cmd=0001 (START). Wait until the START sequence shows sda_oen=0 while scl_oen=1, and continue clocking with the bus remaining high.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at the transition from the SDA-low-while-SCL-high phase to the following phase, scl_oen becomes 0, indicating SCL is pulled low; after the SCL-low phase, cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model or assertion sequence to detect the START phase sda_oen=0,scl_oen=1, then compare the next relevant registered output phase for scl_oen=0 and require a one-clock cmd_ack pulse at START completion.

elements.stimulus: Set nReset=0 and release it, keep rst=0 and ena=1, drive scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, set clk_cnt=0, then issue cmd=0001 (START). When the START sequence reaches sda_oen=0 while scl_oen=1, assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the sequence can enter its following SCL-low phase, then release nReset.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case: reset aborts the START sequence, so scl_oen remains 1 (SCL released) and cmd_ack remains low; no START-completion acknowledgement is generated.
elements.check_method: Sample outputs immediately after asynchronous reset assertion and through the next clock; verify scl_oen=1 and cmd_ack=0, and assert that no cmd_ack pulse occurs for the aborted START command.

elements.stimulus: Select REQ-0083@1 during testplan generation and inspect the resulting hardware-test allocation.
elements.expected_response: No DUT command, input sequence, output expectation, protocol check, or hardware behavioral test is generated for REQ-0083@1; the item is recorded as having no hardware requirement.
elements.check_method: Review the generated testplan metadata and confirm that REQ-0083@1 is covered only by this scope-check element and has no DUT-facing stimulus or behavioral checker.

elements.stimulus: Initialize with nReset low then high, keep rst low, drive ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, and present cmd=0010 (STOP) at an enabled clock edge. Continue clocking until cmd_ack is observed.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case in observed_via: during the STOP sequence sda_oen is initially 0 to drive SDA low; scl_oen then becomes 1 to release SCL high; finally sda_oen becomes 1 while scl_oen remains 1, releasing SDA while SCL is high. The phases occur in that order and cmd_ack is asserted only after the final phase.
elements.check_method: Capture scl_oen and sda_oen after each posedge clk and construct a temporal assertion requiring the ordered pattern sda_oen=0, then scl_oen=1, then sda_oen=1 with scl_oen still 1 before accepting cmd_ack. Compare against a STOP-sequence reference model.

elements.stimulus: Initialize with both output enables released, hold ena=0, drive cmd=0010 (STOP) continuously for multiple clock cycles, and keep rst low and nReset high.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting otherwise case in observed_via: because the enabled STOP activation is absent, sda_oen remains 1 and scl_oen remains 1; the ports do not show the STOP-specific drive-low, SCL-release, and final SDA-release ordering, and no cmd_ack is generated.
elements.check_method: Monitor the output-enable waveform for the entire stimulus interval and assert that neither output enable leaves the released state and that cmd_ack remains low. Confirm the result with an ena-disabled reference model.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=0010 (STOP), and provide a released-high SCL line. Hold the command until the STOP sequence drives SDA low, releases SCL high, then releases SDA high while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: At the STOP completion phase, sda_oen and scl_oen are high and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock, then returns low.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model to identify completion after SDA is released high with SCL high; compare registered cmd_ack and output enables after each posedge, and assert that cmd_ack is a single-cycle pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=0010 (STOP), accept the command, then externally hold SCL low after the controller releases it so the STOP sequence cannot reach the phase where SDA is released high while SCL is high.
elements.expected_response: Because the STOP-condition sequence has not completed, the holding side of the requirement is absent: cmd_ack does not pulse, and the controller remains in the incomplete STOP sequence while SCL is held low.
elements.check_method: Monitor the filtered SCL level, sda_oen/scl_oen, and cmd_ack on every posedge; verify with the reference model that the completion condition is never reached and that no cmd_ack assertion occurs during the induced clock-stretch interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue cmd=1000 (READ) on a rising edge, keep the external SCL line high when released, and drive a valid slave SDA bit. Continue clocks until the READ data-bit phase is reached, identified by the READ sequence/read-window observation, before command completion.
elements.expected_response: During the READ data-bit phase while the slave is expected to drive SDA, sda_oen is high. This is the 'sda_oen is high, releasing SDA for the slave to drive' side of the observed_via shows condition for REQ-0086.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, correlate the sda_oen waveform with the read_sequence/read_window phase and assert that sda_oen=1 throughout the slave data-bit drive window, before cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=0 on a rising edge, keep the external SCL line high when released, and allow the normal WRITE data-bit phase to execute.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit phase, sda_oen is low and the controller drives SDA low. This is the contrasting 'sda_oen is low or the reading is outside the READ data-bit phase' side of the observed_via shows condition for REQ-0086.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, identify the active WRITE data-bit phase from the command sequence and compare the observed sda_oen value against the expected low level; ensure this observation is not classified as a READ data-bit phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and provide a released-high bus. From idle, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) and keep the external SDA and SCL lines high so the controller reaches and remains in the READ sample window.
elements.expected_response: During the READ sample window, scl_oen remains 1, which is the 'scl_oen remains 1 while the sample window is active' side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the read_window probe to delimit the sample window and assert on every settled posedge of clk while read_window=1 that scl_oen==1; record any cycle with scl_oen==0 as a failure.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and provide a released-high bus. Issue cmd=READ (4'b1000), allow the controller to enter the READ sample window, then provide a valid filtered SCL rising edge and allow the READ sample window to complete.
elements.expected_response: At the transition ending the READ sample window, scl_oen changes from 1 to 0, which is the 'then becomes 0 after the sample window' side of the observed behavior.
elements.check_method: Use read_window and filtered_scl_rise to identify the end-of-window event, then sample settled registered outputs after each posedge and assert that scl_oen was 1 during the preceding window and is 0 after the FSM advances from that window.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (1000) while idle. Allow the READ sequence to release SDA and SCL for its sample window. Drive the external SDA line so the filtered SDA value is 1, then produce a filtered SCL rising edge before cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: on the filtered SCL rising edge during the READ sample window, dout is updated to 1, equal to the filtered SDA value sampled at that edge; the READ command subsequently completes with cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered_scl_rise probe to identify the sampling edge and fsda to obtain the filtered SDA value. Sample dout after the corresponding posedge clk and compare it with fsda at the edge; require dout=1 before command completion.

elements.stimulus: Complete a READ command with dout first captured as 0 and cmd_ack asserted. After the FSM returns idle, drive the external SDA line so filtered SDA becomes 1 and create a filtered SCL rising edge while no READ sample window is active.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: at the filtered SCL rising edge outside the READ sample window, dout does not capture the filtered SDA value; dout remains at its previously captured value of 0.
elements.check_method: Use fsm_active/read_window and filtered_scl_rise to confirm the rising edge occurs outside the READ sample window, record fsda=1 at that edge, and compare the post-edge dout against its pre-edge value; require dout to remain 0 rather than change to 1.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 then release it, keep ena=1, set clk_cnt=0, and present a released-high bus. Issue cmd=READ (1000), allow the controller to release SDA and SCL, drive the slave SDA value stable, and allow a filtered SCL rising edge to occur. Continue clocks through the READ low phase and terminal completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: after the filtered SCL rising-edge sampling logic captures the slave SDA value into dout, cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock at the READ command's terminal completion point, then returns low.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for synchronization, filtering, filtered SCL rising-edge detection, READ phase progression, and registered outputs. Assert that dout is updated on the modeled filtered SCL rise and that cmd_ack is high on exactly the following terminal-completion observation cycle, with no adjacent-cycle pulse.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 then release it, keep ena=1, set clk_cnt=0, and issue cmd=READ (1000). After the READ command has been accepted and before any filtered SCL rising edge captures a sample, assert rst=1 for a rising edge, then deassert rst and hold cmd=NOP with the bus released.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: because the READ sample was not captured and reset aborted the active command, cmd_ack does not pulse at any READ terminal completion point; reset leaves cmd_ack low and the controller returns to idle.
elements.check_method: Track the reference model's READ activation and reset-abort transition. Assert that no filtered sample-capture event precedes reset and that cmd_ack remains low during and after reset until a separate valid command is issued and completed.

elements.stimulus: Review list item 14 and attempt to derive a DUT stimulus or behavioral obligation from it.
elements.expected_response: No DUT behavior, output value, timing constraint, protocol sequence, or state transition is required by this item.
elements.check_method: Specification traceability review confirms the item is classified as scaffolding and that no functional assertion or coverage bin is generated from it.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and a released-high bus, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=0, then provide normal filtered SCL high and low progression without clock stretching or reset.
elements.expected_response: This is the din=0 side of the observed behavior: during the WRITE data phase and stable high phase, sda_oen is 0, driving SDA low; scl_oen is 1 throughout the high phase, then becomes 0 when that phase ends to pull SCL low.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked monitor and WRITE-phase reference model to compare registered sda_oen and scl_oen at every posedge after NBA settling; assert sda_oen==0 during the data/high phases, scl_oen==1 while filtered SCL is high, and scl_oen transitions to 0 at high-phase completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset with ena=1 and a released-high bus, issue cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1, then provide normal filtered SCL high and low progression without clock stretching or reset.
elements.expected_response: This is the din=1 side of the observed behavior: during the WRITE data phase and stable high phase, sda_oen is 1, releasing SDA; scl_oen is 1 throughout the high phase, then becomes 0 when that phase ends to pull SCL low.
elements.check_method: Use a clocked monitor and WRITE-phase reference model to compare registered sda_oen and scl_oen at every posedge after NBA settling; assert sda_oen==1 during the data/high phases, scl_oen==1 while filtered SCL is high, and scl_oen transitions to 0 at high-phase completion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=0100 (WRITE), din=0, and clk_cnt=0. Keep scl_i and sda_i high externally, accept the command on an enabled clock, and continue clocking until the WRITE sequence has released SCL high and then pulled SCL low again.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: at the terminal phase after SCL is pulled low, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clock to indicate that the WRITE command has ended. No additional cmd_ack pulse occurs while the FSM returns to idle.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate scoreboard to identify WRITE acceptance and the terminal SCL-low phase from scl_oen/write sequencing. Sample cmd_ack after each posedge and require one asserted cycle aligned with command completion, followed by deassertion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=0100 (WRITE), din=1, and clk_cnt=0. Keep SCL high externally, accept the command, and drive sda_i low during the WRITE released-high arbitration-check phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: arbitration loss aborts the executing WRITE before its terminal completion, so cmd_ack does not assert. al asserts and the output enables release; cmd_ack remains low through the abort and subsequent idle clocks.
elements.check_method: Monitor the write_high_phase/sda_chk interval and verify the injected filtered SDA-low condition causes al and command abort. Assert that no cmd_ack pulse is observed from arbitration-loss detection through at least two following idle clocks.

elements.stimulus: Run a representative idle cycle with nReset=1, rst=0, ena=0, cmd=0000, clk_cnt=0, and stable high external SDA/SCL inputs.
elements.expected_response: REQ-0093 imposes no required DUT output, state transition, timing, or error response for this stimulus.
elements.check_method: Traceability review confirms that this scenario has no REQ-0093-specific output assertion or forbidden-behavior check and that no unrelated requirement is credited.

elements.stimulus: Start a command so the FSM is active and at least one output enable or status can be non-reset, then assert nReset=0 asynchronously between clk rising edges and hold it low for multiple clock cycles.
elements.expected_response: At the asynchronous assertion, the FSM returns to idle (fsm_active=0), scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 release both lines, cmd_ack=0, al=0, and busy=0. Counters and filter state reset, including filter_cnt=0, and fscl=1 and fsda=1 while reset remains asserted; these values do not wait for a clk edge.
elements.check_method: Use an asynchronous monitor sampling outputs and probes immediately after nReset falls, then on subsequent clk edges while nReset remains low. Compare against the reset reference model and assert the listed exact values, including no command-acknowledge pulse.

elements.stimulus: Deassert nReset, keep reset inactive, release the bus high, and issue a valid START command with ena=1. Wait for the START sequence to become active and for the filtered START condition to set busy.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting ordinary-behavior case outside asynchronous reset: the FSM may be active (fsm_active=1), the START sequence may drive SDA by making sda_oen=0 while SCL is high, and busy becomes 1 after the filtered START condition; therefore the reset-specific idle/released/cleared values are not required. cmd_ack may remain low until the command terminal phase.
elements.check_method: After reset release, monitor fsm_active, sda_oen, scl_oen, busy, and cmd_ack cycle by cycle against a START-command reference model. Confirm that command progress and busy assertion occur outside reset, contrasting them with the reset values checked in TP-0000.

elements.stimulus: With nReset high and ena high, issue a START command and wait until the command FSM is active in a non-idle phase. On a selected rising edge of clk, drive rst=1 and keep it high through that edge; drive cmd=NOP and keep the external SCL/SDA bus released high.
elements.expected_response: At the rising edge sampling rst=1, the controller applies the synchronous reset state: the FSM becomes idle, scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, and cmd_ack=0, al=0, and busy=0. This is the reset side of the observation: each observed port shows its reset value rather than continuing the active command or retaining status.
elements.check_method: At the sampled rising edge, compare registered outputs after nonblocking updates against scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, cmd_ack=0, al=0, and busy=0. Also inspect the licensed filter/counter probes to confirm counters are reset and filtered SCL/SDA histories initialize high.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same setup: with nReset high and ena high, issue a START command and wait until the command FSM is active in the same non-idle phase. On the corresponding rising edge of clk, drive rst=0, cmd=NOP, and keep the external SCL/SDA bus and other inputs unchanged.
elements.expected_response: Because rst is not asserted, the controller does not apply the synchronous reset state at that edge: the FSM and registered output enables follow the active START phase or its normal enabled progression, and status outputs retain their ordinary values rather than being forcibly cleared. This is the non-reset side of the observation: scl_oen and sda_oen are not required to become high, and cmd_ack, al, and busy are not required to become zero solely at this edge.
elements.check_method: Use the reference FSM, divider, and filter model to predict the active phase and compare scl_oen, sda_oen, cmd_ack, al, and busy after the rising edge. Explicitly check that the outputs are not equal to the synchronous-reset vector merely because the edge occurred, and that any change matches normal command timing.

elements.stimulus: Provide a specification artifact containing the exact section heading "Processing Flow:".
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0096: the specification contains the "Processing Flow:" heading, and the DUT has no runtime output behavior attributable to this scaffolding requirement; all DUT outputs remain governed by the independently specified functional requirements.
elements.check_method: Parse the specification artifact for the exact heading and confirm by simulation or formal comparison that no DUT output is required to change solely because the heading is present.

elements.stimulus: Provide an otherwise equivalent specification artifact with the "Processing Flow:" section heading omitted.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case of REQ-0096: the specification does not contain the "Processing Flow:" heading, and the DUT still has no runtime output behavior constrained by this requirement; DUT outputs remain governed by the independently specified functional requirements and are not required to differ from the holding case.
elements.check_method: Parse the specification artifact to confirm the heading is absent, then compare DUT behavior against the holding-case artifact or reference model and verify no output difference is required by REQ-0096.

elements.stimulus: Hold rst low and assert nReset low asynchronously between clk rising edges; sample scl_oen immediately, then release nReset while keeping rst low and observe the next clk rising edge.
elements.expected_response: At the asynchronous reset boundary and after the next processing boundary, scl_oen is high. This is the holding side of the observation: reset and initialization have started processing in the initialized idle state with SCL released.
elements.check_method: At the asynchronous assertion event and immediately after the following posedge, compare the registered scl_oen value against 1'b1; record a bin for asynchronous-reset initialization and the first post-reset clock boundary.

elements.stimulus: Initialize with nReset low, release nReset, keep rst low, set ena high and clk_cnt to 0, issue the START command, and continue clocking with both external SCL and SDA released until the START processing phase pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: During the active START processing phase, scl_oen is low rather than high. This is the contrasting side of the observation: the module has progressed beyond the initialized idle reset condition into command processing, so scl_oen is not in the reset-state released condition.
elements.check_method: Monitor scl_oen on settled posedge samples while the START stimulus is active; require at least one active START phase with scl_oen == 1'b0 and distinguish it from the reset-time scl_oen == 1'b1 sample.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and provide a released-high bus. Issue a START command and allow the FSM to become active with at least one status or output-enable change. Assert nReset=0 between clock edges while rst=0.
elements.expected_response: Immediately upon asynchronous nReset assertion, the module returns to the known idle reset state: cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1. The reset result is the holding side of the requirement's shows clauses.
elements.check_method: At the nReset falling edge, sample the registered outputs after delta-cycle settling without waiting for clk and assert cmd_ack==0, busy==0, al==0, scl_oen==1, and sda_oen==1; also verify no active-command output-enable state remains.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and provide a released-high bus. Issue a WRITE command with din=0 and allow the FSM to become active. Keep nReset=1, assert rst=1 before a rising edge, and apply the next rising edge of clk.
elements.expected_response: On the rising edge sampling rst=1, the module returns to the known idle reset state: cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, and sda_oen=1. The reset result is the holding side of the requirement's shows clauses.
elements.check_method: Sample outputs after nonblocking assignments settle on the rst-active rising edge and assert cmd_ack==0, busy==0, al==0, scl_oen==1, and sda_oen==1; verify the active WRITE sequence is abandoned.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset=1 and rst=0. Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, provide a released-high bus, and issue a WRITE command with din=0 while observing the command before any reset assertion.
elements.expected_response: When the reset requirement does not hold and normal command processing is active, the ports exhibit ordinary non-reset behavior rather than the reset state: during the WRITE low-data phase sda_oen=0, and during the command's active phases the FSM is not required to keep cmd_ack, busy, and al all low. This is the contrasting side of the requirement's shows clauses.
elements.check_method: Use the WRITE phase/bin probes and cycle-by-cycle assertions to identify the active low-data phase, assert sda_oen==0 there, and compare the observed active-command outputs against the reset tuple {cmd_ack=0,busy=0,al=0,scl_oen=1,sda_oen=1}; verify the reset tuple is not incorrectly forced throughout normal operation.

elements.stimulus: With ena high, clk_cnt=0, and the bus released high, issue a WRITE command with din=0 and allow the FSM to become active. Between two rising edges of clk, drive nReset low asynchronously and hold nReset low across subsequent clocks.
elements.expected_response: Immediately when nReset is asserted, and throughout reset, the FSM is idle (fsm_active=0), cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, sda_chk=0, and fscl=1 and fsda=1. Any active command is aborted and no command-complete pulse is generated while reset remains asserted.
elements.check_method: Sample asynchronous outputs immediately after the nReset transition and sample registered outputs after each subsequent posedge while nReset is low; compare all listed ports and probes with a reset reference model and assert that cmd_ack never pulses.

elements.stimulus: Start a WRITE command with ena high, clk_cnt=0, and a released-high bus. While the command is active, drive rst high before a rising edge of clk and hold rst high for multiple rising edges with nReset high.
elements.expected_response: On the rising edge at which rst is high, the synchronous reset takes effect: the FSM is idle (fsm_active=0), cmd_ack=0, busy=0, al=0, scl_oen=1, sda_oen=1, sda_chk=0, and fscl=1 and fsda=1. The active command is aborted and cmd_ack remains low for the duration of rst.
elements.check_method: Drive rst relative to clk, sample outputs and probes immediately after the activating posedge and on later posedges, and compare against a synchronous-reset reference model including the requirement that no acknowledgement pulse occurs during reset.

elements.stimulus: Keep nReset high and rst low. With ena high, clk_cnt=0, bus lines externally released high, and din=0, issue a supported WRITE command while the FSM is idle; observe the command after acceptance before its terminal completion.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-reset case: the FSM becomes active (fsm_active=1), the WRITE sequence may drive SDA low (sda_oen=0), and reset-cleared values are not required; specifically, the ordinary command behavior is observed instead of the reset-side values fsm_active=0 and sda_oen=1. No reset assertion may be inferred or required.
elements.check_method: Use a command-sequence reference model to identify the acceptance and active WRITE phase, then sample fsm_active and sda_oen after settled posedges and compare them with the expected ordinary WRITE outputs; verify rst and nReset remain inactive.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low asynchronously, deassert it, assert rst high for a rising edge of clk, then deassert rst. Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Hold sda_i=0 and scl_i=0 long enough for synchronization and three-sample filtering, then drive scl_i=1 and hold both inputs stable for at least six enabled clocks.
elements.expected_response: This is the shows side of REQ-0100 for dout: after the filtered SCL rising edge, dout updates to the filtered SDA value 0. The update occurs only after the synchronized, continuously sampled inputs produce filtered_scl_rise.
elements.check_method: Compare dout and filtered_scl_rise after each settled posedge against a reference model of the two-stage synchronizers, three-sample majority filter, and filtered SCL edge detector; require dout=0 on the modeled filtered SCL rising edge.

elements.stimulus: Complete the same reset activation sequence with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Keep scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, inject an SDA low pulse shorter than the interval required to change the synchronized three-sample majority, and do not generate a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: This is the otherwise side of REQ-0100 for dout: dout retains its previous value because the brief bus activity does not alter the filtered value and no filtered SCL rising edge occurs.
elements.check_method: Use the reference filter model to confirm no filtered SDA transition and no filtered_scl_rise; sample dout on every settled posedge and require it to remain equal to its pre-injection value.

elements.stimulus: Complete the reset activation sequence, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, and hold scl_i=1. Starting with sda_i=1, drive sda_i=0 long enough to produce a filtered START, hold it stable, then drive sda_i=1 long enough to produce a filtered STOP.
elements.expected_response: This is the shows side of REQ-0100 for busy: busy changes high after the sampled and filtered START transition and changes low after the sampled and filtered STOP transition, with neither change occurring from the raw transition before filtering completes.
elements.check_method: Compare busy, sta_condition, and sto_condition at settled posedges with a reference synchronizer/filter model; require busy=1 after the modeled START and busy=0 after the modeled STOP.

elements.stimulus: Complete the reset activation sequence, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, and hold scl_i=1 with busy initially low. Inject SDA and SCL glitches shorter than the synchronization and three-sample filtering interval, returning both inputs to their original high levels before a filtered START or STOP can form.
elements.expected_response: This is the otherwise side of REQ-0100 for busy: busy remains unchanged because the short-lived scl_i/sda_i activity does not produce a filtered START or STOP condition.
elements.check_method: Verify with the reference filter model that sta_condition and sto_condition remain deasserted; compare busy before and after each glitch and require no change.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then drive sda_i=0 before a rising edge of clk and hold both scl_i=1 and sda_i=0 for enough rising edges to complete two-stage synchronization and three-sample filtering.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: the raw scl_i and sda_i values are captured through the cSCL/cSDA stages on rising clk edges; after the resulting filtered SDA high-to-low transition while filtered SCL is high, busy rises and remains asserted.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk, compare the observed busy timing against a reference model of the two-stage cSCL/cSDA capture and filtering latency. Confirm busy rises only after the model detects the filtered START condition and remains high thereafter.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, drive sda_i=0 only between two rising edges of clk, then return sda_i=1 before the next rising edge; alternatively repeat the pulse for less than the filtering persistence interval while ensuring sda_i is high at the sampling edges.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding case: because the raw SDA transition is not present for capture at a rising clk edge or does not persist through synchronization and filtering, no filtered START is produced and busy remains unchanged low.
elements.check_method: Sample busy after each settled posedge clk and compare with a reference model that captures scl_i and sda_i only on rising edges, then applies the synchronization/filter pipeline. Confirm the model produces no filtered START and that busy never asserts.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, establish scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then drive sda_i from 1 to 0 while keeping scl_i=1 and hold the transition stable for enough rising clk edges to pass the two-stage capture and three-sample filtering pipeline.
elements.expected_response: The busy output remains low until the synchronized and filtered SDA high-to-low transition is recognized as START, then busy rises on the registered update associated with that filtered START; it must not rise directly from the raw sda_i transition.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model for the two-stage cSDA/cSCL capture, filter sampling, majority histories, delayed filtered values, and START detection. Compare the predicted first valid busy assertion with the DUT busy waveform and assert no earlier assertion.

elements.stimulus: With the bus initially scl_i=1, sda_i=1, ena=1, and clk_cnt=0, drive a raw sda_i high-to-low transition and observe busy on every posedge clk during the interval before the reference model's two-stage capture and subsequent filtering can produce a START condition; then hold sda_i low until detection.
elements.expected_response: During the pre-capture and pre-filter interval, busy remains at its prior low value. The contrasting behavior—busy rising immediately on the raw SDA transition or before the modeled synchronization/filter latency—must not occur; busy may rise only after the filtered START condition is detected.
elements.check_method: Timestamp the raw sda_i transition and compare busy at each subsequent settled posedge against the modeled earliest valid START-detection cycle. Flag any busy assertion earlier than that cycle as a failure.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, keep rst low, set clk_cnt to 0 and ena to 1, then drive stable scl_i/sda_i values through multiple synchronized sample intervals, including the patterns 00, 11, and 01. Allow the synchronizer and filter sampling stage to process each pattern.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case for REQ-0103: on each filter_sample_update, the newly synchronized SCL and SDA samples are shifted into the three-sample histories fscl and fsda, producing the corresponding filtered-history values.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the synchronizer and filter sampling schedule. Compare every filter_sample_update pulse and the observed fscl/fsda histories against the model after each enabled sample interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset initialization, set clk_cnt to 0 and ena to 0. Toggle scl_i and sda_i through the same 00, 11, and 01 pattern for several clocks, then hold the inputs stable while ena remains low.
elements.expected_response: This is the non-holding contrast for REQ-0103: while the core is disabled, filter_sample_update does not indicate new samples being shifted, and fscl/fsda remain at their previously initialized or retained histories rather than processing the input toggles.
elements.check_method: Monitor filter_sample_update, fscl, and fsda on every clock while ena is low; assert that no filter update occurs and that the histories match the retained-state reference model despite changes on scl_i and sda_i.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, keep rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=16 (binary 0000_0000_0001_0000), then apply enabled clk rising edges while observing filter_cnt through at least one complete reload and expiration interval.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: while filter timing progression is enabled, filter_cnt uses a sampling interval of clk_cnt >> 2 = 4 enabled clocks; its observed reload/countdown cadence and filter sampling events must match a four-clock interval.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model that computes (16 >> 2) = 4 and compares filter_cnt after every enabled posedge, including reload and expiration, against the predicted countdown and sampling cadence.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low, release it, keep rst low, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=20 (binary 0000_0000_0001_0100), then apply enabled clk rising edges while observing filter_cnt through at least one complete reload and expiration interval.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: the sampling interval changes to clk_cnt >> 2 = 5 enabled clocks; filter_cnt must show the corresponding five-clock reload/countdown cadence, rather than retaining the four-clock interval from clk_cnt=16 or using the unshifted value.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model that computes (20 >> 2) = 5 and compare the observed filter_cnt reload, decrement, and expiration timing on each enabled posedge; verify the interval differs from TP-0000 as predicted.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=8. Drive stable scl_i=0 and sda_i=0 long enough for the two-stage synchronizers to contain zeros, then run clk until the reference filter-counter model predicts filter_cnt_expired=1.
elements.expected_response: On the cycle filter_cnt_expired asserts, new synchronized SCL and SDA samples are shifted into fscl and fsda. The post-update three-sample histories match the reference model's shift of the synchronized samples, and the update occurs only at the expiration event.
elements.check_method: Sample filter_cnt_expired, filter_sample_update, fscl, and fsda after each posedge. Compare the observed histories against a cycle-accurate reference model of the filter counter, synchronizers, and three-sample history shift; require the predicted history update on every expiration.

elements.stimulus: Keep ena=1 and clk_cnt=8 with stable synchronized SCL and SDA samples. Select a clock cycle between two reference-model filter-counter expirations where filter_cnt_expired=0, and do not change the synchronized sample values.
elements.expected_response: Because the filter counter has not expired, filter_cnt_expired remains low and fscl/fsda retain their previous three-sample histories; the histories do not receive a new shift on this cycle. This is the non-expiration side of the required expiration-dependent behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge where the reference model predicts filter_cnt_expired=0, compare fscl and fsda with their immediately preceding values and verify no filter_sample_update occurs; check that any observed history change is limited to cycles predicted as expiration events.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 and release it, then set rst=0, ena=1, and clk_cnt=0. Hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 until filter_sample_update occurs and fscl/fsda represent all-high histories. Drive sda_i=0 while keeping scl_i=1 long enough for synchronized samples to be inserted on three successive filter sample updates, allowing fsda to contain a majority of zeros while fscl remains a majority of ones.
elements.expected_response: The updated fscl and fsda histories produce filtered SCL high and filtered SDA low from the three-sample majority values. This majority-filtered SDA high-to-low transition is the START indication, so busy rises from 0 to 1 after the corresponding registered processing. This is the holding case for REQ-0106: busy changes because the histories contain a majority SDA transition while the SCL majority is high.
elements.check_method: At each filter_sample_update, compare fscl and fsda against a reference three-sample shift model and compute each filtered value as (sample0 & sample1) | (sample0 & sample2) | (sample1 & sample2). Check that busy rises only after the modeled majority transition, allowing the documented registered-output latency.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT and establish scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 until fscl and fsda contain all ones and busy=0. Change sda_i to 0 for only one filter sampling interval, then return sda_i to 1 before a second low synchronized sample can be shifted into fsda; keep scl_i=1 throughout.
elements.expected_response: The fsda history contains at most one differing low sample and therefore its majority remains high; fscl remains majority high. No majority-filtered SDA transition occurs, so busy remains at its prior value of 0. This is the contrasting non-holding case for REQ-0106: the port does not show the START response when the histories have no majority transition.
elements.check_method: Use filter_sample_update, fscl, and fsda to verify the modeled history contains no low majority. Compare busy before and after the update sequence and assert that it remains unchanged; also verify the majority expression never produces filtered SDA low.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous nReset low, release it, then keep ena high with clk_cnt set to a small nonzero value. Drive the synchronized SCL/SDA inputs so the three-sample majority histories produce SDA high-to-low while filtered SCL is high, hold the resulting filtered START condition long enough for detection, then later produce SDA low-to-high while filtered SCL remains high for a filtered STOP.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0107: busy rises after the majority-filtered START condition and remains asserted until the majority-filtered STOP condition, then falls. The transitions are based on the stable filtered SCL/SDA values rather than an individual raw sample.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the synchronizers, sampling interval, three-sample majority histories, and filtered transition detection. Compare predicted filtered START/STOP events and their registered busy updates against busy after each settled posedge.

elements.stimulus: After reset with busy low and ena high, hold the filtered SCL/SDA values stable and inject SDA and SCL raw-line pulses shorter than the required filter sampling interval, including a raw SDA high-to-low-to-high pulse while filtered SCL is high and a raw SDA low-to-high-to-low pulse while filtered SCL is high. Ensure these pulses do not alter the three-sample majority values.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case of REQ-0107: raw SCL/SDA activity that leaves the majority-filtered values unchanged produces no filtered START or STOP condition, and busy remains unchanged and low.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to confirm that each injected pulse leaves the majority-filtered SCL/SDA values and filtered transition indicators unchanged; assert that no START/STOP event occurs and compare busy against its pre-injection value on every settled posedge.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, then operate with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. After the initialized filtered SCL and SDA values are high, drive both external bus inputs stably low long enough for synchronization and three-sample filtering to produce fscl=0 and fsda=0, then drive them stably high long enough to produce another filtered transition. Observe fscl, fsda, dscl, and dsda on every enabled clock.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: whenever a filtered value changes, dscl and dsda contain the corresponding previously filtered SCL and SDA values for the delayed interval, rather than changing before or simultaneously with the filtered values; after the delay they follow the new fscl and fsda values. The reference model shall account for synchronizer and filter latency and shall verify the delayed relationship for both low-going and high-going transitions.
elements.check_method: Compare the sampled dscl and dsda traces against a cycle-accurate reference model of the synchronizers, three-sample majority filter, and delayed filtered registers. At each filter update, assert that each delayed output equals the prior modeled filtered value and that subsequent values converge to the current modeled filtered value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, and hold scl_i and sda_i continuously high for many enabled clocks. Continue sampling without issuing commands, and observe fscl, fsda, dscl, and dsda across multiple filter sampling updates.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-transition case: because the filtered SCL and SDA values remain high, dscl and dsda must also remain high and track the unchanged filtered values on each delayed update; they must not be stuck low, retain an obsolete transition value, or otherwise diverge from the stable filtered bus values.
elements.check_method: Use a scoreboard that models repeated filter samples with no majority-value transition and compares dscl and dsda after every enabled clock against the delayed model. Check that the outputs remain equal to the stable modeled fscl and fsda values after the initial delay.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset, deassert reset, and set ena=1. Drive the bus to a stable filtered state with filtered SCL low, then hold filtered SDA and SCL stable for multiple filter sampling intervals. Also hold a stable filtered-SCL-high state with filtered SDA unchanged so current filtered SDA equals delayed filtered SDA.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of REQ-0109: busy remains unchanged because the current filtered SDA equals dSDA, or because filtered SCL is low; no START or STOP bus-event indication is produced.
elements.check_method: At each filter sample update, compare fscl/fsda with dscl/dsda and correlate the registered busy output after the corresponding clock. Assert that no busy transition occurs during the stable periods.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and the filtered bus initially idle high, hold filtered SCL high and drive SDA stably high, then drive SDA stably low for at least the filter interval to create a filtered high-to-low transition. After busy sets, hold filtered SCL high and drive SDA stably high for at least the filter interval to create a filtered low-to-high transition.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting event case of REQ-0109: when filtered SDA differs from dSDA while filtered SCL is high, the START transition causes busy to rise and the STOP transition causes busy to clear.
elements.check_method: Use the filter and delayed-value reference model to identify cycles where fsda != dsda and fscl is high, then compare busy after the registered update: require busy=1 after the START event and busy=0 after the STOP event.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1 for enough enabled clocks to establish filtered SCL=1 and filtered SDA=1. Then drive sda_i=0 while keeping scl_i=1, and hold both values until the synchronizers and three-sample majority filter update.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered SDA changes from 1 to 0 while filtered SCL remains 1, sta_condition asserts for the detected START condition; it is not asserted before the filtered transition.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to predict the filtered SDA transition and sample sta_condition after each posedge clk; require sta_condition=1 on the qualifying filtered transition and 0 on preceding non-transition samples.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Hold scl_i=0 and sda_i=1 for enough enabled clocks to establish filtered SCL=0 and filtered SDA=1. Then drive sda_i=0 while keeping scl_i=0, and hold both values until the synchronizers and three-sample majority filter update.
elements.expected_response: The filtered SDA changes from 1 to 0 while filtered SCL is 0, so this is not a START condition; sta_condition remains 0 throughout the transition and after it.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to confirm the filtered SDA falling edge occurs while filtered SCL=0, then compare sta_condition at every settled posedge clk and require no assertion.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive scl_i high. Hold sda_i low and scl_i high long enough for synchronization and the three-sample filter to settle. Then drive sda_i high while keeping scl_i high until the filtered SDA low-to-high transition is established.
elements.expected_response: The filtered SDA low-to-high transition while filtered SCL is high asserts sto_condition, indicating that a STOP condition has been detected. This is the holding/qualifying side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model for the two-stage synchronizers, filter sampling, three-sample majority, and delayed filtered values; compare the predicted STOP-condition pulse with the sto_condition probe on every enabled clock.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and drive scl_i low. Hold sda_i low long enough for the filtered values to settle, then drive sda_i high while keeping scl_i low until the filtered SDA low-to-high transition is established.
elements.expected_response: sto_condition remains deasserted; the SDA low-to-high transition with filtered SCL low is not detected as a STOP condition. This is the non-holding/contrasting side of the required behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the same synchronizer and filter reference model to confirm that filtered SDA rises while filtered SCL is low, then assert that sto_condition is never asserted for this transition.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and establish an idle bus with filtered SCL=1 and filtered SDA=1. Hold both lines stable for sufficient synchronizer/filter sampling, then drive SDA low while keeping SCL high long enough for the three-sample filter to detect a START condition; continue clocking through the registered update.
elements.expected_response: This is the START side of the observed behavior: sta_condition becomes 1 and busy becomes 1 on the registered update immediately after the filtered START detection, remaining high until a STOP is detected.
elements.check_method: Use the sta_condition probe and the reference filter model to identify the filtered START detection cycle. At the following settled posedge, compare busy against 1 and verify it remains high on subsequent clocks without a STOP or reset.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1, first establish busy=1 using a filtered START sequence: hold filtered SCL=1 and filtered SDA=1, then drive SDA low while SCL remains high until sta_condition is detected. After busy is observed high, hold filtered SDA low with filtered SCL high, then drive SDA high while keeping SCL high long enough for the three-sample filter to detect a STOP condition; continue clocking through the registered update.
elements.expected_response: This is the STOP side of the observed behavior: sto_condition becomes 1 and busy becomes 0 on the registered update immediately after the filtered STOP detection.
elements.check_method: Use the sta_condition and sto_condition probes plus the reference filter model to identify the START and STOP detection cycles. Confirm busy first reaches 1 after START, then compare busy against 0 on the clock immediately following STOP and verify it remains low thereafter unless another START is detected.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and choose a nonzero clk_cnt. Establish a released-high bus, issue START and wait for its cmd_ack, then issue WRITE with din=0 or din=1. Keep external SCL high throughout the released-SCL WRITE high phase and do not introduce an externally caused SCL falling edge.
elements.expected_response: This is the ordinary side of the observed difference: cmd_ack pulses at the normal WRITE terminal timing after the released-SCL high phase and subsequent low-period timing; no additional pause attributable to stretching or clock synchronization occurs.
elements.check_method: Use a divider/filter/FSM reference model to predict the normal terminal timing and compare the registered cmd_ack pulse cycle-by-cycle. Confirm exactly one pulse and that no unexpected delay occurs while filtered SCL remains high.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and choose a nonzero clk_cnt. Establish a released-high bus, issue START and wait for its cmd_ack, then issue WRITE. When the DUT releases SCL during the WRITE high phase, externally hold SCL low long enough for the filtered SCL to remain low across multiple enabled timing opportunities; then release SCL high.
elements.expected_response: This is the clock-stretching side of the observed difference: cmd_ack does not pulse while released SCL remains filtered low, and command progression is paused. After SCL is released and filtered high, cmd_ack occurs only after the resumed low-period timing completes.
elements.check_method: Monitor filtered SCL, the released-SCL phase, and cmd_ack. Compare against a reference model that freezes the divider/FSM during slave wait and permits the terminal transition only after filtered SCL returns high; assert no cmd_ack during the low stretch and exactly one delayed pulse afterward.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and choose a nonzero clk_cnt. Establish a released-high bus, issue START and wait for its cmd_ack, then issue WRITE. During the released-SCL WRITE high phase, externally drive SCL low long enough to produce a filtered SCL falling edge while the DUT remains released, then maintain the low level for the restarted low-period timing before allowing SCL high as required by the bus sequence.
elements.expected_response: This is the multi-master synchronization side of the observed difference: cmd_ack is postponed when the externally caused filtered SCL falling edge occurs while SCL is released. Timing is reloaded/restarted, and cmd_ack pulses only after the restarted low-period timing completes, with no premature terminal acknowledgment.
elements.check_method: Correlate the externally caused filtered SCL falling edge with the synchronized timing model and cmd_ack. Check that the edge causes a timing reload, that cmd_ack is absent before the restarted interval expires, and that exactly one pulse occurs at the modeled postponed completion time.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=WRITE, and provide a valid din value. Accept the command while the bus is idle, then externally hold scl_i=0 continuously from before the controller releases SCL through scl_oen=1 and for longer than the input-filter sampling interval.
elements.expected_response: When scl_oen becomes 1 while the filtered SCL remains low, slave_wait asserts and remains asserted while the external SCL hold continues; the active command does not advance beyond the SCL high-phase wait.
elements.check_method: At every enabled clock after scl_oen is observed high, compare the DUT slave_wait probe with a reference filter model driven by scl_i. Require slave_wait=1 for the entire interval in which the model's filtered SCL is 0, and require no subsequent command-phase progress during that interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, cmd=WRITE, and provide a valid din value. Accept the command while the bus is idle. When the controller releases SCL through scl_oen=1, drive scl_i=1 continuously for longer than the input-filter sampling interval so the filtered SCL becomes high.
elements.expected_response: The released SCL is allowed to become filtered high and slave_wait remains deasserted; the command sequence may proceed through its high phase rather than entering or remaining in the slave-wait condition. This is the non-holding side of the observed difference.
elements.check_method: Use a reference synchronizer/filter model to identify the interval after scl_oen=1 during which filtered SCL is high. Assert that slave_wait=0 throughout that interval and that the FSM proceeds to the next legal command phase once the timing tick occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue a START command (cmd=0001) on an enabled clock tick. Model the bus as externally holding SCL low after the controller releases SCL (scl_oen=1); keep scl_i low until the filtered SCL fscl is stably 0.
elements.expected_response: When the controller has released SCL high and fscl remains low, slave_wait is asserted. This is the 'condition asserted' side of the requirement's indication that a slave or another bus participant is holding SCL low; command phase advancement remains paused while the condition persists.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare slave_wait and the slave_wait probe against the reference model after detecting scl_oen=1 with fscl=0. Confirm assertion persists while fscl remains 0 and no subsequent high-phase advancement occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue the same START command (cmd=0001) on an enabled clock tick, but leave the external SCL line released high so that after filtering fscl becomes 1 when the controller sets scl_oen=1.
elements.expected_response: When the controller releases SCL and fscl is high, slave_wait remains deasserted. This is the 'condition not asserted' side of the requirement's indication: no participant is holding SCL low, so the wait indication must not assert and the START sequence may proceed.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge, compare slave_wait and the slave_wait probe against the reference model for scl_oen=1 with fscl=1. Confirm no slave_wait assertion and verify the FSM progresses beyond the SCL-high wait point.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena high and set clk_cnt to 1. With the bus initially high, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0. When the WRITE sequence releases SCL (scl_oen becomes 1), externally hold SCL low so filtered SCL remains low for many enabled clock cycles, while keeping the command inputs stable.
elements.expected_response: This is the slave-wait holding case: cmd_ack remains low for every clock while slave_wait remains active; the command-phase outputs remain unchanged, the timing counter does not expire or advance the bit-level FSM, and no command-completion pulse occurs.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge during the forced-low interval, compare cmd_ack against 0 and verify the relevant command-phase output enables and FSM phase remain unchanged from entry into slave_wait; use the slave_wait and cnt_zero probes to qualify the interval and verify no timing tick/phase progression occurs.

elements.stimulus: Repeat the same reset, ena=1, clk_cnt=1, bus-high, din=0 WRITE sequence. When the WRITE sequence releases SCL, first hold SCL low for several enabled clock cycles, then release the external SCL drive so filtered SCL becomes high and keep the bus valid until the command completes.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting non-holding/resume case: cmd_ack remains low during slave_wait, then after filtered SCL becomes high the FSM resumes from the held phase, completes the WRITE sequence, and produces exactly one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Qualify the forced-low interval with slave_wait and check cmd_ack is continuously 0; after filtered SCL is high and slave_wait deasserts, compare the observed output sequence with the reference phase model and require exactly one one-clock cmd_ack pulse, with no pulse during the preceding wait.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, clk_cnt to a nonzero value, keep the bus released high, issue a START command, and after the registered scl_oen becomes 1 during the START sequence, externally pull scl_i low and hold it low for sufficient enabled clock cycles for synchronization filtering and timing-counter processing.
elements.expected_response: For the holding case in which an external SCL falling edge occurs while scl_oen=1, the DUT asserts scl_sync at the filtered falling-edge event, reloads the timing counter rather than continuing the prior countdown, and aligns subsequent local low-period FSM timing to the shared externally generated SCL low period. No command phase advances through the synchronized timing point before the reloaded timing interval permits it.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the synchronizer, filter, divider, and FSM. Correlate the filtered SCL falling edge with scl_sync, compare counter-expiration/next-phase timing against the model, and verify the observed phase boundary is delayed by the synchronization reload rather than following the pre-fall counter schedule.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, clk_cnt to the same nonzero value, keep the bus released high, issue the same START command, and after the registered scl_oen becomes 1 during the START sequence, keep scl_i continuously high for the equivalent observation interval without introducing an external SCL falling edge.
elements.expected_response: For the contrasting non-holding case in which no external SCL falling edge occurs while scl_oen=1, scl_sync remains deasserted, the timing counter is not reloaded by clock synchronization, and the local low-period timing proceeds according to the ordinary divider/FSM schedule.
elements.check_method: Run the same reference model and compare scl_sync, counter-expiration timing, and subsequent FSM phase timing. Confirm that the no-fall trace has no synchronization event and follows the baseline schedule, contrasting it with TP-0000.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=3, keep scl_i and sda_i high, and issue a supported START command on an enabled clock. Continue clocking until the START sequence completes, recording cnt_zero and every registered scl_oen transition.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0118: scl_oen changes only after cnt-derived timing boundaries. Each START bit-phase transition occurs on the expected counter-expiration/clk_en event, with no immediate or fixed-rate transition independent of clk_cnt; the command eventually produces its normal completion pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of cnt reload/decrement and clk_en generation. Compare each observed scl_oen transition and its cycle against the model's predicted counter-expiration boundary, allowing the registered one-clock output update.

elements.stimulus: Start a supported WRITE command with ena=1 and clk_cnt=5. After the command enters a phase with SCL released high, first hold scl_i low to cause clock stretching, then deassert ena for several clocks, then restore scl_i high and ena=1.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting-case discriminator for REQ-0118: scl_oen must not advance immediately, at a fixed independent rate, while ena is low or while released SCL remains filtered low. The pending phase transition is postponed until timing progression resumes after the counter can expire and the stretch is removed; subsequent scl_oen transitions again occur only at cnt-derived boundaries.
elements.check_method: Scoreboard scl_oen against a reference model that freezes FSM timing during ena=0 and slave_wait, holds the output phase unchanged during those intervals, and resumes counter-based advancement afterward. Flag any scl_oen transition during the pause or any transition not coincident with the modeled clk_en boundary.

elements.stimulus: Assert nReset low and release it; keep rst low and ena high. Set clk_cnt to a stable nonzero value such as 3, hold the bus released-high with no stretching or synchronization events, then issue a supported WRITE command with din=0 and keep cmd and clk_cnt stable through completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: cmd_ack remains low until the reference-model sequence of divider-timed FSM advances has completed, then asserts for exactly one clock. The completion interval is consistent with cnt being loaded from clk_cnt and decremented on successive rising edges of clk.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk after registered outputs settle, compare cmd_ack and its pulse width against a cycle-accurate reference model that reloads cnt from clk_cnt and decrements it once per clock; assert no early ack and exactly one ack at the modeled terminal phase.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, set clk_cnt to 3, enable ena, and issue the same supported WRITE command with din=0 on a released-high unstretched bus. Observe the command during the first clock cycles after acceptance, before the reference-model prescaler interval and required FSM advances have elapsed.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting/otherwise side of shows: cmd_ack must not occur merely on the next clock or on every clock; it remains deasserted during each pre-completion cycle. Any early or continuously asserted cmd_ack is the otherwise behavior indicating an interval inconsistent with loading cnt from clk_cnt and decrementing it per rising edge.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to mark the earliest legal completion cycle for clk_cnt=3 and assert cmd_ack==0 on all earlier cycles; separately flag any pulse before that boundary or any pulse wider than one clock.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep rst low and ena high, set clk_cnt to a value greater than 1, drive scl_i and sda_i high, issue a supported START command, and after the START sequence enters a timing-gated command phase, sample a clock where cnt_zero is low before the next counter expiration; do not apply clock stretching or synchronization events.
elements.expected_response: While the counter has not expired, cnt_zero remains low and scl_oen remains at the current START command-phase value; the FSM does not advance to the next prescribed SCL phase. This is the non-holding side of the specified port behavior.
elements.check_method: Use a reference divider/FSM model to identify an enabled command phase with cnt_zero low, then compare scl_oen across the intervening registered clock update and assert that no phase transition occurs before expiration. Record coverage for the non-expired counter condition.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep rst low and ena high, set clk_cnt to a value greater than 1, drive scl_i and sda_i high, issue a supported START command, and monitor the active START sequence until its timing counter expires with cnt_zero asserted; do not apply clock stretching or synchronization events.
elements.expected_response: When cnt_zero asserts while ena is high, the internal timing enable is asserted and the FSM advances to the next prescribed START SCL phase. scl_oen changes to that phase at the registered update following counter expiration, demonstrating the holding side of the specified port behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference divider/FSM model and cnt_zero probe to identify expiration, then compare scl_oen with the model on the next settled posedge; require exactly the expected phase transition at expiration and no earlier transition. Record coverage for counter-expiration-driven FSM advancement.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous reset, release nReset, set rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=3, and a released-high bus. Present cmd=START (4'b0001) and hold it through the first enabled timing tick so the START command is accepted. During the active START sequence, keep scl_i and sda_i high with no clock stretching or synchronization event, and observe clocks between successive reference-model clk_en ticks.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of REQ-0121: while the START FSM is active, scl_oen remains at its current command-phase value on every posedge where the reference divider has not asserted clk_en; it does not advance to the next bit-timing phase or change scl_oen on those non-clk_en clocks. cmd_ack remains low until the command completes.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model of the clk_cnt divider to identify clk_en and candidate START phase boundaries. At every posedge with clk_en=0, compare the settled registered scl_oen value against the preceding cycle and require equality; also verify no command completion pulse occurs during the active sequence.

elements.stimulus: Apply asynchronous reset, release nReset, set rst=0, ena=1, clk_cnt=3, and a released-high bus. Present cmd=START (4'b0001) and hold it through command acceptance. Keep scl_i and sda_i high with no clock stretching or synchronization event. Continue until the reference model identifies an active START phase boundary at which the next phase requires a different scl_oen value, and capture scl_oen immediately after that clk_en posedge.
elements.expected_response: Advancing side of REQ-0121: scl_oen changes to the next START command-phase value on the clk_en posedge at the identified boundary. It must not remain unchanged beyond that enabled timing tick; the corresponding change must not occur on an earlier non-clk_en clock.
elements.check_method: Predict each START phase and clk_en tick with the divider/FSM reference model. At the first phase boundary requiring a different scl_oen, compare the post-posedge registered scl_oen with the predicted next value, and assert that all preceding non-clk_en samples held the prior value.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to a nonzero value, keep the bus released and high, issue a supported WRITE command with din=0 while ena=1, and wait until the command is visibly active with a defined scl_oen phase. Then drive ena=0 and hold it low for multiple clk cycles spanning at least one expected timing-counter expiration.
elements.expected_response: This is the requirement-holding case: while ena=0, scl_oen remains at the current command-phase value and does not advance to the next timed SCL phase or command-complete boundary; cmd_ack does not pulse. The timing counter is reloaded rather than producing normal FSM timing progress.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate divider/FSM reference model to predict the phase at ena deassertion and counter reload behavior. Sample scl_oen and cmd_ack after each posedge while ena is low; require scl_oen to remain unchanged and cmd_ack to remain 0, and use the counter/timing trace to confirm reload instead of expiration-driven FSM advancement.

elements.stimulus: Set clk_cnt to a nonzero value, keep the bus released and high, issue the same supported WRITE command with din=0 while ena=1, and keep ena high throughout command execution.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting ena-high case: scl_oen advances through the WRITE command's timed SCL phases according to clk_en, and the command eventually completes with exactly one clock of cmd_ack. This demonstrates the ordinary behavior that is prevented when ena is low.
elements.check_method: Compare registered scl_oen transitions and cmd_ack against the cycle-accurate divider/FSM reference model. Require phase transitions only at predicted enabled timing ticks and require one, and only one, cmd_ack pulse after the normal terminal phase.

elements.stimulus: With the controller idle and ena=1, issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=1 and clk_cnt=0. Model the open-drain bus so SDA remains high during the WRITE stable-high phase, with SCL released high and no external SCL stretch.
elements.expected_response: During the stable-high WRITE phase, write_high_phase and sda_chk assert while sda_oen=1; because filtered SDA is high as expected, al remains low. The WRITE then completes normally and produces one cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: At every enabled clock, compare write_high_phase, sda_chk, sda_oen, filtered SDA, al, and cmd_ack against a cycle-accurate WRITE/arbitration reference model; assert that al stays low through command completion and cmd_ack occurs exactly once.

elements.stimulus: With the controller idle and ena=1, issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=1 and clk_cnt=0. During the WRITE stable-high phase, when SDA is released for arbitration, externally drive SDA low and hold it long enough for filtered SDA to become low; keep SCL released high.
elements.expected_response: During the same stable-high WRITE arbitration phase, write_high_phase and sda_chk assert with sda_oen=1. The filtered-SDA-low condition causes al to assert high, demonstrating detection of lost arbitration; the active WRITE aborts, cmd_ack is not generated for the aborted command, and both output enables are released.
elements.check_method: Use the open-drain bus model and filter reference model to determine the first filtered-SDA-low sample during write_high_phase. Compare al, cmd_ack, FSM activity, and output enables against the arbitration-loss model, requiring sticky al and no command-complete pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide clk_cnt=1, set din=1, issue cmd=WRITE (0100), and keep the external SCL line high without stretching. Follow the command until the FSM reaches write_high_phase=1.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: while write_high_phase=1 during the WRITE stable high phase, sda_chk is asserted high.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge of clk, compare the sda_chk probe against write_high_phase; require sda_chk==1 whenever write_high_phase==1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide clk_cnt=1, set din=1, issue cmd=WRITE (0100), and keep the external SCL line high without stretching. Observe the command while it is idle, during its non-high WRITE phases, and after completion when write_high_phase=0.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: when the FSM is not in the stable high phase of a WRITE bit, sda_chk remains deasserted low.
elements.check_method: At each settled posedge of clk outside write_high_phase, compare the sda_chk probe and require sda_chk==0; specifically check idle, the pre-high/low phase, and the post-ack idle interval.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al=0, set ena=1 and issue a WRITE command (cmd=0100) with din=1. Keep scl_i high and sda_i high through the synchronizer and filter until the WRITE stable high phase is reached, with sda_oen=1, scl_oen=1, and sda_chk asserted.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting 'otherwise' side of the observed behavior applies: because the filtered SDA value is not low while arbitration checking is active, al does not newly assert and remains 0.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model and write_high_phase, sda_chk, fsda, and al probes to identify the released-high arbitration window; sample al after each posedge and verify it remains low throughout the window.

elements.stimulus: After reset with al=0, set ena=1 and issue a WRITE command (cmd=0100) with din=1. Allow the FSM to reach the stable high phase with scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, then externally hold sda_i low while scl_i remains high until the synchronized and three-sample filtered SDA value fsda is low and sda_chk is asserted.
elements.expected_response: The 'shows' side of the observed behavior applies: al asserts high when the controller expects SDA released high but filtered SDA is low. The active WRITE is aborted without cmd_ack, and both output enables are released.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model and write_high_phase, sda_chk, and fsda probes to confirm the activation condition; verify on the next settled clock that al=1, no cmd_ack pulse occurs for the aborted WRITE, and scl_oen=sda_oen=1.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset with al=0, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a supported READ command from idle, and wait until the READ sequence has released SCL high for its active read window. While the FSM remains active, drive the filtered bus inputs through a stable STOP condition: filtered SDA low, then filtered SDA high while filtered SCL remains high, holding each level long enough for the three-sample filter to recognize the transition.
elements.expected_response: At the filtered STOP-condition event during the active non-STOP READ command, al asserts and remains asserted until reset. This is the asserting side of the observed al behavior; command processing is aborted and no command-complete pulse is generated for the aborted command.
elements.check_method: Use the filter/reference model to identify the filtered SDA low-to-high transition with filtered SCL high and compare the sampled al output on the following clock. Assert that al transitions from 0 to 1 at that event and remains 1 on subsequent clocks before reset.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset with al=0, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue the requested STOP command from idle, and allow its active STOP sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL, and release SDA while filtered SCL is high so that the resulting filtered SDA low-to-high transition is recognized as a STOP condition.
elements.expected_response: When the filtered STOP condition occurs while the active command is the requested STOP command, al does not newly assert and remains 0. This is the non-asserting side of the observed al behavior.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to correlate the filtered STOP event with the STOP command being active, then sample al after the event and through command completion. Require al to remain 0, with no 0-to-1 transition attributable to this STOP condition.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and the bus initially released, issue a WRITE command with din=1. During the WRITE released-high arbitration-check phase, externally hold SDA low while allowing SCL to be high; continue clocking until al rises.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of the observed-via shows: on the cycle after al rises, the FSM returns to idle (fsm_active=0), scl_oen=1 releases SCL, and sda_oen=1 releases SDA. The aborted command produces no normal completion pulse.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after al rises, sample al, fsm_active, scl_oen, and sda_oen after registered updates settle. Assert that fsm_active is 0 and both output enables are high on the first post-loss response cycle and remain released until a later command is accepted.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and the bus initially released, issue a WRITE command with din=0. During the WRITE high phase, externally hold SDA low, which is the expected value for din=0; do not inject an unexpected STOP or other arbitration-loss condition. Continue clocking through command completion.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case of the observed-via shows: al does not rise from the low SDA, and the controller does not enter the post-arbitration-loss response. scl_oen and sda_oen follow the normal WRITE phase sequence, the command completes normally, and fsm_active becomes 0 only at normal completion rather than because of arbitration loss.
elements.check_method: Monitor al, fsm_active, scl_oen, sda_oen, and cmd_ack cycle by cycle. Assert al remains low, the normal WRITE waveform and one-cycle cmd_ack occur, and distinguish the normal terminal idle transition from the positive scenario by absence of an al-triggered immediate release.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (1000) on an enabled divider tick. Allow the READ sequence to release SDA and SCL for its sample window. Drive the bus so the filtered SDA value is stable at 1, then produce one filtered SCL rising edge while the READ sample window is active.
elements.expected_response: Shows side: on the posedge that processes the filtered SCL rising edge, dout captures 1, the current filtered SDA value. The READ sequence then completes normally and produces its command-complete indication.
elements.check_method: Use a reference model of synchronization and three-sample majority filtering to predict filtered SDA and the filtered SCL rising edge. Sample dout after the processing posedge and compare it with the predicted filtered SDA value.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ (1000) on an enabled divider tick. Allow the READ sequence to release SDA and SCL for its sample window. Establish a filtered SDA value of 0 using the filter history, while driving raw SDA high so raw SDA differs from filtered SDA. Produce one filtered SCL rising edge during the READ sample window.
elements.expected_response: Shows side, not otherwise side: on the processing posedge, dout captures 0, the filtered SDA value, and must not capture the raw SDA value of 1. Capturing 1 would be the otherwise behavior and is a failure.
elements.check_method: Model the synchronizer/filter histories and predict filtered SDA=0 at the filtered SCL rising edge. Compare post-posedge dout against 0 and explicitly flag dout=1 as evidence of sampling raw or unfiltered SDA.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue the READ command cmd=1000, and let the FSM reach the READ window with scl_oen=1. Drive sda_i low and hold scl_i high long enough for synchronization and the three-sample filter to produce filtered SDA=0 and a filtered SCL rising edge.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: when filtered_scl_rise occurs, dout updates on the corresponding registered clock to the current filtered SDA value 0.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, use the filtered-signal reference model and filter-update probe to identify filtered_scl_rise; compare dout against the modeled filtered SDA value on that event and require dout=0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue the READ command cmd=1000, and let the FSM reach the READ window with scl_oen=1. Drive sda_i high and hold scl_i high long enough for synchronization and the three-sample filter to produce filtered SDA=1 and a filtered SCL rising edge.
