elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: when filtered_scl_rise occurs, dout updates on the corresponding registered clock to the current filtered SDA value 1.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after nonblocking assignments settle, use the filtered-signal reference model and filter-update probe to identify filtered_scl_rise; compare dout against the modeled filtered SDA value on that event and require dout=1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue the READ command cmd=1000, and let the FSM reach the READ window with scl_oen=1. Keep external scl_i low so filtered SCL never rises, then change sda_i from low to high and hold it long enough for filtered SDA to become 1 while scl_i remains low.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting side of shows: because no filtered SCL rising edge occurs, dout does not update to the filtered SDA value; it remains at its previously registered value.
elements.check_method: Monitor the modeled filtered_scl_rise event and dout on every settled posedge; while filtered_scl_rise is absent, require dout to remain unchanged despite the modeled filtered SDA changing to 1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ while the bus is released. Allow the READ sequence to release SDA and SCL; drive the external SDA line to a stable 1 and allow filtering to produce a filtered SCL rising edge during read_window.
elements.expected_response: At the posedge that processes filtered_scl_rise in read_window, dout updates to 1, the filtered SDA value, and presents 1 as the received READ data bit. This is the holding side of the observed_via shows statement.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model for synchronizers, three-sample filtering, and edge timing to identify the filtered SCL rising edge and filtered SDA value. Sample dout after the same posedge and compare it with the modeled filtered SDA value; require read_window and filtered_scl_rise to be asserted for the event and require dout to remain 1 until a later sample or reset.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=READ, then externally hold SCL low so the READ sequence remains in the clock-stretch/read wait before its filtered SCL rising-edge sampling event. Drive SDA high while maintaining the SCL hold for multiple enabled timing ticks.
elements.expected_response: While no filtered_scl_rise occurs in read_window, dout does not present a filtered SDA sample from this READ sampling event and remains at its reset value 0; it must not change to the externally driven SDA value 1. This is the non-holding side of the observed_via shows statement.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to confirm that filtered SCL remains low, read_window is not completed, and no filtered_scl_rise event occurs. Sample dout after each enabled clock and compare against its pre-event value, requiring no update to 1 and no READ data capture until a genuine filtered SCL rising edge occurs.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, release nReset and rst, set ena=1 and cmd=START (4'b0001), and present the command while the divider has not yet expired (cnt_zero=0). Hold cmd and ena stable and observe before the first enabled clk_en tick.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observed difference: fsm_active remains 0 and the command FSM stays idle because a valid command is present but clk_en has not permitted advancement.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after reset release and before the reference divider predicts clk_en, compare the fsm_active probe against 0; require no transition to active during this interval.

elements.stimulus: Reset the DUT, release nReset and rst, set ena=1 and cmd=START (4'b0001) while idle, then keep the valid command and enable asserted until the reference divider expires and produces clk_en.
elements.expected_response: Transition side of the observed difference: on the enabled timing opportunity, the FSM leaves idle and fsm_active becomes 1, beginning the START command sequence.
elements.check_method: Use a divider reference model to identify the first clk_en tick after command presentation, then sample fsm_active after the corresponding posedge and require it to be 1; require it was 0 before that tick.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset so the FSM is idle, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then present cmd=4'b0001 (START) through an enabled idle command-decode opportunity.
elements.expected_response: The START side of the observed difference occurs: sda_oen remains released initially and then falls to 0 while SCL remains released high; the START operation eventually produces its completion pulse and returns to idle.
elements.check_method: At every enabled clock compare the observed sda_oen sequence and eventual one-clock cmd_ack pulse against a reference command-decode/FSM model; require the START-specific sequence and reject a no-operation trace.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset so the FSM is idle, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then present cmd=4'b0010 (STOP) through an enabled idle command-decode opportunity.
elements.expected_response: The STOP side of the observed difference occurs: sda_oen drives SDA low and later releases it after SCL is released high; the STOP operation eventually produces its completion pulse and returns to idle.
elements.check_method: Compare the registered sda_oen waveform and one-clock cmd_ack pulse with the STOP reference trace at each clock, requiring the drive-low-then-release sequence rather than an idle trace.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset so the FSM is idle, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1, and present cmd=4'b1000 (READ) through an enabled idle command-decode opportunity while externally driving sda_i first low and then high during separate read-bit trials.
elements.expected_response: The READ side of the observed difference occurs: sda_oen is released throughout the read operation so the external device can drive SDA, and the operation eventually produces its completion pulse and returns to idle.
elements.check_method: Use a reference READ-decode trace to check sda_oen remains released from command acceptance through completion and that exactly one cmd_ack pulse occurs; vary sda_i to ensure the external drive is not overridden.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset so the FSM is idle, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then present cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) with din=0 through an enabled idle command-decode opportunity.
elements.expected_response: The WRITE side of the observed difference occurs: the write operation begins and sda_oen is driven low for din=0, followed by the command's normal completion pulse and return to idle.
elements.check_method: Compare sda_oen and cmd_ack against the din=0 WRITE reference trace, requiring write-sequence activity and exactly one completion pulse rather than the no-operation behavior.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release reset so the FSM is idle, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, then present cmd=4'b0100 (WRITE) with din=1 through an enabled idle command-decode opportunity.
elements.expected_response: The WRITE side of the observed difference occurs: the write operation begins and sda_oen is released for din=1, followed by the command's normal completion pulse and return to idle.
elements.check_method: Compare the registered sda_oen and cmd_ack waveform against the din=1 WRITE reference trace, requiring the write sequence and exactly one completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: For separate reset-to-idle trials, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0 and present cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) at an enabled idle decode opportunity; repeat with every unsupported 4-bit value other than 0000, 0001, 0010, 0100, and 1000.
elements.expected_response: The contrasting no-operation side of the observed difference occurs: sda_oen shows no START, STOP, READ, or WRITE command sequence, cmd_ack remains low, and the FSM remains idle for each NOP or unsupported encoding.
elements.check_method: For each trial compare the complete sda_oen and cmd_ack trace with the idle reference model; require no command-specific transition and no completion pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the FSM idle, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, present cmd=START, and hold it through an enabled clk_en command-decode opportunity.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: the START command activates start_sequence and fsm_active; stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence remain inactive.
elements.check_method: At the first enabled decode opportunity and subsequent settled clock, sample the FSM probes and compare against the reference command-decode model; assert the exact one-hot sequence selection.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the FSM idle, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, present cmd=STOP, and hold it through an enabled clk_en command-decode opportunity.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: the STOP command activates stop_sequence and fsm_active; start_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence remain inactive.
elements.check_method: At the first enabled decode opportunity and subsequent settled clock, sample the FSM probes and compare against the reference command-decode model; assert the exact one-hot sequence selection.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the FSM idle, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, present cmd=READ, and hold it through an enabled clk_en command-decode opportunity.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: the READ command activates read_sequence and fsm_active; start_sequence, stop_sequence, and write_sequence remain inactive.
elements.check_method: At the first enabled decode opportunity and subsequent settled clock, sample the FSM probes and compare against the reference command-decode model; assert the exact one-hot sequence selection.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the FSM idle, set ena=1, drive din to either value, provide a released-high bus, present cmd=WRITE, and hold it through an enabled clk_en command-decode opportunity.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: the WRITE command activates write_sequence and fsm_active; start_sequence, stop_sequence, and read_sequence remain inactive.
elements.check_method: At the first enabled decode opportunity and subsequent settled clock, sample the FSM probes and compare against the reference command-decode model; assert the exact one-hot sequence selection.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the FSM idle, set ena=1, present cmd=NOP (0000), and hold it through an enabled clk_en command-decode opportunity without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of shows: the idle command leaves fsm_active deasserted and start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence all inactive.
elements.check_method: At and after the enabled decode opportunity, sample all five FSM probes and compare with the idle reference state; verify no sequence probe asserts and the FSM remains idle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep the FSM idle, set ena=1, present an unsupported cmd encoding such as 0011, and hold it through an enabled clk_en command-decode opportunity without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of shows: the unsupported command leaves fsm_active deasserted and start_sequence, stop_sequence, read_sequence, and write_sequence all inactive.
elements.check_method: At and after the enabled decode opportunity, sample all five FSM probes and compare with the idle reference state; verify no sequence probe asserts and the FSM remains idle.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Issue cmd=4'b0001 (START) on a rising edge while the controller is idle, then continue clocking with ena=1 and the bus externally released high until command completion.
elements.expected_response: The START sequence first has sda_oen=1 and scl_oen=1, releasing both lines. It then changes sda_oen to 0 while scl_oen remains 1, producing SDA low while SCL remains high for the START condition. The sequence subsequently pulls SCL low and completes with a one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use a sampled waveform assertion keyed from START command acceptance: observe sda_oen=1 and scl_oen=1 before the START transition; require the next START-generation phase to have sda_oen=0 and scl_oen=1; require the later SCL-low phase and exactly one cmd_ack pulse. Cross-check the phase ordering with the start_sequence probe.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Keep the controller idle and issue cmd=4'b0000 (NOP) for multiple enabled clock ticks without issuing START or any other command.
elements.expected_response: The START-specific release-then-drive-low behavior does not occur: sda_oen remains high and scl_oen remains high, with no transition to sda_oen=0 while scl_oen=1, no start_sequence activity, and no cmd_ack.
elements.check_method: Monitor sda_oen and scl_oen over the complete NOP observation window. Assert that no cycle contains the START-generation pattern of a preceding released SDA followed by sda_oen=0 while scl_oen remains 1; also check start_sequence and cmd_ack remain inactive.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset low and release it, keep rst low, ena high, clk_cnt at a nonzero value, and both external I2C lines released high. From idle, issue cmd=START for an enabled command-acceptance tick. Continue driving the bus high after the controller generates the START phase, then allow the controller to run until the START command reaches its terminal phase.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of the observed behavior: after the SDA-low-while-SCL-high START phase, scl_oen becomes low to pull SCL low, the START command completes and returns to idle, and cmd_ack is high for exactly one clock cycle before returning low.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, use a reference FSM model to identify START-phase completion. Assert that scl_oen is high during the SDA-low/SCL-high phase, then low in the post-START completion phase, and that cmd_ack has one and only one consecutive high sample aligned with completion. Assert no additional cmd_ack pulse occurs without a new command.

elements.stimulus: Apply the same released-high bus and accepted START sequence as TP-0000. Once the START condition is generated with SDA low while SCL remains released high, drive ena low before the next enabled FSM advancement and hold ena low for several clocks.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of the observed behavior: while ena is low and the post-START completion phase cannot advance, scl_oen does not become low and cmd_ack remains low; no command-completion pulse is produced during the disabled interval. After ena is reasserted high, the controller may resume and must then complete the START with scl_oen low followed by a one-clock cmd_ack pulse.
elements.check_method: Use the reference timing/FSM model with ena gating. During each disabled clock, compare scl_oen and cmd_ack against the expected stalled state and specifically flag any scl_oen low transition or cmd_ack high pulse. After re-enabling ena, check the eventual completion sequence and one-cycle acknowledgement.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Issue cmd=0010 (STOP) while idle and sample scl_oen and sda_oen after every posedge until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: This is the holding case for REQ-0136: during the STOP sequence, sda_oen is first 0 while scl_oen remains 0 or its prior driven state, then scl_oen becomes 1 while sda_oen remains 0, and finally sda_oen becomes 1 while scl_oen remains 1. The final SDA release occurs only after SCL has been released high; cmd_ack then pulses once.
elements.check_method: Use a sampled trace checker or reference model to assert the ordered subsequence sda_oen=0, then scl_oen=1 with sda_oen=0, then sda_oen=1 with scl_oen=1, with no earlier scl_oen release or SDA release; require exactly one cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, scl_i=1, and sda_i=1. Leave the controller idle and apply cmd=0000 (NOP), followed by an unsupported command such as cmd=0011, sampling scl_oen and sda_oen for the same number of clocks used to observe the STOP sequence.
elements.expected_response: This is the contrasting, non-holding case for REQ-0136: because no STOP command is active, the ports must not exhibit the STOP-specific ordered transition of sda_oen=0 followed by scl_oen=1 and then sda_oen=1. Both lines remain released in the idle state, and cmd_ack remains low.
elements.check_method: Compare the sampled output trace against the STOP signature; assert scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1 throughout the idle/no-op interval and assert that no cmd_ack pulse occurs.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, provide a released-high bus, configure clk_cnt for a known nonzero interval, and issue cmd=STOP while the controller is idle. Allow the STOP sequence to complete through SDA-low, SCL-release/high, and SDA-release phases.
elements.expected_response: When the STOP terminal phase completes, cmd_ack becomes 1 for exactly one clock cycle and then returns to 0; no additional acknowledgement is generated for the same STOP command.
elements.check_method: At every posedge clk after registered outputs settle, compare cmd_ack against a reference STOP-command FSM model and assert that its high interval is exactly one cycle at terminal completion.

elements.stimulus: Complete a STOP command as in TP-0000, wait for the cmd_ack pulse to end, then issue a new valid command such as START on a subsequent enabled clk_en tick.
elements.expected_response: The STOP command has returned the command FSM to idle: the subsequent START command is accepted and begins its normal sequence rather than being ignored or treated as overlapping the completed STOP.
elements.check_method: Scoreboard the observed output-enable sequence and command acknowledgement against a reference FSM, requiring the STOP acknowledgement before the subsequent START sequence and requiring a later acknowledgement for START.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, drive scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=1000 (READ), and keep the external bus released. Follow the command through its READ data-bit phase until the subsequent cmd_ack pulse.
elements.expected_response: Holding side of shows: during the READ data-bit phase, while SCL is released high for the read sample window and before cmd_ack, sda_oen is high, releasing SDA so the external slave can drive the data bit.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while read_window is asserted and before cmd_ack, compare sda_oen against 1'b1 and record a functional bin for the READ release phase; fail if sda_oen is low at any such sample.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, drive scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=0100 (WRITE) with din=0, and keep the external bus released through the WRITE data-bit phase.
elements.expected_response: Non-holding side of shows: because the operation is not the READ data-bit phase, sda_oen is low during the WRITE data-bit phase, driving SDA low rather than releasing it for a slave-driven read bit.
elements.check_method: Use write_sequence or write_high_phase to identify the WRITE data-bit interval and compare sda_oen against 1'b0 at settled posedges; fail if the output remains released during this contrasting phase.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) while idle, and allow the READ command to progress without reset, arbitration loss, or clock stretching.
elements.expected_response: When the READ FSM enters read_window, sda_oen is high and scl_oen remains high throughout the read window, releasing SDA and SCL. After the read window completes at the filtered SCL rising-edge phase, scl_oen transitions low, pulling SCL low again. This is the holding side of the observed_via shows condition.
elements.check_method: Use the read_window probe to delimit the window; sample scl_oen and sda_oen after each posedge clk and assert scl_oen==1 for every cycle in read_window, followed by a registered transition scl_oen==0 before the READ low phase completes.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, keep scl_i and sda_i high, issue cmd=READ (4'b1000) while idle, wait until read_window is asserted, then assert nReset=0 asynchronously before the filtered SCL rising edge that would normally end the read window; release nReset only after observing reset outputs.
elements.expected_response: Before reset, scl_oen is high in the READ read window. Reset aborts the READ sequence and leaves scl_oen high; no subsequent transition to scl_oen==0 occurs for that aborted READ. This is the otherwise side of the observed_via shows condition: scl_oen is not high throughout a completed READ window followed by a low transition because the sequence is aborted by reset.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a READ command while the external bus is released. Drive stable filtered SDA=1 during the READ sample window, allow filtered SCL to transition low-to-high, and wait for the filtered_scl_rise probe. Ensure dout was previously 0.
elements.expected_response: Holding case: when filtered_scl_rise is asserted, dout updates on the corresponding clocked observation to 1, equal to the filtered SDA value at that rising edge.
elements.check_method: Use the filter and synchronizer reference model to identify filtered_scl_rise and filtered SDA at the same sampled event; compare the post-posedge dout value with the modeled filtered SDA value and require dout to change from 0 to 1.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue a READ command while the external bus is released. First establish dout=0, then drive stable filtered SDA=1 before the READ sample window and allow filtered SCL to transition low-to-high until filtered_scl_rise is asserted.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting case: if the requirement were absent, dout would not update to the current filtered SDA as a consequence of filtered_scl_rise and would remain 0; this is the negative contrast that must be distinguished from the required capture behavior.
elements.check_method: At the modeled filtered_scl_rise event, compare dout after the posedge against both contrast expectations: record failure of the contrast if dout becomes 1, and require the compliant capture result from TP-0000 rather than accepting an unchanged dout.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=1000 (READ) with a released-high bus. Allow the READ command to reach its read window, drive a stable filtered SDA value, produce a filtered SCL rising edge, then allow the read window to end and the terminal SCL-low phase to complete.
elements.expected_response: HOLDING CASE: After the filtered SCL rising-edge sample and completion of the terminal READ bit-cycle low phase, the FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack pulses high for exactly one clock; no additional cmd_ack pulse occurs until another command is issued.
elements.check_method: Use the divider, synchronizer, and filter reference model to identify the filtered SCL rising edge and terminal low phase. At each posedge after registered outputs settle, assert that cmd_ack is low before completion, high for exactly one clock at completion, and low thereafter; confirm no further active READ output transitions occur.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=1000 (READ). Allow the controller to enter the READ window and sample a filtered SDA value, then inject an unexpected filtered STOP by driving filtered SDA from low to high while filtered SCL is high before the READ bit cycle reaches its terminal low phase.
elements.expected_response: NON-HOLDING CASE: The READ bit cycle is aborted or remains incomplete, the FSM does not complete the normal READ return-to-idle sequence, and cmd_ack is not asserted for that READ command.
elements.check_method: Use the filter reference model to ensure the injected SDA transition is a valid filtered STOP during the active READ sequence. Monitor cmd_ack on every settled posedge through the abort and for the remaining observation window, and fail if any command-complete pulse is observed for the aborted READ.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=WRITE (4'b0100), din=0, and provide a released-high SDA/SCL bus. Issue the command on an enabled clock tick and keep inputs stable until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the active WRITE data-bit phase before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 0, meaning the DUT drives SDA low. This is the din=0 side of the required sda_oen behavior.
elements.check_method: Monitor the WRITE-active interval using the command acceptance and cmd_ack edges; compare sampled sda_oen against a reference model of active-low open-drain encoding and require sda_oen==0 while din==0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1, cmd=WRITE (4'b0100), din=1, and provide a released-high SDA/SCL bus. Issue the command on an enabled clock tick and keep inputs stable until cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the active WRITE data-bit phase before cmd_ack, sda_oen is 1, meaning the DUT releases SDA high. This is the din=1 side of the required sda_oen behavior; the contrasting incorrect side would be sda_oen==0.
elements.check_method: Monitor the WRITE-active interval using the command acceptance and cmd_ack edges; compare sampled sda_oen against a reference model of active-low open-drain encoding and require sda_oen==1 while din==1.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and present cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=0. Provide a normal released-high SCL/SDA bus and allow the WRITE operation to run through its data-bit phase until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit phase, sda_oen is 0, which drives SDA low; this is the din=0 side of the required behavior. The operation then completes with its normal command acknowledgement.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while write_sequence is active and before cmd_ack, compare the observed sda_oen against 0 and verify the corresponding open-drain bus line is low; also verify exactly one cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and present cmd=WRITE (0100) with din=1. Provide a normal released-high SCL/SDA bus and allow the WRITE operation to run through its data-bit phase until cmd_ack pulses.
elements.expected_response: During the WRITE data-bit phase, sda_oen is 1, releasing SDA so the bus is pulled high; this is the din=1 side of the required behavior. The operation then completes with its normal command acknowledgement.
elements.check_method: At every settled posedge while write_sequence is active and before cmd_ack, compare the observed sda_oen against 1 and verify the corresponding open-drain bus line remains high; also verify exactly one cmd_ack pulse.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold scl_i and sda_i high, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=1, and issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100) while the FSM is idle. Keep the external SDA high throughout the WRITE high phase so arbitration is not lost.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for REQ-0144: after WRITE acceptance, scl_oen becomes 1 to release SCL during the stable high phase, then becomes 0 to pull SCL low again. The FSM returns to idle and cmd_ack is asserted for exactly one clock after the terminal low phase.
elements.check_method: Capture posedge-aligned scl_oen and cmd_ack waveforms and assert the ordered sequence release-high -> pull-low -> one-clock cmd_ack, with no cmd_ack before the SCL pull-low phase and no additional pulse afterward.

elements.stimulus: After reset, hold scl_i and sda_i high, set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, din=1, and issue cmd=WRITE (4'b0100). When the WRITE phase releases SCL high for arbitration checking, externally pull SDA low and hold it through that high phase to cause arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise case for REQ-0144: the required normal release-then-pull-low completion pattern is not completed. On arbitration loss the command aborts, cmd_ack does not pulse, and scl_oen remains released (1) as the controller returns to idle and releases the bus.
elements.check_method: Use the posedge-aligned scl_oen and cmd_ack waveform, correlated with the injected SDA-low interval, to verify arbitration abort occurs before terminal completion: no cmd_ack pulse is present and no post-high-phase scl_oen=0 completion transition occurs; confirm scl_oen is released after abort.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, provide clk_cnt=0 and a released-high bus, then issue START while idle. Observe every active START phase through cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the active START sequence, scl_o and sda_o remain continuously 0. scl_oen and sda_oen alone control the lines: each is 0 during its actively pulled-low phase and 1 during its released phase. This is the holding side of the observed_via shows.
elements.check_method: At every posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_o and sda_o against 0 and compare each output-enable against the reference START phase model; verify the externally modeled line is low when enable=0 and released when enable=1.

elements.stimulus: Establish a busy transaction, then issue STOP with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Observe every active STOP phase through cmd_ack.
elements.expected_response: During the active STOP sequence, scl_o and sda_o remain continuously 0. scl_oen and sda_oen switch between 0 for actively pulled-low phases and 1 for released phases, including SCL release before SDA release. This is the holding side of the observed_via shows.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-by-cycle STOP reference model to compare both constant drive outputs and both registered output-enable values throughout the sequence, including the final released state.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue READ while idle; externally return SDA values 0 and 1 on separate runs and allow the command to complete.
elements.expected_response: Throughout each READ sequence, scl_o and sda_o remain 0. SDA is controlled only by sda_oen and is released during the read window; SCL is controlled only by scl_oen and is released for the read window and driven low afterward. This is the holding side of the observed_via shows.
elements.check_method: Sample all four ports each settled clock and compare against the READ phase model; assert that no nonzero value appears on either drive output and that output-enable transitions match the required drive/release phases.

elements.stimulus: With ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue WRITE with din=0, then repeat with din=1, allowing SCL to complete normally.
elements.expected_response: For both WRITE values, scl_o and sda_o remain continuously 0. With din=0, sda_oen becomes 0 to pull SDA low; with din=1, sda_oen becomes 1 to release SDA. scl_oen similarly selects driven-low versus released SCL phases. This is the holding side of the observed_via shows.
elements.check_method: Compare each settled-cycle output against a WRITE reference model for din=0 and din=1; independently assert constant-low scl_o/sda_o and verify the active-low polarity of scl_oen/sda_oen.

elements.stimulus: After reset, keep ena=1 and issue NOP and each unsupported cmd value while idle; do not start a supported command.
elements.expected_response: Outside an active supported command sequence, scl_o and sda_o are still constant 0, while scl_oen and sda_oen remain at the idle released value 1 and do not represent command-sequence drive phases. This is the contrasting otherwise side of the observed_via shows.
elements.check_method: Monitor the ports from reset release through several enabled clocks after each no-op command; compare against the idle reference state, requiring scl_o=sda_o=0 and scl_oen=sda_oen=1 with no command phase or cmd_ack.

elements.stimulus: Assert and release nReset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, then issue a START command while scl_i and sda_i are externally high. Observe the START sequence through the phase that pulls SDA low while SCL is high and the subsequent phase that pulls SCL low.
elements.expected_response: On every sampled output row, scl_o=0 and sda_o=0. During the SDA-active phase, sda_oen=0, meaning SDA is actively pulled low, while scl_oen=1 if SCL is released. During the subsequent SCL-active phase, scl_oen=0, meaning SCL is actively pulled low. This is the active-pull-low side of the stated behavior.
elements.check_method: At each posedge after registered outputs settle, compare scl_o and sda_o against constant 0 and correlate each observed output-enable value with the START phase: output-enable 0 must correspond to active pull-low and output-enable 1 to release. Record coverage bins for SDA-active and SCL-active phases.

elements.stimulus: Assert asynchronous nReset low between clocks, release it, keep ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, and issue no command while the controller remains idle. Also observe the initial release phase of a START command before SDA is pulled low.
elements.expected_response: On every sampled output row, scl_o=0 and sda_o=0. In the reset/idle state and the START initial release phase, scl_oen=1 and sda_oen=1, meaning both SCL and SDA are released rather than actively pulled low. This is the release side of the stated behavior.
elements.check_method: Sample all four outputs after asynchronous reset and on each subsequent settled posedge; assert scl_o==0 and sda_o==0 continuously, and assert scl_oen==1 and sda_oen==1 during reset/idle and the START release phase. Record a release-state coverage bin.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=START while the filtered SCL and SDA bus lines are high. Wait for the enabled timing tick and observe the START sequence when sda_oen becomes 0 while scl_oen remains 1.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for sda_oen: while sda_oen is 0, sda_o is 0, indicating that the SDA line is driven low. scl_o remains 0 as the constant-low SCL output.
elements.check_method: At the settled clocked observation in the START SDA-low phase, assert sda_oen==0 and sda_o==0; also assert scl_o==0.

elements.stimulus: After reset, set ena=1 and issue cmd=START while the filtered SCL and SDA bus lines are high. Advance through the START sequence until it pulls SCL low, with scl_oen becoming 0.
elements.expected_response: Holding case for scl_oen: while scl_oen is 0, scl_o is 0, indicating that the SCL line is driven low. sda_o remains 0 as the constant-low SDA output.
elements.check_method: At the settled clocked observation in the START SCL-low phase, assert scl_oen==0 and scl_o==0; also assert sda_o==0.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and leave the controller idle with ena=1 and no command accepted, so sda_oen remains released at 1.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for sda_oen: when sda_oen is not 0, sda_o is still 0 because the contract declares the SDA output port constant low; this observation does not indicate active SDA ownership.
elements.check_method: After reset settles, assert sda_oen==1 and sda_o==0, explicitly distinguishing the released-enable state from the low-enable holding case.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and leave the controller idle with ena=1 and no command accepted, so scl_oen remains released at 1.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting non-holding case for scl_oen: when scl_oen is not 0, scl_o is still 0 because the contract declares the SCL output port constant low; this observation does not indicate active SCL ownership.
elements.check_method: After reset settles, assert scl_oen==1 and scl_o==0, explicitly distinguishing the released-enable state from the low-enable holding case.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, reset the DUT, then issue a START command while the external SCL and SDA devices are released high. Observe the START sequence phase in which both output enables are high.
elements.expected_response: For the holding case in REQ-0148, scl_oen=1 releases SCL and sda_oen=1 releases SDA; with no external low driver, the resolved SCL and SDA lines are high due to the external pull-up resistors.
elements.check_method: After each registered output update, sample scl_oen, sda_oen and the resolved bus lines. Assert that both enables are 1 and both resolved lines are 1 during the released phase.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, reset the DUT, then issue a START command and allow the sequence to advance through the phase that drives both bus lines low.
elements.expected_response: For the contrasting non-holding case in REQ-0148, scl_oen=0 and sda_oen=0 indicate that SCL and SDA are actively driven low; the resolved SCL and SDA lines remain low despite the external pull-up resistors.
elements.check_method: After each registered output update in the driven-low phase, sample both output enables and the resolved bus lines. Assert that each enable is 0 and each corresponding resolved line is 0, distinguishing active drive from release.

elements.stimulus: Apply nReset=0 then release it, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, hold scl_i=1 and sda_i=1, issue cmd=START=4'b0001 on a rising clock edge, and allow the START sequence to reach its terminal low-SCL phase without reset or arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: At the registered cycle after the START terminal phase, cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle. It is low in the preceding cycle and low again on the immediately following cycle. This is the holding side of the observed shows statement.
elements.check_method: Use a reference FSM to identify the START terminal phase, then sample cmd_ack after each posedge and assert the pattern 0,1,0 around completion; assert that the high interval is exactly one clock period.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset and configure ena=1 and clk_cnt=0. Issue cmd=STOP=4'b0010 on a rising clock edge while providing a released-high bus, and allow the STOP sequence to drive SDA low, release SCL, release SDA, and reach its terminal high-SCL phase.
elements.expected_response: At the registered cycle after the STOP terminal phase, cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle, with cmd_ack low both before that completion cycle and on the next cycle. This is the holding side of the observed shows statement.
elements.check_method: Model the STOP phase progression and compare the sampled cmd_ack waveform against a one-cycle pulse aligned to the terminal-phase completion; fail on a missing pulse or any two consecutive high samples.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ=4'b1000, hold SDA released, provide a stable external SDA value of 1, allow the read window and filtered SCL rising edge to complete, then allow the terminal low-SCL phase to complete.
elements.expected_response: At the registered cycle after the READ terminal low-SCL phase, cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle and is low in the immediately preceding and following cycles. This is the holding side of the observed shows statement.
elements.check_method: Use the reference model to locate the filtered SCL sample and READ terminal phase, then check that cmd_ack has one and only one high sample at completion and no adjacent high sample.

elements.stimulus: Apply reset, set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, set din=1, issue cmd=WRITE=4'b0100, keep the external SDA high during the released write high phase, and allow the write sequence to reach its terminal low-SCL phase without arbitration loss.
elements.expected_response: At the registered cycle after the WRITE terminal low-SCL phase, cmd_ack is high for exactly one clk cycle and is low in the immediately preceding and following cycles. This is the holding side of the observed shows statement.
elements.check_method: Track the WRITE terminal phase with the reference model and assert a single-cycle cmd_ack pulse aligned with completion; check that no pulse is extended or repeated.

elements.stimulus: Start a WRITE command with ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, set din=1, allow the FSM to enter the released SDA high phase, then externally hold SDA low to cause arbitration loss before the terminal low-SCL phase; continue clocking without issuing another command.
elements.expected_response: Because the command is aborted before its terminal phase, cmd_ack remains low for the aborted command and does not produce a completion pulse. This is the contrasting otherwise side of the observed shows statement: no terminal completion means no required one-cycle ack; any ack at or after the abort is a failure.
elements.check_method: Detect al and the transition back to idle, then monitor cmd_ack from arbitration loss through several clocks and assert it never rises for the aborted command.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, and a released-high bus; issue cmd=START on an enabled clock and provide the normal START bus conditions through completion. After the completion indication, issue a second valid command on the next available enabled command-acceptance opportunity.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: at the terminal phase of the accepted START sequence, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle, then deasserts. The controller returns to its command-acceptance state so the subsequent command can be issued.
elements.check_method: Use a cycle-accurate reference model to identify the START terminal phase and compare cmd_ack on every clock: assert it on the terminal completion report, assert that it is high for one and only one consecutive cycle, and verify acceptance/progress of the subsequent command after the pulse.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1, clk_cnt=0, establish a busy transaction context with SCL and SDA high, and issue cmd=STOP. Drive the normal STOP sequence, including external SCL high during the release phase. After completion, issue a valid next command on the next available enabled command-acceptance opportunity.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: when the accepted STOP sequence reaches its terminal phase, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle and then returns low. The controller is ready to accept the next bit command after the pulse.
elements.check_method: Compare registered cmd_ack against a reference STOP state model at each posedge; check exact one-cycle width, no extra or early pulses, and successful subsequent command acceptance after the pulse.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=READ, keep SDA released for the master, provide a stable external read bit, allow the normal SCL high sample window and following low phase to complete, then issue another valid command after the completion indication.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: at the terminal phase after the READ bit has been sampled and the low phase has completed, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle and then deasserts. The next bit command can be issued after that pulse.
elements.check_method: Use the filtered-SCL rising-edge and READ reference model to locate the terminal phase; compare cmd_ack cycle-by-cycle for one pulse only and verify the following command is accepted after the pulse.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=WRITE with din=0, allow the bus to respond normally without arbitration loss, and wait through the SDA setup, SCL released-high, and SCL low phases. Then issue another valid command after completion.
elements.expected_response: Holding case of shows: at the terminal phase of the accepted WRITE sequence, cmd_ack asserts for exactly one clk cycle and then deasserts. No additional completion pulse occurs, and the next command may be issued after the pulse.
elements.check_method: Track WRITE phase progression with a reference model and compare cmd_ack at each posedge; require one high cycle aligned with terminal completion, low on adjacent cycles, and successful acceptance of the subsequent command.

elements.stimulus: Set ena=1 and clk_cnt=0, issue cmd=WRITE with din=1, and hold the external SDA line low during the released SCL-high arbitration-check phase so the accepted WRITE operation aborts before its normal terminal completion phase.
elements.expected_response: Contrasting otherwise case of shows: because the bit-level operation does not complete normally, cmd_ack is not asserted as the completion indication; it remains low for the aborted operation and no completion pulse is generated.
elements.check_method: Inject the arbitration condition at the filtered high phase, use the reference model to mark the operation aborted rather than completed, and check that cmd_ack is low on the abort cycle and throughout the remainder of that operation, with no one-cycle completion pulse.
